I played Robocraft alot when it was first out a few years ago and at the time It was a fairly fun game, that I played often until my computer had not supported it until recently when I find that a large ammount of the fun has seemingly vaporised into the air with the newer changes. For insance I will start with the Possitives.
Possitives:
1:The new team death match. (so when you die its not the end)
2:And the new painting of blocks. (though with only 4 paints when your not prenium, being Light blue, Orange, Gray, and White, all other colors you require prenium for.)
3:The lack of a part tech tree.
4:And the Crates of new random parts. (more so the ones you earn while playing, and the ranks of crates you get form how well you did the previous round)
Though There are many possitives form the previous versions of robocraft there are many negitives to replace them.
Neutruals:
1:The new 1 type of Cube. (instead of having to replace all your cubes with higher tiered cubes costing a large sum of Robits)
Negitives:
1:The New Part Ranking system.
2:The Lack of Tiered Games. (many times over I've meet a game where I found a player who is just a Plasma Goliathon/Lock-on Missile Launcher/Ion Distorter/Laser Leviathan/Aeroflak Cannon just on a single block with a mode of transport (most likly Hover, Copter, or Wheels) Getting  MVP and killing everyone in 1/2 hits while everyone else concentrates fire on them and they hardly scratch.)
3:Over Powered Parts Everywhere in weaker games. (Above)
The new cloaking device and Teslas combined. (The new cloaking device allows for one to seemingly appear right next to you then instantly kill you with melees, and hiding them selves after being spotted instantly.)
4:Proto-Seekers UnderPowered/OverPriced. (For being 10,000 Robits it does less damage than the weakest laser (the wasp at 25 times the price (400 robits) It is also quite a large weapon so it would be best if it where to be buffed to the power of at least the Hornet or Blaster.)
5:The lack of a one buy forver Premium. (Heck if it where forver I would buy it for 30$)
6:Only 1 map for Team Death match. (even if the enviorment was Earth everytime at least have the difference of land marks and obsticales be different.
7:OP Weapons Vs Respawns (Some of the Legendaries can kill you in one hit even if you just respawned with the new repair instead of invencibility)
What I would Change:
1:Respawn Changing: I would make it so when you spawn you are cloaked for between 3-5 seconds and you can freely move while being invencible but you will not beable to inflect damage or heal allies, this will allow for less spawn camping and more fair fights.
2:Reinstallment of Tiered Groups or Scaled Armor/Power: To prevent the "Pay-2-Win" weapons from owning everyone stuck with an empty wallet form spending money on stupid things like food, water, and shelter. There is two things you can do, either make it so such over powered weapons highly weigh one towards a higher tiered game where they would be meet with an equal challange (and less free protonium crates form care-less MVPs) or make it so depending on how your robot is made (ie:block count) Effects how much power your weapons can inflect, and how much you can take.
3:Make a one time buy Premium, you might just earn way more money that way. (especially if us customers buy it and then go meh and esentually waste the money that we could've saved if we payed only as much as we play.)
4:Also just something that mainly I face, and mostlikly a few others, a way to change our ingame names.

Planetside 2 is a game that attempts (and mostly succeeds) at replicating what a future war might entail if all the factions essentially had unlimited resources and soldiers. It's constant fighting on 4 continents, until one faction manages to capture the majority and essentially locks the continent from further fighting for a short period.
Sound fun? It is... most of the time. New players will be utterly lost as this game subverts the usual gameplay of having each battle be a contained server with connected players, and instead just puts all of them onto a single large map. This means the battles themselves are over facilities, and some areas are completely without conflict. The game tries to help newcomers by adding an "Instant Action" button, but even this will confuse a lot of people as they're hurled into a fight with a vague objective of "Capture X Facility".
Once you do figure out what the hell is going on, there's a lot of fun in joining a huge battle that's chaotic as ever and a sense of accomplishment when you successfully capture a facility. Now, with all this praise I need to go straight to the negatives.
The game runs, well, mediocre. I'm packing more than enough power to max this game (i7 2600-k, MSI GTX 970 and 16 GB of DDR3 ram) yet even when lowering several settings like completely disabling shadows, the game will still drop under 60 FPS during downtime due to the scale of the game world. I'm not exactly saying this is unexpected, but just realize unless you are running a hefty rig you will be playing on low settings and the games visuals suffer considerably.
But that's not the worst part by far, I consider this game to have the WORST F2P system of any (good) game. To earn the in game currency for unlocks (Certs) you need to play, a long, long time. You will earn around 30 an hour being as active as possible, yet upgrades (basic upgrades, things you will need to be effective) can cost up to 1000. This can be avoided by paying, yet the paid system isn't much better. It's $1 per 100 "SC" (Station Cash) and still that same upgrade will be 700 ($7 if you didn't keep track). That's pretty rediculous when you consider you have to spend this on each class, and if you want to play on another server, each character.
Overall, I'd say if you don't mind grinding hours just to be useful, or have $100 burning a hole in your pocket this game can reward you greatly. Just don't expect to get by easy if you want to go the free route.
tl;dr if you don't mind grind or spending loads of do$h this game is amazing, otherwise don't bother downloading.

This is far and away the best FPS I have played in a long time, and further more it accomplished this being free to play.
Graphics are simple and gorgeous, the colors really stand out and everything just pops. Guns are very detailed as are charcter models and environments.
The level design is really, really well done. Most of the maps have very enjoyable choke points and push to make those intense moments of making it to the objective, or defending it, that much more exciting. Multiple paths provide plenty of options for flanking but it is not so open to leave you itching for a fight for very long at all.
The sound design is very well done with characters yelling out actions accordingly and guns sounding menacing with heavy clinking and clanging. Explosions are deep and the inclusion of a very unique "headshot" hit marker sound let's you know when you are putting the hurt on.
Gameplay is fast paced, taking many cues from both Call of Duty (in the good ways) and Team Fortress 2. They shooting mechaanics arre very rewarding and kills feel earned and deaths feel deserved in almost every instance. Rarely have I experienced anything I felt was the game being cheap or cheating. There is a nice addition of a "kill-cam" like moment where it shows your killerss exact position, aiming direction, and stance as well as your own with the killing bullets trajectory highlighted showing exactly how the enemy scrubbed you out of existence withhout the goofy replay from Call of Duty. Using this model of kill-Cam it let's you keep spectating the acction while your ghosted death "replay" can be seen staticly in the level. I really like how it was done. The time to kill(TTK) in this game is quite long, it can be summed up to play A LOT more like TF2 than a game like CoD, each class, or "Merc" has different health and movement speeds making them play and have to play differently.
The classes are each varying in terms of gameplay fromScout Sniper like Vassili, to the brick wall that is Rhino. Classes are allowed 3 main weapons such as Light Machine Guns, Assault Rifles, Submachine Guns, Sniper Rifles and Shotguns (pretty stanndard stuff). you also carrry a sidearm weapon such as an SMG or Pistol and a melee weapon ranging from a knife to a cricket bat. Weapons are found on loadout cards which are all preset in their design and as you level up the cards by trading in the ones you buy or are awarded after a match you get increasing rarity including skins/color changes and perks.
Perks in this game do alot of different things from decreasing the time it takes to arm/disarm objectives to reducing explosion damage and weapon reload speed. you can have up to three perks per loadout card and perks are again, assigned to specific cards and cannot be changed out.
The loadout cards are what makes or breaks this games Pay-to-win rating. I whole-heartedly feel this game IS NOT PAY TO WIN in any way, every mercenary's standard loadout is plenty effective to wipe the floor with the guy who spent $7.50 USD on his rare cobalt card. The perks do not upset the game balance in any major way and only enhance your merc in very small amounts.
Overall I give this game a personal score of
!
I highly reccomend it to any fans of the shooter genre, ESPECIALLY if you like games like Team Fortress 2, Call of Duty, or Battlefield.
TL;DR- This game is awesome, free, in no way pay to win and there is literally nothing lost by trying it!

When I first played this game, I was like "Wow, this is cool!": There were only a few cubes available: white cubes (very weak but extremely cheap), T1 SMGs and plasma and wheels. There was a good progression system which encouraged you to level up to try out new parts, such as hovers, nanos (weapons that can heal), etc. You got a constant income of RP (manni) based on your performance. Back then I recommended this game to everyone.
The best part about this system was that you weren't overwhelmed with tons of parts and that you were rewarded based on performance. There weren't many parts yet there was sooo much depth. The main problem back then was that FJ never added tutorials (and I still believe this is one of the main reason all these problems exist) (there still aren't any tutorials btw). They also never removed completely broken and unintuitive mechanics such as anti-gunbrella (extremely broken when used with Mech legs).
Now? FreeJam (the devs) decided to simplify the game as much as possible by removing things such as the pilot seat (the core of a bot (yes, bots have no core according to FJ)) and adding autoaim weapons (look at someone and hit them with 95% accuracy wwithout doing any effort (a chicken can use it)). They also decided to add tons of content, even if the other content isn't balanced (Lasers UP). They ignore the most important bugs such as desyncs (very serious bug) and keep adding more issues by adding more content. They replaced the constant income with RNG crates, so if you perform very poorly, you can still get better rewards than the RC WarGod himself. They also made all content available to ALL players so new players will be OVERWHELMED with all the content (and it only gets worse). The bad thing is that if you buy ('craft') something and you don't like it, you are screwed because you only get 10%-25% back when you sell ('recycle') it.
What makes me sad is that FJ doesn't want to create their own game: They want their game to be another FPS (yes, they actually want a BUILDING THIRD-PERSON game to be a FPS) and thus they waste time making the UI crappier ("we want 'Edit Mode' to feel like a gamemode") and meanwhile they pretend that adding a copy of your bot in the middle of the test map (to test damage redirection and IMPROVE your bot) may be "too confusing" or "will take too much effort" (believe me, it is not (Unity has a built-in method to copy pasta objects such as your bot)).
What do I recommend? Find another building game with devs that really want to create their own game and don't just try to copy elements from different genres. You will likely be dissapointed if you like building.

When it comes to puzzle games, Portal 2 easily takes the cake (haha get it?).
Even by today's standards, this game looks amazing. It has its own unique style that looks great no matter how old it is. Plus performance is butter smooth.
Possibly the best story I've ever been told by a video game. The story is told with absolutely no cutscenes, a unique method at the time. Telling a story in a puzzle game is incredibly difficult because if a player gets stuck in one section of a puzzle too long, they might lose immersion. However, Valve nails the story aspect flawlessly.
Valve has created a brilliant puzzle that actually relies on thinking. This might sound obvious, but many puzzle games feign difficulty by making certain puzzle aspects difficult to spot. Portal 2 makes sure that all aspects of the puzzle are clearly visible and makes sure each function is clearly defined. Pressing a button releases a cube. Standing here makes you jump higher. Every item has a clear and simple purpose, but its up to you to string them together to beat the puzzle.

I enjoy this game.  It's creative, allows for unlimited build options, and it's fun to battle!  If you're good at building, original bots can be winners.  If you're good at fighting, but not building, you can purchase bots made by other players.  OR, you could get inspiration from those, and build your own.  The only way you aren't satisfied with your bot is if you suck at building and are too proud to try somebody else's build.
Yes, things have changed significantly with the game, and will change even more before it's out of early access.  Read- EARLY ACCESS.  It's not P2W any more than any other game that has microtransactions.  It allows you to buy premium, which is not the sum of $1.99 X 30 days for a month's worth, it is priced so that you can purchase the time you are able to purchase.  If you can only afford $1.99, you get one day.  If you can afford more, you get a month for roughly $15...similar to many other games on the market.  Being premium gives you double the slots on your winnings from crates, but does not increase your chance of getting higher items.  Purchasing crates does not give you a better chance of getting better items than winning them, you simply get more crates.  I've opened 65 before, and only received 1 legendary item.  I don't call this P2W, it's no different than the previous version of the game where you could purchase galaxy cash to buy items that were ONLY available with GC.
Bottom line, Freejam bends over backwards to listen to their players.  They can't help it that the players complain about EVERYTHING.  Beg for a nerf and you get it, then you complain that it's not a good weapon anymore.  The only thing wrong with Robocraft is the community.  Once the spoiled players stop whining they will realize that they can work with the devs to continue to create a great game.

Game modes -
Single player:  Kill bots with very poor AI for loot  and get a crate every 10/25/50/100/200/etc kills.  Avoid getting stuck in or falling through the map .  Don't use melee to mostly avoid this.
Team Deathmatch:  Pretty much what it says.  Pugging is a crapshoot, and you either wind up with people that can play, or others that are somehow almost as bad as the bots in single player.  Only one map.
Once you hit level 10, two more game modes open up, each on the same map.  One is a Capture the Flag type where you shoot crystals at towers to control them, then destroy the enemy base.  The other is a deathmatch where you kill each other, and you get more points for killing those in the lead. First to 20 points wins.
The last mode is League play, which unlocks at level 50.  I'm not there yet, but I'm sure it's more of the same.  The fact that colors are behind a paywall is pure greed on the developer's part.  If you have $20 to spend, don't buy crates for this game.  MAV is a much better choice.  Gear Up is a good choice as well, if you want simpler customization and less of a grind.

Age of Empires II HD is the High Definition remake of a classic RTS. If you're a fan of game series like Warcraft and Starcraft, you are likely to be a fan of this. Thanks to The Forgotten DLC, the game is balanced ever better than before. Game contains multiple campaigns, a LAN multiplayer, and an online multiplayer. The Steam Workshop contains some very nice texture packs and the like.
There are some problems, however. Even being the HD version doesn't solve the problem of dated graphics. If old graphics drive you crazy, you may lose interest pretty fast. Playing online can be a little difficult with connection problems between players being commonplace, so online play requires some patience.
If you've read this and are still considering Age of Empires II HD, get it. It's fun, doesn't require a supercomputer to play, and you'll never experience a thrill quite like using your Monks to steal an enemy's army. Wololo!

A long time back, Freejam made a game called Robocraft. The aim was simple, you made a robot and fought with it. There was 1 gamemode. History of robocraft:
The Good Old Days:
A long long time ago, when this game was fun to play, you used to get robo points to buy parts and tech points to research new parts - this was awesome, a sense of progression. Weapons were well balanced in their associated environments (e.g. SMG's did wonders at close range, with plasmas being effective barrage weapons and rails sniping off crucial parts etc.)
The era of Megabots was ushered in, providing tantalising new content for veteren players and something to really look forward to for newer ones. The game was still fun, didnt feel like a grind and premium simply gave faster levels for more CPU and more robo and tech points - it was essentially pay to grind less.
Now:
I'd like to start off with a good point, then name the bad points in the middle and finish with some good points to represent what this game is now: A Turd Sandwich.
+ Beautiful game that inspires creativity
- Hackers are now present
- If you dont have Premium, you will die of old age before you can afford one of the shamefully OP legendary weapons
- Lost all sense of Progression
- People spamming the chat begging people to buy their robots from factory
+ Air Doge is funny

Roboraft is a game of building a robot and havin it battle other robots, almost the entirety of the game consists of battling with other players.
Pros:
full robot customizability
several types of weapons and mobility types to fit your play style
Cons:
Premium players are alowed 2 additional players in a platoon
Premium players get more xp and double loot from crates, as well as more colors to paint your robot
Pay to Win players are able to simply buy dozens of the top tier crate while being premium to get an absurd amount of stuff before anyone else
The matchmaking is completely unbalanced
Lets talk more about the matchmaking of this game, which is why i had to stop playing it. It matches you based on the CPU you are using, which is increased for each item you place onto your robot, in itself, it doesn't seem bad, however you only get a 10 CPU max increase each time you level up. The brackets for matchmaking are also absurdly large, players like me that used a little over 500 CPU are being matched with players up to 1000 CPU, meaning that they can have several times the amount of weapons, shields, and mobility parts that you have and recieve no penalty in any way. Players playing against these high level players without having their level of gear and part limit have absolutely no chance of winning as the other player can kill them in 3 shots were it takes you 4 shots just to destroy one of their weapons.
This is a game that rewards high level and premium players while punishing new players and those who dont give them money, making only about a 2.7/10.

I love the game overall, escpecially since I'm a fan of good RTS games, but you may want to grab a few buddies for this game. AoE II's AI isn't exactly all for the "Epic Grand Battle" stuff, if you pick Moderate+ difficulty, get ready to be spammed by waves and waves of Petards, which can get very annoying. But their's good ways to counteract the Petard Spam; Mobile Ranged Units. But after the Petards the AI will spam you with Catapults and Archers. Even though I've only played about 17 hours of this game currently, I can easily counteract them, but my friend who is less skilled than me, not so much. He entitles himself a "Master of RTS'" even though he can't beat me in a game of chess.
Now that the personal stuff is over, let's give you what you came to read. AoE II is a fantastic game, but you can't automatically become a master at it, it requires practice and (A LOT OF) patience. Beware this game will test your wits of RTS to the finest if set on the right difficulty. This game is also better than AoE III IMO. It's because AoE II has nations that technologies can turn the tides of battle even though you may be outnumbered 10-1 (unless the dude your facing Petard spams, remember kids, don't be that dude) but AoE III is basically "Whoever has  more riflemen and siege equipment win" but it's not a bad game. This game was great, once.
Until the developers ruined it. This is my opinion for 3 reasons.
1. The Tech Tree
Robocraft used to be so much fun when the Tech Tree was there. It gave the game a purpose, something to aim for, to       unlock better gear. Since that us now gone the game has no purpose, it has become Minecraft 2 where you can just build whatever you like.
2. The Tier System
All the original players would agree that Robocraft was better with the Tier System. It made the game fair for everyone and made it so you could get matched with Robots the appropriate level to yours. The Tier System and The Tech Tree were what made the game great as you had to play games, earn tech points, unlock new gear and keep doing this until you could get your Robot to the next Tier.
3. Gameplay
In the Respawn and Overclocked update the gameplay changed dramatically both negatively and positively. It made it some once you were dead you were still in the game but this damaged certain things. For me this update made the medic useless. Instead of the idea of the medic helping fallen team mates and stopping team mates getting eliminated they altered it so if you were damaged you could just respawn. I know they kept the normal gamemode but no one played it. Recently to help with the creation of this game becoming Minecraft 2 they have made it so your Robot no longer requires a pilot seat. This is stupid in so many ways and now the Rail Cannon has become somewhat useless. It used to be that if you headshotted a Robots pilot they were instantly destroyed and still is. This means that people who don't have pilot seats have a huge advantage.
Overall Robocraft has been completely destroyed and made unenjoyable.
P.S. I used to play the game through the launcher not through Steam so don't think I'm just some noob with 8.9 hours.

Robocraft at one point had a decent ranking system, a good currency system, and basically a good everything else. It seems as if the developers didn't see what promise they had, and consequently shoved the whole thing down a toilet full of polished turds. There seems to be a misallocation of priority, with all of it going towards radically changing the base game rather than actually listening to the players, and fixing the game.
The old tiering system worked fine, along with the different tiers of armor you could have. It gave a clear difference between the tiers, and actually was something to work towards upgrading. The currency system was also working well, as it didn't give too much money to the point progress was too easy, and never too little to make things seem impossible. But, literally all of that got thrown out the window in favor for absolutely worthless crates and pay-to-win mechanics. The weapons long ago actually had a clear difference as to what they were used for, but again, it was thrown out in favor of new weapons that you're encouraged to buy with real money.
If you've heard the saying, "if it ain't broke, don't fix it," you could very safely assume the developers haven't.

When this game came out, I picked it up and it seemed pretty fun. Limited amount of options for weapons and mobility, but it made sense at the time since I was just starting out. I somehow got to level 81 and stopped playing, thinking I'd come back after playing some other games. Came back and there was a new update. Cool, things seemed a little different, maybe some new blocks came out and I'll have to play some more to unlock better stuff. It didn't seem like something I wanted to do, so I stopped playing. Came back shortly after and there was -another- update. I was given premium for three days, which has become incredibly exclusive now. More blocks added, some visual quirks, got bored because I didn't feel like I was getting anywhere.
Come back.
Another update.
Now, the whole system is revamped. The tech tree is gone, so I can buy anything, I suppose, but at ridiculous prices I would never have enough for unless I paid real money for premium or spent incredible amounts of time grinding. Even if I bought premium, I would still have to spend a ridiculous amount of time playing battles to get money, and it was based on how many other premium players there were. More game modes were added that were confusing.
Another update. Got rid of the currency and added a new form of currency? Which doesn't seem any different except you don't get it at the end of a round. You only get it from selling items you recieve in the new loot crates, (which, by the way, only yield 50% of what they could yield if you spent money on premium) and the crates drop based on placing in the leaderboards. I'm not doing well because other people have better weapons than me because they have more money because they're PREMIUM. I'll automatically place lower because I didn't make the choice to spend money? That seems a little odd to me.
If I wanted to sell my items to buy something else, considering I'm not a premium player, the selling rate is 50% of the purchasing price. But I don't have enough 'robits' to purchase what I want because I had to spend all my money buying basic stuff to keep my robot standing. I can't experiment with other things because it's TOO EXPENSIVE TO DO. Either way, I'm still at a net loss because if I want to buy something. It's frustrating, and grinding is tedious. It should't have to be stated over again.
There's no in between for premium and not-premium. It's either you spend real money to get in game currency, or you spend so much time grinding. Why would I want to buy premium if I don't have any somewhat-easy way to expose myself to the benefits of it? At least give me something to buy that's in my price range and also seems fun to use. The new weapons seem unobtainable due to outrageous prices. It's all so deterring to look at, I feel like quitting and playing something else.
Robocraft could be a really fun game if everything didn't feel so exclusive. Instead of adding new items, make the existing ones more obtainable. Grinding is tedious. I don't want to do it. I want to play a fun game about robots and cool weapons, not slaving away to make pitiful amounts of money.
Please, give us something. I don't get to express my creativity if I don't have enough money to do so. It seems counterproductive.

This game really brings me back to the days when this game was first released.  I was honestly amazed when I figured out how well this game actually aged, and am really happy a facelift like this came about.  I reccommend this game because the more support it gets, the better it will ultimately get for this surprisingly active community.
The updated graphics are welcome, but at the end of the day are not too impressive.  What I do find impressive is the new buildings and units brought in from the Forgotten Empires mod.
Finally the one thing that brings down some points for me is the userpatch has yet to be integrated, which means that the AI, while it has been improved, is not nearly as powerful as it has the potential to be.  I understand the primary focus of this game is multiplayer, so it is a small thing at the end of the day.  But the balancing is very well done, the mechanics work beautifully, and the new graphics give a very nice facelift to this well-aged game.

The following is a forum post I made recently about the state of the game, my overall thought of it is, it requires more work before I can recommend it.
Forum post:
Freejam is ruining this game, slowly but surely...
When I started playing this, there were only thrusters and wheels, and now look at it!
We have wings, propellers, Helicopter blades, tank tracks, legs and all sorts of cool and very fun stuff to make contraptions with!
And that's about it, you make them, and you'd do yourself a favor if you never play with it.
This game and Freejam make absolutely no effort to balance this game. Your CPU level/score is a mere limitation, not a display of complexity or tier. I liked the tier system, it had some problems that could have been ironed out, but what we have right now is the absolute worst thing we could have had.
The game will not care for your 500 cpu marvel that you carefully crafted over the course of an hour, it will not care how well constructed your AT-AT is, or how practical your design was, it will pit you against anyone it can find, for better or worse, the games are never a challenge, they are a chore.
There are two possible ways in which the game will go,
A) You will be crushed, hard, without care.
-The amount of times I found my <1000 CPU robot pit against a guy with a no-less-than 1.5K CPU SMG tank or a ghost-shotgun combo and get literally insta-punted in to a pile of legos is just a proof that this game does not care about you.
B) You will face an enemy that has no more than 3 hours in to the game rolling at you with a slightly modified starter tank or a robot that is begging to be put out of it's misery.
None of the above is fun.
The addition of loot crates is an amazing idea, until you realize that now, the only way to get currency is to smelt things.
So here is what happens:
1) You get blocks/items.
2) You smelt them for, what is essentially, nothing.
3) You grind for days to make a half-decent robot (that will get insta-punted by one of the above)
4) You realize that without Premium the game essentially is a chore.
The things you might do to counter this:
A) Play a different game, wait for a better implementation of this idea to spring up.
B) Buy crates, get nothing useful / don't get what you wanted (This is called gambling and I am pretty sure Freejam is exploiting it's customer base and especially kids with this model).
C) Pay for premium, what is an amount that seems only worth it if you get the life-time pack (since 11$/month for this game is not what I would call worth it ) keeping in mind that paying 50$ for a life time premium for a game that hasn't even come out yet, suffers major changes and loses performance every next month is not a good purchase idea.
What can be done?
This sounds like a stupid idea but keep on reading, REVERT!
Seriously, Last time I played (around when the proto-seeker came out?) was looking pretty well!
You get the in-game currency to buy your gear with, you can recycle, you have your premium mode, which gets you more in-game currency from matches, you have the premium currency (which bought you the premium mode, hence it was slightly exploitative, but not so much as, say, LoL) and allowed you to unlock the parts faster.
I recently noticed that I have some obscure amount of money (~50 cents) in the game's system locked away, that I will probably never use since i use steam for my purchases, and I don't remember (willingly) agreeing on that (my guess the EULA has a "cover my ♥♥♥" section that allows them to even sell my soul, but still...)
But most importantly, clearly define ranges for robots to queue with, for example, you have 0-500, 501-1000, 1001-1500, 1501-2000.
BAM, you have self-balanced system.
As a game-developer and a programmer myself, I see no technical hurdle with this.
If you want to play with a friend, well, you all make robots in the same tier, that's it.
I recently introduced some of my friends to this game and the overall impressions were so low, only one is playing it with me, and I'm about to stop playing (and so will he), because I feel like my time making the robots and my time playing the game are both rewarded with nothing exciting or interesting.
Now, all of the above are just the "Meta" part of all this.
In-game balance has it's own issues.
One such issues is the FLAK, I understand why we needed it, but adding something like a flak cannon seems like a very heavy handed solution to a problem that perhaps required more finesse.
AA in games like this is a big question (balance vise).
You make it too strong, people stop playing air.
You make it too weak, people take advantage.
Right now it's in the middle, but in the worst way possible, what do I mean by that:
The amount required for effective air-denial is locking likely locking you out of effective ground combat, and the effective amount in this case is so effective that anything the air just melts to a puddle of salt and tears.
Sounds like a specialization thing, right?
NOPE.avi
As soon as there are no Air vehicles, you are doomed to drive around with a few sorry-looking smgs you put on there and you wonder, what is the purpose of the basic FLAK, it's too costly when it's effective and too weak when it's reasonably taxed...
The only effective FLAK/AA is the high end one, and the high end one is too effective, making air-play frustrating in almost all cases.
The solution:
We make so many robots, yet at a time we can only use one, why not a loadout system, you can have 4 loadouts (one for each CPU tier) with 3 bots in each loadout, they are the same CPU tier, and you can swap them at will upon re-spawn.
Problem solved, now you have a dynamic circulation of play-styles, no AA, punish for lack there of, not enough support?, no problem shield + heal coming right up.
With the complexity of the game, it's understandable that this might be harder to implement, but considering how bad the load-times are already, the performance is already plummeting.
I also have thought for a long time on how to fix the melee, and one my ideas was that it would be like a normal weapon, deal damage only when activated, once it is activated, it deals damage for .5-1 seconds and is on CD for that much longer, the damage can be also adjusted to fit the bill, but honestly other than it being OP with certain modules the melee is fine, perhaps it can be subject to mutual exclusivity along with other modules (blink and ghost for example) or those modules can just have higher cpu and/or energy costs to ballance out the effectiveness.
I am surely missing some things, but I would like to add that I am writing all of this not (only) out of anger and salt but because I really, really enjoy this game, but I am pushed away more and more by both this new meta game and business model.
I hope to find constructive and thoughtful comments and perhaps even for a developer response, but something tells me that won't happen...

This game had a lot of potential. Now you're at the mercy of an RNG that I'm 90% certain they rigged so purchased crates give better loot.
I spent money on this game a while back, not to give me any "combat advantage", but to support developers whom I honestly liked, and because I could get some cool cosmettics in exchange. Now I wouldn't think about spending a cent because they may as well rename the company "Freescam".
Some of the good stuff they had (emphasis on "
"):
Megabots: An endgame goal for you to achieve, giant robots with their own tier and gamemode. These puppies were a big reason a lot of people played, to try and achieve that status. And they're gone.
Boss battles: A gamemode that pitted 12 or so low-level players against 4 high-level players. This was a really fun gamemode on both ends, because the high level players need to stick together and protect eachother in order to win. And it's gone.
Leveling system: The old leveling system had 2 things: Levels and Tiers. Your tier was dictated by how many parts you had, and strength of said parts, and would have you fight people of simillar strength. Your level was dependant on how much damage you deal/heal, and would increase your maximum CPU, which allows more blocks to be placed. The old system also had Tech points, which allowed you to choose what items you want to unlock and use. All of this is gone.
Before the "Epic" loot update, you had Robopoints, or RP, which you earned by playing your role in multiplayer battles. You used these to purchase the items you unlocked with Tech Points, and the prices weren't too outrageous. Now, post-epic loot, you have Robits, which replace RP. They said they divided all shop prices and RP balances by 63 to "give them more round numbers". I did the math, and they most certainly are lying. The Mega module (previously mega seat) was worth 1,000,000 RP before epic loot, now it's 145,000 robits. 145,000*63=9,135,000.
Apparently FJ owes like a million dollars to some mobile gambling game company, so that may have had something to do with it.
Now you've got people who just make a flying cube with shields all over, and 1-2 lock-on missile launchers which outclass the old Plasma launchers entirely. Then there's the Protoseeker which is like the old SMG except with autoaim. Oh, and railguns are useless now since they removed pilot seats, thus making it impossible to punish people for bad building. Oh, and let's not forget the Nanos, AKA Mediguns. These WERE arguably the most important bot type, especially in higher tiers. Now they've removed their ability to do damage so as to "balance" them since we now have the ability to have all weapon types on one build. Also autohealing, that makes them entirely useless.

I do not usually bother to review a game if I believe it is bad, but this is an exception. This game was once an amazing game full of potential. That was a long, long time ago. It went from being a fun game, where thousands of players designed unique robots, and took to the battlefields to duke it out, robot laser mayhem style. Since then, it has really gone downhill. I feel it is not imporant to go into a long list of the problems, as thousands of users already have. A quick overview of these problems are: Absurdly expensive guns that literally require hundred of matches of grinding to obtain one of, or can be easily bought with micro-transactions, unoriginal and overpowered bot designs taking advantage of an exploit (looking at you TESSERACTS!) which are shared through the bot store (For absurd prices, of course) The matches, after loot revamps, have gone from teams battling strategically to win, to selfish individuals using more than one gun type, trying to be a one-man army and get all the points, (And the MVP crate). To highlight some of the stupid updates; Full Spectrum Combat: Want your tanky robot to be able to be one-hit by mega plasma bombs? We do too. Armor has been removed, and the unique tiers and respect they afforded you are also gone. Tiers are gone, and matching is now based off robot ranking. Logic has been decapitated, and now your robot can simply be a massive plasma gun powered by it's own recoil (Which is actually kind of fun) To make matters worse, they released a loot revamp update. Guess what this removed... MONEY. You now get crates (Because originallity is dead) at the end of each battle, which, if you do not screw over your team to solo and get the highest score, generally give your bad items... BUT you have to pay money to be premium to even get half of it. Matching has been destroyed, and you finally get into battles in under 30 seconds. BUT those battles are generally with robots that make your robot (if you are not endgame) look like a speck. I said I would not go into a long list of problems, and that is mostly true. Though this list is quite extensive, it hardly scratches the surface of the horror this once-great game has become. The developers, of course, refuse to listen to the communtiy, and release horribly update after horrible update, with nothing in mind but cash. Just to show how bad this has gotten, the reviews say "Recent: Mostly Negative. Overall: Mostly Positive." This is the only game I have ever seen mostly negative on in any way. I join the flocks of long-time players disapointed with this game, and the only thing I have to say is, Get your crap together developers!
P.S. The developers claim they listen to the community, which is of course a blatant lie.

Robocraft in one word...'progressing'. It is most certainly not to the point where I would stand up for Freejam's decisions as of late, as most of them have upset a large portion of their more senior fanbase; which also includes me. I have 800+ hours clocked in this game, and the early 500's were really a blast, but the farther I got, the more the game got ever-more diluted by bad updates and poorly executed decision-making. While this game is certainly not P2W as most would say, I think it is highly unfair to all the players that paid for many things in this game early on that all the things they bought with real money is suddenly free for everyone, and all their efforts were wasted. When I first began playing, it was an amazing (and honestly terrifying) experience. You would leap into a fast-paced battle, discovered that no, fleeing off of a cliff is not a good idea, and battle really felt like battle. Everything was balanced, even though there were few things in the game itself to balance, and it just felt as if your every move really did count. Nowadays, it's a miracle if you don't get into a game with a hacker or some form of a smurf. Recent weapons added into the game made it seem as if the little guys would never ride because their would always be just another rocket launcher on a cube with 2 treads waiting for you on the other side of that wall. I used to love this game to bits, it made me happy, I aspired to fly, to have freedom over my decisions, to succeed and grow...But now, all that's really left is a community only willing to spite one another and a game that feels like it's taken several steps backwards. This game isn't done, and probably will never be, but at this point, I don't think it's worth starting out. I know I wouldn't again. If the game gets fixed and balanced, then maybe I'll be willing to change my review, but at it's current state, I doubt I'd change my mind any time soon. Sorry Freejam, but you can't just ignore the people who've been with you since the beginning.

TL;DR: Try this game for yourself and make your own opinion. Hey, it's free.
First of all, I played before the Epic Loot update, and I played enough to understand the gist. I spent no money (and still haven't)
Almost every negative review on this game is from people who dislike the Epic Loot update. Now, some of them are actually intelligent and mention some major points to why the update damaged the game, and that's fair. But, most of them are people complaining that the game became "pay to win." Which is absolutely ridiculous. If anything, the game was more pay to win before the update. For anyone unfamiliar, instead of the typical robits of today, you had basic currency and premium currency. You were rewarded basic currency after every match you completed, but the only way to earn premium currency was to buy it with real money. That premium currency was used to buy items like the Sabertooth, Eagle, and Rhino heads, etc. Now this wouldn't be a problem if the premium currency didn't also buy weapons, but it did, like the aeroflak cannon for example. That weapon used to be locked behind a paywall. Now, in this version, every weapon and every vanity item can be earned through loot boxes or the forge. It's also important to mention that premium was still a thing in the old version of the game. Based on all of these facts, you can probably understand my confusion when people go around saying the devs "got greedy" when the game was probably MORE PTW before Epic Loot.
I think the update improved the game rather than damaging it, because it evened out the playing field. Everyone had the same chances at getting every item, so you had to design your bots accordingly to counter every situation, Aeroflak or railguns for flyers, lasers or chainguns for closer range, etc. Now, even with everyone being capped out at 2000 CPU, the game evened out even more, leaving the deciding factors of battles to equipment and design prowess. Building a tanky bot increases health, but decreases weapon energy and speed. Building a small fast bot does the opposite. Rarer weapons don't gurantee victory. Every weapon and tactic has a counter, but if you're caught without one, you will lose. I think people mistake this for "overpoweredness."
Personally, I like where this game is going. With the new update allowing you to earn Robits in boxes (which are much more valuable than the items themselves, I might add) saving up is becoming easier, allowing every player to own the more interesting legendary weapons. Gamemodes are becoming more tactical. Above all, I think you should try this game out yourself with an open mind, whether you played before Epic Loot or not. Who knows, you might actually have fun.

Im gonna be honest. Robocraft is not what it used to be.
2 Years ago, this game was pretty good. No crate ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t, no premium ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t. Build, Drive, Fight.
The game just got greenlit on steam, i picked it up and gave it a try. I loved it. You could build your own robot and fight other people, damnit! That was cool! And the more you played, the bigger you could make your robot, unlock new weapons, and rank up your robot to new tiers. You had to repair your robot with robopoints after each fight. I remember going into Tier 6 with my dinky little Tier 5 robot and getting demolished. But as i played through, i got better, and stronger. When megabots were announced, i'd hop into a boss battle with my friends and coordinate against this stupidly high level player and loose most of the time, but when we won, it was great. I'd scramble for a premium code every time an update was pushed so i could have those few days of extra robopoints from each battle. It was the most fun i'd had with robocraft. That is what robocraft (in my opinion) should have stayed.
Then the 'Respawned and Overclocked' and 'Team Orders' updates came out. I think this was a great improvement to Robocraft as a whole. New gamemode, New features, Actual teamplay without chatting was huge. I felt like this was the best time for jumping into Robocraft and just having fun. But i missed the old gamemodes, like boss battles and such. I love the new Battle arena game mode but those other ones were fun too! Why remove them?
Im not sure when Robocraft started to take the wrong path, but i think it was around when the 'Robocraft: Unleashed' update happened. Tiering was removed entirely so that any player could start using any cube they wanted. This was pushed so that players could be more 'artistic' with their builds. Literally, the update promo is a bunch of robots that wouldnt really be good in a firefight. This is when Robocraft didnt feel like Robocraft again. The entire progression part of the game was just swiped away into the trash. You no longer had to earn new cubes, they were just laid out infront of you. All you had to do was earn enough money and bam there you go. You still had to earn the new cubes, but not in the same way. It didn't feel right.
After this they had a good flow of new content. New movement types, new weapons. They upgraded their engine, added more and free robot garage slots, and added a paint gun to color your robot. Although most of the colors were locked behind a paywall, i didnt really care to color my robot much. It didnt really affect gameplay. My only gripe in this stage of the game was that you had to grind intensely to get one of the new weapons. They cost alot of robopoints, and you would spend way more time than you probably should have to get them. What really bothered me is that if you just payed a small price for their 'Premium Currency', you could unlock the weapon immediately. The game turned from free-to-play progression battle arena to Pay-to-win robot fights. If you didnt have premium, or didnt want to spend money to get a new weapon or gadget, tough luck. This was more of the calm before the storm.
Then Freejam removed a feature that had been in the game for a long time, and took players many hours to make and grind for. Megabots. They just completely wiped them out of the game. They replaced the megabot module with a 'Power Booster' which if equiped increased the robots power regeneration. Alot of players didnt like this, as they spent alot of time making megabots. It was sad to see the feature go.
This is where♥♥♥♥♥♥hit the fan. New update to the game 'Epic Loot' threw out everything and replaced it (again), and added crates as a cherry on top. They changed the currency and made all the cubes you received centered around the crates. You'd get cubes from crates, but you could get more if you bought premium. How convenient. No progression, just RNG crate drops. You could buy cubes still, but you'd have to 'recycle' the cubes you already had. Not cool. Items were now branded with rarity so the bigger, more cooler weapons were rare drops from crates, sometimes only available if you had premium. So now anyone could get the weapons in the game if they were lucky, or had money to spend. I wouldnt say compeletely pay-to-win, but it certainly would be alot easier to progress if you had some cash to throw around.
Oh and aparently this game is still 'Early Access'. This game was finished maybe a year ago. Highly disapointed with Freejam, and their response to the latest update. Maybe, just maybe, if your recent reviews are mostly negative, you'd think you did something wrong.
TL;DR - Game was fun with tiering and progression. Constantly added new features and improved the game. Game was good. Suddenly flipped the game on its head and removed progression, tiering, changed the currency, and made the games progression centered around RNG crate opening. GG Freejam.

Reposting of a review I made for the original, sans HD features:
Unquestionably my favorite RTS, Age of Kings has claimed more hours—more DAYS—of my life than any other strategy game. I've been trying for several minutes now to come up with something brief that would summarize why this game is the best, but I find that I am unable to. There's just too much. If I were to list all of the things that I like about this game, I would basically be making a list of everything there is in the entire game, because I quite literally like EVERYTHING about this game. The map types, the game modes, the civilizations, the buildings, the units, the technologies, the unique features of each civ, the artwork (256 colors have never been used so well) and of course, the scenario editor. The quality of the mod tools is fantastic, and if you browse online, you can find thousands of great multiplayer maps, full campaigns, and even heavily triggered scenarios that play out like RPG's or adventure games. This game does not support the higher resolutions that you're probably accustomed to, but it is still a great-looking game and of course the gameplay is still as great as it ever was. Highly recommended.

Age of Empires II is the very first video game I ever played and it remains my favorite game till today. The aesthetics, history, complexity of this game had me hooked to it for nearly 15 years. And this new HD version obviously kept all the original games charm since it's virtually the same. But there are a few very nice new features that I enjoyed immesely.
What I like best about the HD version is the steam workshop support. Mods can be conveniently applied to the game, I had a few graphic textures installed to my version and it totally revitalized the experience.
The Forgotten expansion is a bit rough on the edges in the beggining, but with almost a monthly update it is getting better and better. In time I think all the new content added to the game, such as new civilizations, new campaigns, new units would match the quality of the first expansion: the Conquerors.
I have never played multiplayer in the past, now with steam support I did try a few games, and it is very user friendly to say the least, I might do that more in the future.
In summary what I love about this game and this HD version is that it brought a ture classic game back to life, it brought a generation of gamers who love this game together. I would recommend this game to anyone who have played AOE2 in the past, who is open-minded to classic strategy games, and people who love ancient civilizations. Age of Empires 2 is one of those rare experience that never grows old and keeps getting better. No game has ever impacted me as much and no other game ever will.

I got into this game a year or two ago. A genius idea it was back then. Near unlimited creativity, fun gameplay, a good community, low lag, yadda yadda yadda. That's all auxillary stuff. It's what makes a good game into a great game. But what about the essential stuff? It was all there, too, and in innovative fashions: a well-developed and balanced tech tree, specialization to create diverse teams, currency rewards based on how well you performed, quick and fair matchmaking, the list goes on and on. All of this was essential; you play well, you get currency, you upgrade your robot in the direction you want, and you go through the tiers, facing harder opponents as you go.
Ah, what I wouldn't give to go back to the days when this game wasn't a steaming pile of pay-to-win trash.
Creativity? Gone. Premade robots are the only real contenders now. Why is that?
Progression? Gone. Now you get a linear tech "tree" that unlocks without the tech points of before.
How do you get new parts, you ask? Why, with the currency of course!
...Except not the same currency.
Now you get a currency which is only granted to you based upon how many parts you sell. And how do you get these parts?
With the completely original and foolproof crate system, how else?
For just a single match, YOU can get a crate of at least five items that YOU didn't choose. Oh, not even that, though, since one is dangled in front of your face like a pet toy, essentially going, "You COULD have this, but you have to be a PREMIUM MEMBER!"
And there's the center of the problem. Membership.
Jesus H. Christ on ice skates, membership costs so much that you'll need to just start paying with your dignity. $1.99 a DAY. That's about $60 a month -- money that could EASILY buy you at least three retail games on sale, or a full-price title -- and about $725-730 a year.
You could buy at least 25 decent games with that kind of money.
Oh, but that's not even the half of it.
What do you get for your money? Well, you get:
-A color wheel (Did I mention you only get a whopping FOUR colors to choose from, if you're a normal member?)
-Some rare weapons in crates (that don't do nearly as much damage as they originally did)
-Instant access to the stronger weapons (I omit the word "tier" because there IS no tier system any more; little Johhny that just joined the game and threw together a gun on a car frame with no armor will go up against someone with 2,000 hours with a fully decked out air bomber. Funny thing is, if you get lucky, you can take down the "highest level" players with entry-level gear.)
-Some cosmetics and stuff that don't do anything
...I think you get the gist. It's not worth it.
So, in conclusion, it's a prime example of what happens when money goes to a dev team's head but they want to keep that "free to play" sticker on Steam so poor losers with nothing in their wallet can actually play something. Or, rather, suckers with too much money to spend waste it on their pay to win scheme. After all, winning feels good!
Oh, and did I mention it's buggy and laggy now?

Cons:
Losing a good item sucks.  (It shows the 3 items you would've gotten from the loot box if you'd bought membership.)
You only have access to four colours when editing your craft, unless you buy membership.
If one person on your team leaves, prepare for it to become a 2v5 or even a 1v5. (Even if your team is still winning.)
Needs 2-3 more weapon types to tie it all together.
Spawn-camping is a huge issue, and I'm part of the problem because it usually causes people to ragequit.
Too much Gundam. Not enough Medabots.

Time makes fools of us all. When Age of Empires II was originally released in 1999 it was simply an astounding game. Between the multitude of civilizations, random maps, deep campaign, and multiple gameplay modes a person could play for hundreds of hours EASY and never touch the additional content. When such stuff was touched not only could people play in tense multiplayer matches but there was a detailed scenario editor that allowed us to make whatever we saw fit. It seemed truly revolutionary, truly amazing to have such control and seemingly unlimited possibilities. Then the expansion came out and even more was added. For a time it seemed as if Age of Empires would change the face of gaming.
That was in 1999. It's now 2013 and the game has finally been re-released for a new generation to play. Does it still hold water? Or is it a relic of the past best left to be admired and forgotten?
The answer is 'both'.
First off the good. The gameplay, which has always been Age of Empire's strong point, is still amazingly strong. Age of Empires, since the day it was first made, has always slowed down the gameplay in favor of more drawn out and epic engagements which the series still manages to preform wonderfully. This is not, nor ever has been, a game about having towering champions that fight through slews of foes with carefully timed spells and abilities. This has been a game about armies clashing while heavy sieges rage on and allies preform expert flanking maneuvers with well-developed armies to allow you the chance to win. And Age of Empires plays to this wonderfully. Almost everything is run smoothly and battles can reach truly epic scales. When playing with my friend a battle happened where a massive army of invading Franks smashed up against my Persian walls and I needed to preform a desperate scramble for resources to develop and field a few war elephants to fend them off while my British friend sent a small squad of longbowmen to aid in my defense while he flanked around back and laid into their now-undefended town. The entire battle hinged on if the Franks could break my wall before my friend reached their town. It was fierce and over a hundred units must have died in that one battle alone, but the wall survived with 95 HP left.
Such epic-scale battles happen with frequency in this game. With the defensive focus it is very possible for games to become very long, drawn-out, and epic. Simply allowing the player to build walls alone grants a unique perspective not easily found in other RTS's while the slower development times and option for in-depth research makes it so that every battle will truly be distinct as it will be hard to find opponents who play the exact same way. To top it off, the random map function increases the replayability immensely. Having a completely new and different map every game allows for every game to unfold in a different manner. Age of Empires fits very well into the 'easy to learn, difficult to master' category while never being too brutal or too easy.
Additionally much off the campaign is wonderfully detailed still and very challenging. Though it lacks the technical depth found in more modern RTS's the sheer size and detail allow for many hours to be sunk just chewing through the default campaign. That's not to mention that many of the campaigns are very fun and enjoyable and can easily end up being played multiple times.
Lastly the inclusion of the Steam Workshop is wonderful. Allowing people to create and modify some of the game content and create and share their own scenarios makes it so that the game will, almost certainly, endure for many years to come.
And now for the bad.
The game has clearly aged. It came out in 1999 and it plays like it did so. Many simple conveniences that would have been easy to implement, some of which were in later titles, are simply non-existent. Things like an auto-explore button which would have helped out with the early game simply do NOT exist. The limit on the number of selectable units is also particularly annoying when there is no need for such a limitation. Even minor technical bugs, like trebuchets unpacking as if they had 17 range when they only have 16 (this means you need to manually pilot each into range instead of simply telling them to attack a building) persist despite that they should have been corrected long ago.
Additionally, despite being a 'HD' version, many of the graphics are simply not 'HD' quality. It's very easy to see individual frames on buildings with motion, like mills, which ruins the whole point of making it 'HD'. Though this is alleviated somewhat by steam workshop mods, the obliviousness to detail makes people who haven't spent time figuring out the 'best' graphics patches truly jarring. To say nothing of how cumbersome many of the sprites function, often lacking true sprites for a given direction and simply going with the animation closest which results in things like people managing to walk diagonally while facing right.
Too add to this, the scenario editor that gathered much praise originally simply lacks the detail it once had, and could have easily obtained. Simple things like allowing players to edit all of a unit stats instead of a select few and allowing players to make their own, unique, civilizations were not included, despite these potentially offering much replayability.
And to put the icing on the cake, the achievements tend to act buggily, sometimes not registering until the next time the person plays the game or later instead of appearing on the spot.
The Verdict: On the whole Age of Empires II HD plays more like a port of the original game with some minor graphics upgrades, tacked-on Steam Workshop, and few other, similar, upgrades. On the positive, it retains much of the original charm that caused the original to be a classic. On the negative, it retains so much of the original charm it fails to take advantage of the more than ten years of improvements that have come out since then, both in other RTS's and in their own series of games. If you were a fan of the original and no longer have your disks or are unable to use them due to many years of use, you will almost certainly enjoy this game. If you are not, if you enjoy it or not will likely come down to the deciding factor of 'are you willing to play a game that, basically was made 14 years ago and plays like it'. If you are willing, Age of Empires HD offers loads of depth and replayability that can keep you entertained easily for well over 100 hours without even truly scratching the surface. Otherwise, it's a relic from a bygone era best looked at, admired, and then moved on from.

- Water looks way way more like water, they added a 3d rendering option. (So you can switch it off too)
- In the "Forgotten Empires" Expansion which is new to this game, you can play more (lacking a better word) "modern" Empires, such as India, Hungary,  etc.
- Many new map types were added, and the option to size the map EPIC. Which it really becomes! Your scouts take 10 minutes to go a whole round. (At least mine do).
- Various little improvements to the User Interface (UI). You can now select more units with one selection (which comes in quite handy with the 500 Population Limit)
- Military units can now "invade" a location. Sending them to a spot on the map with that command, they will attack anybody on their way.
- You can now ultra fast forward (to save time in single player, i don't reccomend it for multiplayer, though it is possible)
And a few more I forgot to mention or even don't know of yet.
All in all, "Microsoft Studios" set themself a really low goal in adding tiny features like the ability to select a few more units at a time, and changing a number "200" to "500" for the Population Limit (which a mod that was made for AOE 2 already did.)
So now you may ask me, "why do you NOT recommend the game?".
Well the answer is simple. The masterminds at "Microsoft Studios" broke the game.
By that i mean, it's unplayable if you don't own a brandnew last generation high end PC that can play Crisis 3, Battlefield 4, and all those games at Ultra Graphics.
I have, like many of you, a 2 year old configuration:
CPU: AMD FX 4100, Quad-Core, downclocked to 3 GHz
GPU: AMD HD Radeon 6970, 2GB  GDDR5 RAM
RAM: 8 GB, CL7
The other parts to not influent the raw game performance.
My OS is Windows Vista Ultimate 64bit.
After you read this, you might think: "Ok, so you can run the game 4 times parallel of course."
Well, no i can't. And the majority around the world can't either.
===
Here is the problem why:
After like 5 minutes into the game, when i've built maybe..5 houses, the game gets a seizure and drops the framerate to about 10-5. Additionally, every 1 or 2 seconds, the game halts for another second, like someone hits the pause button every second. (Which of course nobody does, it occurs in bth Singleplayer and Multiplayer.
I did experiment with that, too look what is causing it. The more units are present on the map, you know because logically every players empire grows in the first 10 minutes, the more it lags permanently.
On the other hand, the more units are "on screen" like when one of my friends sends me an army of 100 Knights or other stuff, the more it lags proportionally to the number of units present on screen.
===
What did help temporarily, was to turn the screen resolution (which you strangely can not do in the game's settings anymore) down to 1024x 768. With that, it runs at 30 FPS, which seems to be the max for the game (i guess because it's 2d, but i'm not sure about that.
Many of you might know what this resolution looks like ingame. You can see your Towncenter but nothing else, because of the small resolution. And that is, of course, unplayable. Raising the resolution to 1280x720 (which is JUST A TINY BIT more pixels difference if you do your math.) makes the game drop it's FPS to 15 again.
Dont even think of Full HD (which is 1920x1080), that is my native resolution.
It doesn't solve the problem too, because you can still feel the 1 second intervall lag when scrolling and when units move.
So what did I try next, I set the game's executable to run only on 1-2 cores of my CPU, because lots of older games have difficulties adjusting the game's clock to the CPU clock speed because its so much higher than the game was designed for.
Didn't help.
Downgrading GPU Drivers. Didn't help.
Running the original AOE 2. No problems at all.
===
If you remember, i said something about brandnew high end PC earlier in this text. (Sorry it is so long, but i want as many players as possible to read it so they don't waste their 20$, or 30$ if you add the "Forgotten" expansion pack.)
What i meant by that is, a friend of mine owns a brandnew (a few months ago) elite gaming notebook, that has all the newest CPU and GPU to that point.
He can run Battlefielfd 4 at Ultra smoothly. And even on his machine the lag of this AOE 2 HD game is noticable. It doesnt drop the FPS, but every second you can see the stuttering. For him it doesnt affect the gameplay like it does for me.
You can read throughout the internet (and here on Steam) of this "massive lag" problem. And no-one knows any solution to it.
Today is the 26th of April. I saw right now that on 24th of April there was an update to the game. But in the changelog they only mentioned adding a few campaigns (which of course is
important) and minor fixes of displaying bugs in leaderboards in multiplayer.
I'm going to check it out now, if somehow magically it suddenly works.
But it won't. I know it.
If you don't believe me, google it.
Make sure you know what you are talking about before you comment.
I hope you found my article to be useful, and you will not give your good money to "Microsoft Studios" anytime soon.
Thank you.
You are welcome to contact me to discuss this review, or bring any attempts on solutions for the broken game.
- Sgt Cold.
Update 1st Nov 2017:
After giving it another try 3 years after my initial review, and some of the performance has improved indeed.
By that I mean I can now play smoothly until I have around 100 units. Once I reach the ~200 mark, the game starts to drop FPS again, and constant stutters and freezes are the norm, and increase the more time goes on.
The worst part is, that the AI (Im using the "new" AI, which does not behave any different to the classic one by the way, the units seem to get stuck during tasks more often even) is incapable of doing navigation calculations when "too much" is going on on the map. I played a 8p "ludikris" map and a group of ~40 paladins was unable to hunt down a slower moving infantry unit because they all simultaneously stopped every few steps (to recalculate or whatever crap) but the single enemy infantry just kept moving without any interrupting. So one swordman was able to outrun a pack of 40 cavalry units because they didn't move properly? A joke.
I also noticed some building collisions not woring properly for navigation, like a castle was treated as only a 3x3 obstacle, so units moved through one side like there was nothing.
Now I can play somewhat properly, but not at all to the point where the "new" population limit is intended to go.
I assume that ai players are always ahead of me every age until the imperial age, because I farm resources and don't build military until late into the game. By that logic, when I have 150 units, they all must have about 180-220 units, which would result in  ~1600 total player units. This seems to be already too much for the engine? What about when all 8 player have 500 units? 4000 total? I will do some tests using the editor.
However this game remains as a big ♥♥♥♥♥íng middlefinger from Microsoft Studios to me.
Not only does it not feature any original new content (all "new" content were previously made by users as mods for the original game but it performs worse than the original game made for machines in 1999 with system requirements of: CPU: 166 MHz, RAM: 32 MB

Without going into too much depth, this game started making updates that not only started making the game crash for most players, and they havent even tried to fix it. they just keep putting out updates.
the game itself used to be unique and fun like an engineering simulation, like an advanced-yet-still-somehow-simpler multiplayer Besiege.
however, the recent updates and stuff have added about 1% cool stuff and about 99% things that ruin it.
for example, the domination-like game used to have 4 towers, this prompted each team to maintain about 2 towers each. if you have any less, then you need to start a defense and regain control. if you have more, then you need make sure that you keep them and start pushing more for either the last tower or just to kill the teams base. this admittedly could potentially make games REALLY long (one of mine lasted an hour!) but it required the team to maintain more communication and some form of strategy. it somehow simultaneously made it harder to speedrun, yet easier to play. all the different towers made it so even a team with 0 towers can potentially recover, if they do it right.
however they reduced the towers to 3, meaning whichever team that has the middle tower is more or less garunteed a win, seeing as the game becomes 2-1 and more towers makes you even stronger. it is alarmingly more difficult to either take the middle tower back, and maintain your last tower at the same time, because the whole opposing team is now going for your tower, and you still have to manage defense/offense at the same time. basically, whoever gets two towers first, wins the game. unless the other team is really bad.
to put simply, the games current reviews are mosty negative because they ruined it and ARENT LISTENING TO THE COMMUNITY
until they start making some free online polls and actually take them into consideration, i would not suggest you play this game, or buying any of the DLC.

Old-school addictive fun; Age of Empires II brings back nostaligia of my earlier years, but with revamped graphics that do not ruin the character of the old game. Although dated, this real time strategy is still more fun that ever, with online lobbies bustling so it's easy to find or create a game within a few minutes. I would reccomend this game even to those who are new to AoE. Just beware newcomers, the online lobby is a harsh place and you may have to get used to loosing a lot of games!
However, this game is not without it's faults. Both offline and online, this game has a few bugs. Nothing that is a deal-breaker, but nonetheless you will spot a few if you put a few hours into this game. To name but a few, units getting stuck in the graphics, AI players donating you resources that they don't even have (even if they are your opponents!) This happened during an offline game, and both myself and the AI had no market, so this should not have been possible even if they did try to send me resources... Online gameplay can sometimes be ruined if bad connections are apparent between players, the most irritating of which are when the game hangs and can't be quit without killing the games process in Windows Task Manager and rebooting it. Also, if someone goes out of sync in the game, everyone in that game looses rank, this can be quite substantial and is extremely unfair to the team that may have won the game fair and square.
Other than those small issues, this does not stop me from putting stupid amounts of hours into this game. It's a good laugh, very fun to play, and it's very, very addictive. You have been warned!
I still love the game! A must buy, I play it once a year and still enjoy it every year!

I'm not going to review this game like others have (based on recent changes) because I only picked up the game recently. Therefore, my review will be 100% based on the current state of the game.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Robocraft is a robotic vehicle building/combat simulator where the player uses voxel (minecraft) style building tools to create a machine to fight other players. Players can choose from a variety of weapons (though there is a problem with this system, which I will adress later), movement options and additional tactical equipment that can be added as you like it. The only constraints are what you have, a CPU limit (meant to keep lower level players from making super-bots) and your imagination. You can make an all-feared death tank, a flying twig with a missile rack, a bipedal man that falls over whenever you deploy him, or just a box that does nothing. I've actually seen a few of those.
The gameplay itself is fairly simple and split up into about five modes. One single player mode versus (admittedly awful) cpu robots, a multiplayer 'deathmatch' where the first to a set amount of kills wins, a moba-like tower-capture simulator that takes much longer than the other modes, a free-for-all arena, and a team versus deathmatch with permadeath somewhat akin to Counter strike. The last one was my favorite mode, but also the shortest in terms of round length and rewards.
Each battle ends with the player obtaining a loot box (except for in the cases of disconnection or absolute failure) of varying rarity. Better performance results in greater loot. Boxes contain anywhere from four to eight items that you can add to your robot, ranging from wheels, legs, weapons, block packs, and some aesthetics. You can also craft any items you can find in loot boxes, somewhat lowering the RNG issue a lot of people express, but to do this you must recycle items you have, and the return rate is incredibly low. I've scrapped the full content of twenty boxes that I got last night and I still don't have enough for some of the items in the shop.
This leads to the first issue; the reason I have been scrapping most of my items I get is because they are worthless to me (I only use one robot for battles, a plasma walker with a heavy cannon I got legitimately and other low-tier weapons) and will never be used. Some of the epic and legendary tier items are incredibly overpowered; For example, one legendary item is a missile rack that locks on to opponents, has massive health, and can instantly destroy most other bots in one volley. Worst of all, it can be attached to a very small flying bot (the physics in this game are shot, but that generally just leads to hilarious falls except for in this game) and wreak havoc on any team without a good sniper or the (also rare) aeroflak cannon.
As well, games are not ranked based on player experience or skill; they are ranked based on CPU used. Since lower level players have less CPU to use, it usually means that low CPU games have worse players. However, anyone with a good weapon and knowledge of vehicle design can do the aforementioned 'stick a legendary on a helicopter' exploit and kill off new players who have no idea how to counter this, and oftentimes cannot do anything to stop it. This allows the exploiter to get a free high-level crate in nearly every match.
Other than that, the gameplay community seems pretty tame. Most players never even use the chat feature, and I only tend to feel angry or cheated when an enemy is using a legendary item against me (because it implies they are winning because of luck, not skill) and I tend to find most games satisfying.
All in all, I would pretty well say that Robocraft is in a good spot right now. The game could certainly use some work with its currency, as it feels broken and worthless right now, and i have noticed a few very obvious exploits, but other than that, I've had a lot of fun with it.
I did not realize at the time of this review, but apparently the game features heavy-handed premium content. I wrongly stated that you get four to eight items from boxes; As it turns out, premium doubles the amount of items you get, and the game gives you free premium at the beginning if you attach an E-Mail account to the game. Since my premium has ran out, I have muissed multiple rare/epic items because of the spots I could no longer obtain.
This feature is EXTREMELY frustrating, and added on to the fact that premium players also seem to obtain  extra EXP from matches as  well, lowers my favor by quite a lot. The game is very fun, but I do not plan on playing  any  more as my progress was  just shot.
