I may still play the game every now and then, to see how things are doing, but honestly, the game began going downhill long ago. First, the tier-flattening from ten tiers down to five. Next, the introduction of weapons other than the original trio (SMG, plasma and rail) and the Nanotech Disruptors, starting with Flak. The introduction of using multiple weapons at once sealed the deal, and this new loot-crate system is just the devs taunting us all. The energy system was strategic, at least for a while, but with the loot crate system's rebalance to all weapons, it's now just "there," as energy runs out either too quickly or too slowly.
The game is now more of a contest of who can shoot first, between shotgun-mechs and shotgun-hovers, "Tesla trolls" who waste all their energy in one shot and are only efficient in cutting large guns like shotguns and flaks off of enemy mechs, then taking ages to kill them, and railgun-bed mechs who are literally just 9 or so mech legs held together with aero-rods (extended connectors) and coated in railguns.
And yet, what do the devs do? They pretend it's the tiering that's the problem, so they get rid of tiering all at once, allowing new players with tiny starter bots to run into hulking colossi lugging around shotguns, missile launchers and flak cannons that promptly one-shot them.
I would post a legitimate review, since the game used to be simple and fun, back when Nanotech Disruptors were introduced, and even before that, but I literally cannot think of any positives for the game now. The gameplay has gotten glitchy and laggy with all the new weapons introduced, and the old weapons have been made either grossly overpowered or grossly underpowered. Armor tiering was removed, along with weapon tiering, so everybody's the exact same. And while you'd think that might help make it more skill-based (the devs sure did,) believe me, it doesn't. The gameplay stayed the exact same in some cases, and got worse in other cases, while we had less and less variety to work with over time.
And the "paint" for your bots... having to pay to use the colors that were previously free for everyone to use via different tiers of armor? Low-blow. But, I guess Freejam has gone the path of the greedy dev on this one, since now, with the introduction of the loot crate system, you have to use RNG just to earn money, and the RNG itself is horrific, it doesn't scale with level either so a new player might get parts that are too big for their bots that they'll have to scrap and sell, and scrapping/selling them returns barely any money.
Meanwhile, a high-level player, at the same time, will get those same parts, which are too weak for his usage, and so he has to do three dozen matches and top-score every single one just to get enough "Robits" to buy one Tier 5 leg for his mech, thanks to how bad the RNG is. Meanwhile, both players frequently win Epic and Legendary parts for their bots... but those Epics and Legendaries ALWAYS show up in the "premium row" where you'd have to be paying to get the loot. Eeeeh... maybe it's just a coincidence... you know what? No. No it is not.
With how the new update works, the monetary gain from fighting in a high-tier match is the same as fighting in a low-tier match, so seal-clubbing is now going to be the game's meta, as high-level players take all their skills and fancy bots against absolute newbies just starting the game, in order for an easy win and top score in order to get the best loot crate available. Meanwhile, the newbies are getting decimated, and most likely will end up quitting within a few days of trying the game.
I could go on and on forever about how Freejam's devs really, really messed this one up, but I'll cut myself off here for now. Let it be said, the only reason for you to play Robocraft now is... well, actually, I can't think of any. Oh well.

One of the RTS classics alongside C&C & Starcraft, Age of Empires 2 is brought remastered on steam. Now supporting all HD resolutions, reworked terrain, water & building textures/sprites, it definetly looks better than it did a decade ago. Gameplay is left mostly untouched, with the only notable change being a pop cap increase to 500. Multiplayer is handled through steam, meaning (generally) more stable MP, but with the caveat that LAN got removed from this version.
The constant support and existing features makes this a version to get even if you still have your old copy laying around.

I began playing around September 2014, past all the early 2014/2013 things that occured to this game and as such a lot of the system was already in play. The tech tree, the tier system, RP/GC while it may have taken time you could feel a sense of accomplishment moving forward with the TP system, leading one to be able to buy upgrades to improve your bot. Shift forward a bit the game went into a hazzy patch of performance problems, but things slowly got better they introduced a boss system, and the megabots which while it did suck at times Mega's introduced both good and bad scenarios to games. Horrible mega's meant absolute loss in most cases, medics had to wage between healing the team or the mega to survive and as such many hated mega's when they qued up fair game. Shifting forward still the Tech Tree became abolished, tiers were abolished, megas gone, colors we all once had were put behind a paywall, rather than give us basic colors we should of had and instead introduce fancy textures and shades behind a proper paywall, no they took away basic rights of the community most of us had as part of the coloring which was paired to each tiering group before. But things sort of improved, while other things got left behind. Now we have Protoseekers, shotguns, shields, hyperdrives and cloaking devices. What's not to like except the things much of the community really asked for before this stuff should of been implemented, more bug fixes, performance boosts and basic things the community reasonability asked of Freejam[Excluding nonsense of course]. The population of RC used to be a lot lot bigger, but some updates and changes drove players away, for better or for worse and while I can still kind of enjoy it with the loot and currency change (I did get a shotty much quicker like I was astounded) due to the currency change, the rewards just don't give you the same feeling, the progression doesn't give you the same tingly feeling it once did. I did +1 this intially because I do have countless off steam hours and of course my obvious 700+ hours and counting on steam and the fact is if I could give a +1/-1 mixed rating recommendation I would its a mixed bag, but for the most part its very much mixed feelings. Veterans like myself did gain from the old RC just seeing the way its improved and the way it has let many down kind of hurts insides, but don't let the massive negative reviews sway your judgement.
MAKE YOUR OWN JUDGEMENT AND TRY IT, SEE FOR YOURSELF WITH THE FACTS OF HANDS ON EXPERIENCE, I may be not recommending it, but the feelings it once gave me have suddenly shifted negative no matter how hard I try to be like "TIME TO PLAY RC!!!, then it just leaves me empty inside after a match free stuff through loot or not." I feel like many they are trying to mash RC into too much of too many things and its robbing it of the unique dignity it once had.

EDIT: Freejam is attempting to fix it, with much more balanced resell values/better loot, but it still doesn't fix the problem for me. The problem is the seal-clubbing and "overtiering" (yes, it's back in a way) that is occuring in the lower tiers, driving new players away, and the fact that the loot crates control what you can build if you have no Robits.
...this saddens me.
I LOVE this game. Well, LOVED it, that is.
The latest update completely ruined the game. RP were converted into "Robits", which would be fine if prices for everything weren't raised and recycle rates were incredibly low.
Then there's the loot crates. Awful. I used to make at least half a million RP every match. If you do the conversions, Robits are your old RP value divided by 63. You don't get Robits at the end of every match, and have fun trying to make 8000 Robits (500,000/63) every match off of the terrible recycle rates from the parts you get in the Crates. We're talking resell value of around maybe 10%, and for cosmetics it's even lower- LESS THAN 1%.
And then there's the "tier flattening." Freejam attempted to balance out the guns by making each tier have a different "ability" but have the same overall damage, and having everything unlocked from the start. Tier 1 SMG fires really quickly, but is short range and inaccurate, Mega SMG fires slowly but is accurate. But they failed at even doing that- if you do the math, the top tier weapons still do more damage, and that's assuming you hit your target with 100% accuracy on the low tier weapon. They also buffed some of the "specialty" weapons like the missile launcher and Aeroflak cannons- which leads to a huge problem. This change also completely removed the progression- the only thing that you unlock by leveling up now is more CPU.
As the tiers are now gone, Freejam removed Robot Ranking, so matches are now solely based on CPU. Here's where the huge problem comes in- missile launcher + rotor blade is around 300 CPU, meaning a super powerful weapon is being matched up against new players. And that's just one example- a lot of "exploit" bots like this exist now. There's even one as low as 80 CPU- top tier rail combined with lowest tier mech leg. That rail just completely destroys anything at that level.
This update was supposed to bring new players in while retaining veterans. They've accomplished neither. A lot of my friends that were relatively new to the game stopped playing, and I actually got somebody to start playing the day that Epic Loot hit. They hated it.
Premium is now double price, and you can buy some protonium Loot Crates that have a CHANCE of giving you a good item. That's right, no longer do you buy GC as it doesn't exist- you buy Loot Crates which may not even give you what you want. Robocraft isn't fun anymore. It's digital gambling. Terrible recycle rates and scrawny payouts per match, coupled with inflated prices, is pretty much forcing you to buy the Loot Crates, or just "play well." With the current exploit bot situation, though, have fun "playing well" to earn a good Loot Crate. New players pretty much have to pray for a good item in a low tier Crate, just to survive.
That, though, isn't the final nail in the coffin at all. What is? Developer response.
From the Freejam CTO himself, @sebify on Twitter: "Boring reviews on steam by who doesn't accept meta changes. Tiers won't come back, deal with it." If a few players were complaining, that would be one thing, but the entire fanbase is rapidly abandoning ship, turning to other games to get their Robocraft fix. It's apparent now that they just don't care about us. All they want now is money. They've become greedy, and now they're paying the price for it.
Freejam isn't listening any more. They've turned Robocraft from a game with a ton of potential into just another failure.

All in all, I'd say this update really hit RC hard, which is a shame, because I LOVE this game. For now, I've very sadly uninstalled Robocraft. That being said, I hope Freejam will be able to bring RC back to it's former glory.

This game is not for those looking for an easy time.
-Style of Gameplay-  "2D Overhead View Real Time Strategy"
This is a real time strategy game using a semi limited resources concept.  You have a 2D overhead view and can only issue orders in real time.  There are 4 types of resources.  Some of them are almost limitlessly renewable while others become scarce or run out depending on the scenario in question and your allowed level of advancement.
-Graphics-  "Average"
Since this game is a bit older, the graphics are limited.  However, this allows the game to run very smoothly and it can still run at an acceptable resolution without appearing pixelated.
-Historical Context-  "Stone Age to Colonization"
Part of this games concept is building up a country from its very beginnings.  You research from foragers and gatherers up to ships and cannons.  It has fictional and non-fictional based stories from Britain, France, Spain, Rome, Middle East, and Asia throughout these varies time periods.
-Modding- "Good"
This game has a large community of map makers.  It was a popular game of its time.  It also had a nice resurgence after its rerelease on Steam.  Many maps of all kinds are available.
-Shortcomings- "Resources"
Some resources are nearly limitless, some can be supplemented by others, and some units are available that don't require the more specialized resources.  However, this game is still based much on the hoarding of resources.  This can make for a very challenging game, but also a frustrating or boring game.  Your patience and determination will decide.

I've put 2 days of playtime into this game already in little over a month, so I'll put my thoughts out there.
Age of Empires 2 is a magnificent RTS game, my personal favourite. I would reccomend it in a heartbeat however this is of course the steam version, hence I will concerntrate on what the steam version offers, seeing as you could just buy a disc copy off amazon for £5.
First, the multiplayer support. Whilst in its current state it isn't all it could be, it is perfectly fine for matches with friends. No LAN however so this isn't suitible for LAN parties. Before the steam version I'd have never been able to play with most of my firends; now I played numerous matches & had tonnes of fun.
Second, workshop support. This has allowed for some really neat custom maps, scenarios & texture packs. The original game was moddable but this has revived the modding scene for this game, at least for now.
As for the HD part, theres no point in buying it for that. It looks the same for the most part, with some nicer water. To its credit though, it does now support modern screen resolutions which is a big plus. Some people don't like the new textures for farms, cliffs etc, but thanks to steam workshop they can be modded to be like the original or into something new.
There are achievements, records of your playtime & other standard steam accessories. They're nothing special but they don't hinder the game in anyway, and if you like achievements, or knowing how much time you've played the game they are neat functions.
My conclusion: If you're wanting it for LAN gaming, don't bother but otherwise it is very much worth getting.

I've put 2 days of playtime into this game already in little over a month, so I'll put my thoughts out there.
Age of Empires 2 is a magnificent RTS game, my personal favourite. I would reccomend it in a heartbeat however this is of course the steam version, hence I will concerntrate on what the steam version offers, seeing as you could just buy a disc copy off amazon for £5.
First, the multiplayer support. Whilst in its current state it isn't all it could be, it is perfectly fine for matches with friends. No LAN however so this isn't suitible for LAN parties. Before the steam version I'd have never been able to play with most of my firends; now I played numerous matches & had tonnes of fun.
Second, workshop support. This has allowed for some really neat custom maps, scenarios & texture packs. The original game was moddable but this has revived the modding scene for this game, at least for now.
As for the HD part, theres no point in buying it for that. It looks the same for the most part, with some nicer water. To its credit though, it does now support modern screen resolutions which is a big plus. Some people don't like the new textures for farms, cliffs etc, but thanks to steam workshop they can be modded to be like the original or into something new.
There are achievements, records of your playtime & other standard steam accessories. They're nothing special but they don't hinder the game in anyway, and if you like achievements, or knowing how much time you've played the game they are neat functions.
My conclusion: If you're wanting it for LAN gaming, don't bother but otherwise it is very much worth getting.

Kudos to Valve for this classic that is ahead of its time, but somehow resonates with the gamers of its era.

REREVIEW
After giving the game multiple tries again, the game still hasn't improved. The community is very defensive with feedback, often using examples such as 'the developers need to eat' or 'it's not pay to win'. My points were constructive takes on why the game's currency system is inferior to the RP system featured before, and how it would benefit from a revert. While I did get some constructive points made, a lot of it featured strawmanning.
In terms of actual gameplay, the gameplay is relatively decent but littered with bugs, glitches and balance problems. Nanos are extremely broken, able to heal incredibly fast in a burst. This makes dealing with them incredibly annoying when almost every robot on the battlefield can have nanos thanks to the weapon flattening.
As well as the nanos being unbalanced, certain weapons are under powered and almost useless. Protoseekers have no role in the game, other than being a generic laser clone and Aeroflak is ridicolously situational that Missiles just all round do a better job at taking out aircraft.
If people enjoy this game, good for you, but with my honest stance this game is extremely mediocre. Most of the enjoyment from the game is taken out by a loot system ripped out of a typical mobile game as well as a community that while at times can be helpful, in other times can be extremely toxic and hostile to people who voice feedback. This is apparent on the subreddit on forums.
If you're a new player, you should have enjoyment and I do not want this review to taint your experience, but be warned that the developers are incredibly flawed at doing their job, possibly even worse than Wargaming.
Good luck with your game, Freejam, but I still do not approve of your way of handling the community. Make polls regarding Epic Loot and what the community actually feels about it, the weapon flattening and the clans. Do not add features just for the sake, try and get an overall opinion on what people like. If this was a game that was entirely free, it wouldn't be an issue, but people actively pay money for this game, and they feel cheated when you change the overall corse aspect drastically for no apparent raeson.

Adored Portal 1, but Portal 2 is a beautiful and story-rich but essentially badly made game.
Good bits:
- really pretty with lots of details in each area you visit.
- Great voice actors acting out a good story.
Quick list of grievances:
- Stupidly easy with handholding and magic helping mechanics from start to finish.
- One unexplained help is your magical ability to see through walls. Makes zero sense and feels like help only small children or really absentminded people would need.
- A magical help rotates and puts you at the precise middle of each portal you go through (removing all sideways momentum in relation to the portal, so you no longer can fall into and come out of a portal at an angle)
- No exploration allowed since you can only put the portals on pre-assigned spots, of which there are only very few. So essentially there is a straight line path for you to walk on and view the beautiful areas from. Big disappointment.
- All puzzles are trivial because of there being only an extremely limited number of places to put your portals. So few, that to solve any puzzle, you just walk in, look around, and then almost instantly see the solution to them all.
- The physics are broken if you don't want the annoying help. As in it no longer follows basic physics principles of the normal world thereby making some puzzles impossible. Normal physics dictate (like in Portal 1) that speed and angle going in equals you flying out with the same speed and going at the same angle. This is no longer true in Portal 2 since you only ever fly directly out the portals (again, no explanation given why the portals no longer just are two sides of the same hole). In essence this means, that if you have any sideways motion (in relation to the portal) going into a portal, your speed out will be your speed directly towards + your speed sideways to the portal, which just makes no sense.
- So to recap the above: some puzzles are absolutely impossble if you don't let the magical help essentially play the game for you. You are only there to plop down a few portals and then let the game play itself.
- Physics of the world is broken too. You can paint with magical speed reversing paint and put a portal on it, which sounds cool and it should be. But for some reason the portals have a border that you can hit even though logic dictates, that either you hit the ground or you fall through the portal, which is just a hole. But no, you hit a magical invisible border in stead making you just stand there in stead of bouncing up or going through the portal. Again, you need to let the game play itself to avoid this.
TL;DR:
Game has departed from the basic tenent of simply being fun with normal physics since physics no longer follow normal rules. It's so easy as to be trivial and you are not even allowed to explore the otherwise beautiful areas.

Alright, I will start off by admitting.
I am addicted to this game.
And it very much is a good game! The battles are fast and intense and the ability to make your vehicle however you please in order to play the game however you want is a lovely concept. But that's about it for the cream this game provides. Now bear with me while I write down a huge list of the bugs and all aorund terrible features.
-Firstly, wether the game works or not is borderline random, sometimes it will work just fine, other times it flat out doesn't want to start.
-The steam login is broken, sometimes the option is there, other times it is not.
-The game is grindy as♥♥♥♥♥♥ and will require you to pay up in order to get anywhere beyond the first few tiers.
-The gameplay, although fun, feels unrewarding and stale, for two reasons. Firstly, everyone does their own thing, and due to the size of the teams, no matter how well you do it never feels like a great achievment on your part makes a difference in the outcome, and even if it says you got 20 000 of the ingame currency (I am not calling it "Robits", ♥♥♥♥ off) you really only get around 10 000. -Sometimes players will get stuck under the map, and you cannot shoot at them, but they can shoot at you.
-There is hardly any way to combat the new lockon weapons, especially if you are a flyer.
-Freejam, alot of the time, buff things needing a nerf, and nerf things needing a buff.
-They would also much rather add random cosmetics to your vehicles, instead of adding things people care about, like new and interesting maps or new blocks that do anything.
-There are really only two maps with different layouts. "Generic desert" (mars) and "generic snowy mountain" (♥♥♥♥ telling you the name).
-Good and creative builds are not rewarded, and instead the game opts to promote people making the same platform of guns.
-The servers are slow and unresponsive.
And for some of my minor nitpicks.
-Sometimes, if a railgun kills you, the last shot will not display, causing you to randomly explode.
-The layout is confusing.
-The builder feels clumsy and awkward, it's difficult to explain why without you having tried actually good builders in games and then comparing it to this.
And here are some recommendations for what I think could be done in order to fix the game! Yay!
-Fix the multitude of bugs.
-Add a couple of maps, how about a jungle planet? Or an ocean? Maybe even a gas giant? And even if you don't want to add new regions, atleast make the old ones interesting, such as protonium extraction sites, or cities?
-Add flares. So some may have seen military aircraft shoot out little glowing, smoking fireballs, these are flares, and they confuse heat seeking missiles into targetting them instead of the aircraft. This could help balance out the unfair lockon weapons.
-Buff the mediguns. As it stands right now, the mediguns are next to useless in games.
-Clean up the GUI and fine tune the builder.
-Reward people making creative builds, maybe monthly or weekly building contests?
-Stop adding cosmetics... Stop it... There are enough of them right now.
-Give us the money you promise after a game.
But those are just my thoughts, you are completely free to form your own opinions.

The sad truth is that, after nearly 3 years, the current developers of the HD Edition seem incapable of fixing the game's neverending conveyor belt of bugs, glitches and crippling performance issues. The extremely well-received 4.3 patch seemed to finally rectify a lot of these concerns, but now after the release of the latest expansion The African Kingdoms, more or less every problem with the game has made a return in some form, the very worst of all being the downright unacceptable performance issues. Small freezes and hangups occur every few seconds, making the game effectively unplayable.
That said, the original game is an absolute classic, and still the greatest RTS of all time in my opinion. The eclectic mix of exploration, city building and combat is incredibly enjoyable and addictive. It is a great shame that Microsoft has handed over the rights of such a genre-defining masterpiece to a team of developers who are clearly in over their heads.
Avoid the current version at all costs until these problems are corrected, which, if the developers' track record is anything to go by, could take a very long time.

A HD revival of the classic Real-Time Strategy game Age of Empires II: Age of Kings and it's expansion The Conquerors. Originally released 14 years ago during the golden age of Microsoft Game Studios with classics such as Halo, Rise of Nations, Dungeon Siege, Fable etc. Age of Empires II might be the most acclaimed RTS game of all time, with exceptions of maybe Starcraft and Warcraft due to the importance they had in the competetive scene compared to Age of Empires. Age of Empires never were a real successful tournament title but there has always been small communities surviving throughout the years.
The original game is still available in some Retail stores as "classic" branded title, often as a third-party release. I bought a DVD copy a few years ago just for the sake of nostalgia, it featured both the 1997 original Age of Empires and the sequel for 9,99€. Yet I instant-purchased AOE2HD when it arrived on Steam. I would've bought it even if it costed me 29,99€ for the sake of getting it on Steam with workshop support, achievements and higher resolutions.
The HD version does not include Any high-definition textures or effects, as one might expect. The game is rather a High resolution edition, supporting up to multi-monitor resolutions, not that it's recommended on a Strategy game, but still neat. Some people argue that the price is too high and the title is false marketing since the game does not feature any HD changes to the textures. Combine that with the amount of issues some people had upon relaese - and you get quite a few disappointed customers.
This game introduced me to Video Games, Age of Empires (1997) was the first game I ever played, at least that's what I remember. The sequel did play an even bigger role throughout my childhood and even up to this date. A supreme LAN title to play with your friends or on your High-schools computer's. No doubt this is the game I have played the most ever. Which does say quite a lot, I regularly return to play some Single or Multiplayer.
Age of Empires II HD recently recieved it's first expansion - The Forgotten. Which adds 5 new Civilizations, 4 new campaigns, a bunch of more units and upgrades, new custom maps and settings. This is probably what fans wanted with the original HD release, since the expansion costs 9,99€ alone. I am still extremely excited for new official content after such a long time!
If you do not have a personal connection to this game then I suggest checking out some videos and maybe look out for a sale. If I were to install the game from my DVD and gotten the fan created high-res support as well as server hosting service (Voobly, GameRanger), then if I would've tried to play online - I would have gotten my♥♥♥♥♥kicked. I open Steam.
I open it only to boot Paladins.
A simple task, right?
Wrong.
A shiver runs down my spine as Steam updates. The Store opens. I shakily move my mouse over to the Library icon. After a few seconds of me whimpering with the psychological strain, I click gently.
My game list loads up on the left. I drag my mouse with sheer force of will up towards Paladins. Almost there....
But no.
My eye has caught. The game. The digital experience which shall not be named.
Portal 2.
Now I'm stuck. To my horror, my mouse begins the slow descent towards it. I begin to sweat rapidly, trying to regain control of my arm, but it is no use. In a fit of panic, I grab my right arm with my left, attempting to force it upwards, but my left abandons me and joins the traitor arm in its treason. I can hear the mouse click, see the Portal 2 page come up. I now try to leave get up from my seat, but my legs are just as paralyzed with fear as I am.
The mouse hovers over the play button.
It clicks, and Portal 2 boots.
Dang it.
I'd promised myself I wouldn't play it for another 7 years, to forget about it ... but ... now that I'm here on its menu, one little level wouldn't hurt would it?

Stay away from this game. Simply put, the development team (FreeJam) is utterly incompetent. There have been so many points in time where the game could have become significantly better with a few minor changes here and there (primarily related to rebalancing weapons/components or various quality of life changes). Instead, FreeJam ignores those high-impact low-hanging fruit, and instead decides to flip the entire game on its head and release major updates that change everything in a big way. This accomplishes nothing other than introducing a multitude of new problems, while rarely addressing those issues that could have been easily fixed. Sure, during the course of the coming weeks and months, FreeJam will slowly but surely resolve some of the screw-ups they made during their last update, until the game once again gets to that point where it could be great with just a few small changes...but then the cycle repeats itself and as expected, just on the horizon is another game breaking update.
Other major issues with the game:
1) Building/engineering used to be a major component of the game, and high level players used to take pride in their building skills. Nowadays, building skill is hardly worth anything anymore. Any new player can slap something together in 5 minutes and compete toe-to-toe against a bot that took hours to complete. In fact, don't even bother building anything, because within weeks, FreeJam will render your bot utterly useless by breaking it. Either they'll nerf your movement or make various components 10 times heavier, etc. Regardless of how they break it, just be ready to say goodbye to your favorite bots, as they won't be able to perform nearly as well as they once did "because FreeJam said so."
2) Significant weapon imbalances and easy-mode weapons. Simply put, FreeJam rarely gets weapon balance 100% right, or even close to it. In the current state of the game, there are weapons that are grossly overpowered, and there are weapons that are grossly underpowered. There are also weapons that take little to no skill to use, and yet have been high-impact weapons previously (a new patch attempted to address some of these issues, but the jury is still out).
3) FreeJam doesn't care about players who have been around for years, players with thousands of hours in the game, players who have been active and have helped spread the word about the game. They won't listen to your feedback, no matter how good it is or how well-written it is. Instead, FreeJam does its own thing, with a bias towards catering to new players. Basic things that the competitive/veteran community has been requesting for years...still not here. Things like clans have been "on FreeJam's radar" since mid-2014 or earlier - and guess what? Still not implemented, and it is almost mid-2016. The sad part is, by the time FreeJam actually decides to implement clans, all of the top clans in the game will be dead, as all of their veteran members will find better things to do with their time than to play this.
4) Minimal skill required. If you were looking for a game where putting in tons of hours would give you a significant skill advantage over new players, please look elsewhere. FreeJam has stated that they want the game to be more accessible to new players. This might be good for new players, but for anyone who has invested a significant amount of time into the game, it is just a slap in the face.
FreeJam: One step forward, two steps back. Always.

Portal 2 is one of Valve's most recent titles, and is very well made, I think we can all agree. It is the sequel to the critically aclaimed game 'Portal'. Now, Portal has become so popular that I don't believe I need to explain the game's mechanics; it is such a simple concept and yet has been parodied and explained 100s of times across the Internet. Portal 2 expands on why we all loved Portal, with new mechanics, new story, new characters and new settings. The game keeps it's original mix of difficulty and ease to make a title that you can play in almost every mood. Portal 2 has so much replay-ability, that I've played the game 77 hours; beating the single player campaign three times and the Co-Op campaign twice, gaining every achievement. And not once did I get bored of playing, not once did I think 'this is getting boring', as quite a few games would make you feel after 77 hours.
Portal 2 starts out waking the player up an unknown amount of time since the last game. The announcer even breaks, from saying so many '9's, of time that you've been there. After a fairly slow start, you get thrown into testing almost immedietly. Although I'd like to ignore the story for the sake of the review, it helps keep the flow of the game. The story puts together reasons to add new mechanics, instead of just slapping them in and hoping fans overlook it. The game makes sure to keep its ties to Half-Life in secrets hidden around too, which I find really interesting.
Portal 2 does even better than the original game at keeping it puzzle centered. It keeps itself faithful to what Portal built, and made tests that require quick thinking like an action game, as well as thought out and intricate thinking like a puzzle game. Not once does the game hand the player a weapon, which I feel is a good thing. Portal is like Half-Life's puzzle counterpart. You go to HL for action, and Portal for puzzles, which I really like.
Portal 2's Singleplayer mode carries on the story from Portal, as I said. We are given a ton of new tests, with new mechanics such as mobility gels, light surfaces, excursion funnels, but keeping Portal's mechanics such as flinging, momentum and turrets, occasionally mixing them together to make a game worth the label 'created by Valve'. Our original only characters, Chell, GLaDOS
are brought back in Portal 2, each as main characters, still, while bringing on a new main character, Wheatly. His character was made very well, with the perfect voice actor for his lines, the perfect lines for his voice actor, a hilarious personality and more. He was even added into Team Fortress 2 as the Ap-Sap (my favourite sapper). All in all, Portal 2's singleplayer is definitely fun to experience. It's something you can sit down and play in the evening and feel relaxed. A mug of tea, a warm blanket, and some puzzles.
Now, I think I should probably preface this with a disclaimer; I don't dislike Portal 2's Co-Op. I've played it with three friends, and gotten every achievement for it (thank you
,
and
for helping me with all the achievements :3)
I felt, personally, that Co-Op was very shoved in your face and rushed, unfortunately. After how much I enjoyed Portal, when I bought Portal 2 I was hoping for something very similar; more story, more challenges and more of my favourite characters. And, although there are those things, there could be more if it wasn't for Co-Op. We are given two, barely distinguishable robots with 'personalities' that are really just a couple forced quirks given to them. The puzzle aspect is good, they use the two players to make puzzles impossible without teamwork, and, obviously, four portals, getting you across new distances otherwise impossible with one portal gun. However, this is just brought down by the rest of it. GLaDOS is written completely different to how she usually is. Instead of a passive-agressive AI, she is clearly just agressive, which really makes no sense. One of the best things about GLaDOS is that she is terribly passive-agressive, and for whatever reason, in Co-Op that is all just flung off the table, and instead we have a new GLaDOS; one that is just plain agressive, messing with the robots' friendship by saying different things to eachother, exploding them at the end of each course, and generally just being mean. This doesn't fit her at all, and it makes me almost sad to see how they did this.

Good ol' Age of Empires II is back! Or sort of; perhaps not so much the 'good' part, but certainly the 'old' part. Why is that, thou may ask. Well, my friend, thou art exposing the major flaw of this game: it's still almost the same. ALMOST.
Making a port of an old game is not easy; you have to contemplate many aspects: keeping the same gameplay dynamics, but updating them with the features this generation has to offer. For example, this port adds Steamplay for easier matchmaking, rooms, achievements, and - the one that excites me the most - Steam Workshop support, for mods, maps, textures and sounds. Yay, now we can customize our game with a single click! Well, sort of.
Maybe it was a badly stablished development cycle; maybe it was that they rushed the final release before accuratelly testing every detail; or maybe it was they just wanted to fish for money with the pre-sale. Whatever the reason for this, what we have here is an incomplete product. And one can see it when doing what Age of Empires was made for: playing with somebody else, online. It's choppy, laggish, even playing in LAN; sometimes it makes the game rather unplayable. If you ever were into RTS games, you know that you need to have a steady connection to properly react to the events in the game. However, since giving an order will be around 3-5 seconds behind the unit actually carrying out that order, due to the delay, your plans will be destroyed just for losing those seconds. Imagine you get attacked by the enemy or wild animals, and you react quickly enough but your units don't obey right away; you'll end up losing units, resources and time.
There also seems to be some bugs with the Workshop system; unsuscribing doesn't remove the mods. Not even unload them. It's like after you installed them you'll have them forever. And game rooms, even if set to private, will be public to anyone, so if you just want to play with friends you'll have to kick everybody.
Finally, achievements don't work properly. Two weeks since release and they're still bugged. Yesterday I won a bunch of achievements without even meeting the requirements; and trust me, I didn't meet them, I was just playing around with the map editor, and didn't even test the map, and I won the "destroyed 100 buildings in a single fight" achievement; I mean, come on.
I sincerely hope this will get updated, patched and finished in time. Don't get me wrong-- it's a fun game and I love it just as I loved it before. But come on, you can do a better product to meet the expectations. I know you can fix it. Make me proud.
EDIT: The new expansion sucks, stay away from it. No voice dialogs, the edited races are okay I guess but the campaigns are not good enough, and the problems still persist.
EDIT 2: As of today I change my review to recommended because they fixed the multiplayer lag.

The last update (EPIC LOOT)  just ruined the game. The previous update was almost perfect. Was one of my favorite games, now possibly not worth the time.
The Good:
- Possibly one of the best build and fight games out there. Lots of possibilities for robot construction.
- Great players. Can be very punishing if you are new. But ultimately good to help you learn.
- You are forced to bring your A-Game. Good bot construction, good strategy, and good teamwork and planning.
- You have to think on your feet, or you'll be spending most of the time waiting to respawn. Cover, position, speed and stealth mean just as much as skill, bot construction and weapons loadout.
The Bad:
- All weapon, movement and special blocks now cost more relative to previous releases.
- Money was removed in exchange for Robits and you accumulate those at a significantly decreased rate.
- Loot relies heavily on RNG and the loot tables are poor at best. They could be tweaked for better gear to improve rewards, but the way they are now, they're very poor.
- New players will struggle to build up an arsenal that will have them competative with endgame players. Ultimately I think this will stifle entry of new players.
- Ranking system and matching system are broken. Players with very low level (low CPU and poor construction) are getting eaten alive in those matches probably resulting in a very bad experience for them.
- The energy mechanic means you'll be shooting less (probably less load on the servers), but it is a lot less satisfying now than just opening up your entire loadout on an enemy and completely decimating them.
- Oh yeah, and with the slow Robit accumulation, good luck forging that Power Booster you now need to run most of your builds.
The Ugly:
- The "epic loot" you get is anything but. Most of the loot you get, even when you're on a winning streak just maybe a few blocks that you don't need. Once in about maybe 30 games you get a legendary that comes up and even then you need to subscribe to VIP to get that.
Ultimately, spending money on the game isn't worth it at all. You have to put up with the random number generator (RNG) to give you gear. After having bought 12 protonium crates (i had a bit of money left in my account), I got 1 useless legendary, 2 useless epics, aabout 10 rares that I already had and a bunch of blocks that are ultimately wortheless. What I'm saying is that with the current loot tables, even the best crates grant mostly useless loot. Using money is now worthless.
Grinding for gear at such a slow rate will ultimately alienate new players and just frustrate long time supporters like myself. It is unfortunate that the game has reached this state, however, it is fixable.
1) Tweak the loot tables so that the higher quality loot boxes really do give loot that's valueable.
2) Increase the loot table floor so that even losing matches more quickly accumulate robits.
3) You could lower robit prices.
4) Make more decoration/customization items that are valueable or useful in order to increase more real/money purchases.
5) Make visual customizations VIP only or more expensive (many won't agree with me on this, but if you really want to make your bot LOOK kick♥♥♥♥♥ hey shell out a little).
6) Or you could just revert to the old mechanic of credits and GC.
Overall, it's a better game when you're playing with other bots that are designed well. That means giving people a better way to get equipment that's useful. Make it so if you want a beautiful looking bot, cash is necessary.
Hopefully FreeJam will get their act together and either tweak the loot tables, or revert partially to the last update. Still possibly good to play if you have already saved up enough gear to outfit all your bots. But for those of us still building up, it's frustrating.
(edited for spelling, and to confirm that buying protonium crates are mostly useless)

Alright, so I've written a review of this game before, but I was about 4 hours into the game. Now, having played over 250 hours and counting, I still love it.
I don't think you need any more proof; you should have already been hooked from seeing their plethora of trailers up there on the store page, and from what you've heard from, say, everyone who's ever played this game: IT'S GOOD.
Seriously though, it's good. Unbelievably good. One of the best games of our generation. I always say, you could make a puzzle game, but it will still never be as good as either of the portal games. So why even bother?
If you're like me, the community test chamber system will keep you playing daily, for months at a time, constantly designing, tweaking and editing to make your puzzle the best it can be. Not to mention there are some really amazing and fun community test chambers out there, by other players, waiting to be solved.
Now, with all that said... if you're like me, you enjoy modding your game. You like downloading custom maps and enhancements, and designing a lot(a lot) of test chambers that are stored locally. While all this can be done, it isn't... well, easy. Let me put it this way: Portal 2 is a fantastic game, with one of the worst relationships with its own platform that I have ever seen. Seriously. It's incredible how poorly it cooperates with the Steam Workshop, and don't even get me started on how steam cloud deleted every one of my un-published test chambers. (like seriously? if the steam cloud doesn't save your local test chambers, why even have it?)
Along with that, there are countless issues with steam multiplayer and how broken co-op is. 90% of the reproducable bugs I've found have something to do with the game relying on Steam to do the work. and Steam falls short, almost always.
It has its problems. And plenty, at that. Most of them have to do with the workshop, and not the game. But like I said and could not emphasize more, Portal 2 is fantastic, and I'd definitely recommend it to anyone who wants to experience it.

It really is a shame what Freejam did to this. Mark's constant bias towards flying robots definitely made the previous few patches bad with autoaiming noskill weapons that only worked against non-cheese builds, but this? I haven't updated to the "Epic Loot" patch, and certainly don't feel like it, going by what I've seen. Straight to the uninstall bin after this review.
Here's a quick rundown.
-Parts shop is gone, and new players are left to the mercy of RNGesus
if they want decent parts. Anyone who had spent a decent amount of time playing prior to the RP patch already had enough parts to make something worth using in combat, which leads to point two.
-The various tiers between robot ranking, y'know, the tiers that separated players based on their Robot Ranking? It's gone. Once again, this takes a massive, brown, oozing crap all over new players, because their new bots get wasted against a seasoned player with Protoseekers, the OP shotgun, or high-tier rails.
-The CRF now has zero use, quite literally. If you have all the requisite parts, you can "buy" someone's bot for free, and have it assembled with your own parts. Of course, this also brings into question the concept of "buying", seeing as the maker of the bot in question receives part of the money used to buy it. If you're still processing this train of thought, I'll simplify it: Free robots that give the maker almost nothing in return. Combine this with the removal of GC, and you can't even gain premium time off sales anymore. Low level players cant see your high tier bots to prevent them from skipping right to max level, and people in your own level most likely have all the parts to build your robot, so theyll get it for free, or pay very little, meaning almost no income from selling robots.
Once again, Freejam has failed spectacularly with another update. First it was autoaim weapons that did nothing against their intended targets (read: tesseract builds), and now they're turning this into a dumbed-down TF2. Anyone who has stuck around from before the previous two or three patches can abandon ship now. There's no salvation for this game, or the devs who willingly let the vocal minority of foolish players ruin what this once was, and could have been.

It seems it is so bad that only handful of players left, since I am seeing exatly the same names and afker's since yesterday and almost no new players.
What changed and introduced?
Forge?
Reforge values are atrocious. If the prices won’t be fixed, then it is way too grindy to do anything, reforge values are incredible (75%+?). For example, from items that cost 20000 to forge you can only recover 25.
For newbies, I assume, it simply won’t do. As well as for players, who don't already have everything.
They also divided RP/63 to get to Robits balance.
However, if you were smart enough to buy thousands of weapons to reforge them, literally millions of money could be saved. I wasn't.
Crates?
Even with premium I get 3-6 simple blocks from gold/diamond/protonium crates. And some customization trash. And I can’t even recycle it from the crate’ screen.
Oh, since you can recover only a few robits from the crate, even protonium ones, good luck playing thousands of battles to get some weaponry. And only BA/LA battles, TDM gives 1/4 reward of BA/LA or 1/3 of The Pit.
Want to donate to buy 300 crates and get some good items for you bot?
You will only get thousands of simple blocks and very few movement parts and weapons. But, duh, you will can tons of customization dirt.
Newbie-friendly?
Ah yes, simple robot blocks. They are now 10x times more expensive, some newbies cannot even build a normal robot since they do not have enough money even for blocks.
I do not even know how newbies can get into high-tier now, seeing everything is way too expensive even for old players.
So much of a newbie-friendly game. Also, the matchmaking with FJ' fixes.
Matchmaking?
Did I mention that even 500 CPU (sized) bots are still thrown into 1500-1750 CPU battles?
Ah, now I did.
Also many afk's, since being afk and wait till the battle's end is much more profitable than trying to do anything.
Robot-building?
Forget about it, simply place some cubes, just make sure it is not too hollow, some weapons, at least 6 of them, and you are ready to go.
Building does not really matter for a long time.
Of course, there is a meta-builds, but why build it when you can buy it from roboshop?
Obviously, FJ undestands it and now you can buy it for free.
Game-modes?
The Pit is incarnation of killstealing along with ion distorters little bots. Not very interesting.
Team Deathmatch is a good mode still, however, FJ hates this mode and to promote Battle Arena they made severe nerfs to rewarads from TDM, so if you like to play TDM you will never get much money (now you really won't get anything, since you get only one item from the TDM and you can recycle for around 50 robits, while new weapons and modules cost thousands and hundreds of thousands).
Battle Arena/League Arena - gamemodes with highest rewards right now. FJ likes to think they are making game similar to MOBA and promote this gamemodes as hard as they can, reducing rewards from other gamemodes and increasing rewards in BA/LA.
How bad BA/LA?
Small maps, countless campers, in the lattest update you are guaranteed to lose if you have Robocraft's target auditory (10-12 year old kids, from FJ's comment on the official forums) and one or more disconnected people or leavers.
So, if you want to play BA, do not forget that disconnect and wait for two minutes is much faster than try and lose in the battle witch lasts for 15-20 minutes in average.
Weapon rebalance?
High-tier battles became way too boring and low-tier battles are full of shotgunners.
Seriously, a few shots from SMG and you have no energy. And SMG's don't really damage anymore.
Protoseekers, which I disliked, first were changed into close-combat ones, which was much less fun than longranged annoying weaponry, but now they were nefted into dirt and completely pointless to use.
Plasma?
Unless you manage to land the hit into dead center of the robot it is weak and after each strike you can go to make a tea to wait for energy to reload.
Rails?
Oh, somewhat useful, one of two weapons that can damage enemies now. But you have only two shots before you have to wait ~10 seconds to energy to restore.
Ion distorters?
Only weapon of close combat capable of 1-3 shotting any bot. And there are many of glass-cannons on low-cpu battles literally humiliating newbies, who can do nothing against them.
FJ also told that low-tiered weapons will be useful.
They are not, however still being a little better than high-tiered ones. Still bad. And forcing to turn beatuful bot into cactus of small plasmas/smgs is a disgrace.
Modules?
Blink is fun, this much I can tell. One of the best ideas FJ made ever.
Invisility is strictly limited to shotgunners, has some uses for planes and copters, but not much.
Megamodule turned into powerboost is a must in high-tiers, without it there is simply too big delay in weapon' fire.
Disc Shield Module is not really of use now, but I sometimes see someone to use it only to enemy rush through it and kill the DSM' user with ion distorter (shotgun).
Bugs?
One of my friends can’t play, since he is getting white screen/falling underground/crash issues.
He is, obiously, not the only one.
And I got another fps drop, but I am used to it.
Exploits?
FJ removing bonus to players' score when the latter spot the enemy to fix exploits.
I really think it is not a way to fix exploits.
And desync is still not fixed, FJ cannot into fixes, duh.
EAC?
Points 1, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8 are still relevant. They are seriously doing almost nothing.
As for point 2 - I do not see crashes and issues with the game in the last update, but in previous update I could start the game only a few times out of ten, because EAC would simply not start and then the game would crash since EAC is not running.
As for point 3 - now it is hard to understand if it's FJ's fault for optimization or the EAC's, so I can't say anything about it. To be honest, optimization is not very bad, however, there are lag-spikes and sluttering with micro-freezes from time to time.
I am not saying I am quitting, I already have more than 20+ detail each and some robits, so I will stay to see when FJ hits the rock bottom. Seeing this update it shouldn’t be too far away.
However, this update is much worse than I expected and I expected something bad.
I am disappointed in FJ and especially Mark, the latter one could read the forums and not hide in his twitter ignoring any messages that matter and making silly updates which make the game worse.

Portal 2 is a game with a gripping and intense storyline where you must solve puzzles inside a facility known as Aperture Laboratories. During this game puzzles become more difficult as you play and more tools to solve them are added such as various gels, cubes and more. There are four robots you encounter during the story, the first being Wheatley, a core who makes the biggest twist in the whole story happen, the second being GlaDOS, a giant robot who learns many lessons about friendship during the adventure and then two robots who are the opposite of each other, one is small, round and blue (Atlas) whilst the other is tall, thin and orange (P-Body) however these two have a very short appearance in the singleplayer part of the game. There is a multiplayer section on Portal 2 where one of you must be Atlas (person who is hosting) and the other must be P-Body (guest in the game) and you solve puzzles together whilst listening to commentary from GlaDOS. If you are a fan of puzzles and science or even just good storylines then I can guarantee that you will enjoy playing Portal 2.

It used to be good... It used to be really good... Now? It's a piece of trash.
I read all of the most recent reviews, where most the veterans hours rated it negatively, and sadly, I could not agree more. The developers really messed this game up. They ran it straight into the ground, said "Lets make this a more complex! Also add a MOBA mode! Lets screw around with the currency! Oh no! Are planes having a hard time with SMGs? Lets add HOMING ROCKETS and FLAK CANNONS! You know what? F**K IT! ADD AN INSTA-LOCK RAPID FIRING LASER THINGY AND A SHOTGUN! LETS ALSO ADD SOME MOBA BASED ABILITY BLOCKS! WOO HOO! NOW THE GAME IS SO MUCH F**KING BETTER!"
They not only ran it into the ground, but poured hydrochloric acid on it, beat it up with a bat, took a big dump on it, and then threw it into the ocean. I would not be suprised if most of the playerbase has already abandoned the game, but lets take a look back into the golden ages...
There used to be a research tree type of unlocking system, where you could use points you earned from games to unlock the blocks you wanted. There were many different tiers of armors, guns, sheilds, radars, aerofoils, etc. And unltimately, it worked very well. I though it was pretty good.
Then came the Level Unlocking System. You unlocked a new block each time you leveled up. and I said "Ok... they didn't screw it up too bad. It's playable." After all, I was already level 98. However, a little piece of me died that day. It took that special customizable feel away. With the old system, you had to choose what you wanted to upgrade depending on which area you specialized in, you chose the path of your robots design. Now, they just feed you whatever block they have at that level, and it is just not the same.
Moving onto the most modern system... oh wait, I don't even know what it is. They don't even have a tab to cheack what blocks you unlocked!
It used to only be the railgun, SMG, and plasma. That was it. And tbh, I was glad that they added the Nano-Disrupters and Tesla blades. It only made the experience more fun with different types of robots and strategies. The downhill spiral started with the introduction of the Flak Cannon. It was powerful, had an area of effect, and obliterated planes. I was the plane type of guy. I loved to fly around in my Heli-Plane hybrid (gives you the speed and mobility of a plane and the hovering capabilities of a helicopter). SMGs were already a challenge for planes as one hit from a medium-high tier SMG could cripple your vehicle. The arrival of Flak Cannons rendered planes effectively useless, esspecially the slow ones. It didn't get any better from there. Homing rockets definitly did not make the situation any better. Of course there is going to be some where to hide when you are the in the middle of the sky. And the proto seeker is just a joke. What kind of weapon even is that and why would anyone add it to a game. A never miss, auto homing/locking, rapid fire, slightly sub-SMG damage laser. It just doesn't make any sense...
And that is not it. The worst part comes with the new "energy" system. Seriously FreeJam?!?! YOU ARE GOING TO PUT ENERGY USAGE ON GUNS AND LIMIT THEIR FIRE? Hell no! The best part of robocraft was the big battles where people just just continuouly firing at the enemy team. Now, you just can't get that same euphoria from the heat of battle. This is just an example of making things more complicated.
Then they adjusted how plasma cannons work. Instead of firing them all at once with a reload time, they made the firerate like a SMG's and it only shoots one "plasma shell" at a time. WTF!?! It is literally a SMG that shoots plasma projectiles! THIS IS NOT ACCEPTABLE! Plasma cannons are supposed to be shot all at once, demonstrating that powerful blast damage. And it was not overpowered or anything. Others could easily sustain plasma attacks with sheilds...
There are many more mistakes that the devs made (mega boss battles, premium paint, epic loot, maximum loadout, failure to balance weapons, lack of new and cool maps, bad matchmaking, etc) but I have already dragged on too long. Just note, it is not worth the time and effort to play this game anymore. It's just not fun anymore.

Portal 2 is a game with a gripping and intense storyline where you must solve puzzles inside a facility known as Aperture Laboratories. During this game puzzles become more difficult as you play and more tools to solve them are added such as various gels, cubes and more. There are four robots you encounter during the story, the first being Wheatley, a core who makes the biggest twist in the whole story happen, the second being GlaDOS, a giant robot who learns many lessons about friendship during the adventure and then two robots who are the opposite of each other, one is small, round and blue (Atlas) whilst the other is tall, thin and orange (P-Body) however these two have a very short appearance in the singleplayer part of the game. There is a multiplayer section on Portal 2 where one of you must be Atlas (person who is hosting) and the other must be P-Body (guest in the game) and you solve puzzles together whilst listening to commentary from GlaDOS. If you are a fan of puzzles and science or even just good storylines then I can guarantee that you will enjoy playing Portal 2.

Age of Empires 2: HD Edition is a solid comback for the nostalgic strategy gamers and the new ones alike. This wonderful remastered version of the classic title has been catered to perfectly. The gameplay remains the same as it did so over a decade ago, which was important to be left alone; considering the fact it is perfectly balanced. Nostalgia and newcomers are welcome to this awesome strategy game, and for me this is a nostalgic viewpoint.
The graphics have been enhanced on multiple levels. The game engine still runs of the isometric and sprite based visuals, but they have been improved drastically with high resolution sprites and land. The water visuals have been also given a very nice look that is nothing like the old water. It has caustics and waves; reflection and the water looks more natural. One of the biggest perks to this remastered game is the native widescreen support. The older games featured some tolerance for widescreen through special editing; but this game runs flawless on widescreen and on triple monitors.
The gameplay is that of the original one as mentioned; none of the game mechanics or stats have been altered. I believe that this game's stats and mechanics should remain unchanged due to the fact it was made so perfectly.
Another great perk to AOE 2: HD is that multiplayer via internet is much much easier. Steam is used for server hosting; which means less pain for people to play together. In the old times; gamespy arcade was used mostly to play mutliplayer with AOE2. AOE2: HD also uses steam workshop, which is awesome because map uploads and mods can be obtained rather fast since most of them aren't too large in file size.
Conclusion: I don't know how big of a review this game will get from metacritic; but any review that attacks it for adhering to old gameplay style should be ignored. (Ad Hominem) Those people are just new age ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s. (/Ad Hominem) Despite how much people love to look at professional critic reviews; I think this game is amazing even with my appreciation for newer game titles that have broken away from this RTS style.
10/10 (Nostalgia biased)
8/10 (Non-Nostalgia bias)

Portal 2 is a truely unique puzzle action game which makes great use of a portal gun that can form two seperate portals which would allow the player to traverse the levels.
A great sequel to the original Portal game, Portal 2 is a much longer game which features much more complex puzzles and introduces lovable new characters. The voice acting and dialogue in this game is amazingly entertaining and funny, I found myself chuckling multiple time during the game due to the character dialogues! The level design in this game is also great as there were some levels which left me stumped for quite awhile and it took me quite alot of brain power to solve them and that gave me a great feeling after doing so!
This game features a co-operative mode which allows players to play with people in your friend list or complete strangers through match-making. There are some form of customization options such as hats in the co-operative mode that can be unlocked through completing the game. There was supposed to be more customization options available in a shop but it has since been discontinued. Trading is also unavailable which is pretty unfortunate as it would be great for players to exchange or sell cosmetics.
There is also a level creation tool in this game which allow players to create their own Portal 2 levels and share it online with others by uploading it to the workshop! Several interesting extra content includes a portal 2 comic which serves as a prequel to the game and a super 8 (a pretty old movie by now) interactive game demo.
Overall, Portal 2 is a very entertaining game with great puzzles, characters and voice acting. I would give it a 9/10! A must buy if you enjoy action puzzle games!

You're in a room covered in non-portal walls

I finished Portal in two days (one late night, one early morning). As someone who has rarely played anything that isn't an MMORPG or Minecraft, it was overwhelmingly awesome. I'd never come across a game that managed to combine an amazing story arc, awesome graphics, first-person shooter mechanics, AND puzzle levels successfully. Not to mention the totally epic boss battle.
Usually I don't expect too much from sequels, but, based on the awesomeness of the first game and the good things I'd heard about the second one, I had some relatively high expectations of Portal 2. Let me just say that any preconceptions I'd had were blown away.
Maybe I'm not the hardest person to please where games are concerned, but, for all intents and purposes, Portal 2 is the bomb.
Although it had far less cake than the first Portal, the humor was just as good, if not better. I loved the way the tutorial blended perfectly into the storyline of the game without seeming completely invisible. The graphics (which I thought were good in the first Portal) were some of the best I've ever seen. The atmosphere was incredible, even though it changed rapidly; this game has so many moods and settings, from the verdant, overgrown beginning, to the empty, haunted ruins of the old Aperture facility, and finally to the smooth but jilted, futuristic-but-half-destroyed world of Wheatley Laboratories. (Was that a spoiler? Sorry!) The voice acting was perfect; it's a challenge to make two robots convey emotion with limited or no facial expressions, but somehow, Valve's writers did it.
The gameplay was great. Although the tests all consisted of the same mechanics and elements, they were all so different that they didn't seem repetitive at all. Ingame, it ran very smoothly, although it crashed a couple of times when I tried to minimize it.
And then... the story. Ooooh, boy.
What I considered the first Portal's story was more a combination of rich history and a great climax (if you don't count the unseen Doug Rattmann's portion of the plot). This one, though, somehow managed to convey an amazingly rich story with only five characters (Chell, GLaDOS, Wheatley, Cave Johnson, and Caroline - does she even count as a separate character??), one of whom never even speaks. This game has so much heart and feeling, despite the austere, sterile environment.
The boss battle was just as good as the one in the first Portal, if even better. The new mechanics made it a hundred times better than it would have been otherwise. The ending to the first Portal game was poignant, if predictable, but the end of Portal 2 was unexpected, ingenious, and a huge tearjerker. (Hint: Stick around to the end of the credits. Not only is the song hilarious, but the post-credits scene makes the whole ending a thousand times better - or is that worse?)
So, bottom line. Would I recommend this game to a friend?
Heck, yes. I already have. She bought it, and we've spent hours playing the equally amazing co-op mode together.
If you've never played a Valve game, if you've never played a Portal game, if you've heard of it but never gotten around to buying it, if you've played the first Portal game, if you've seen a friend play both games, if you've watched playthroughs of Portal 2 and know everything about it... basically, if you like video games, buy this game. I swear, you won't regret it.
Do I want a Portal 3?
...I don't know. On one hand, another Portal game would never be a bad thing. On the other, this game left off in such a perfect spot... I don't know if I want it to be ruined.

Well, back once again with a new update.
The so called Epic Loot update finally fully removes the tech "tree" once and for all, everything is now is what is called Robits and the shop now allows you to forge any item you wish regardless of one's level, this holds true to items that were locked behind GC as well, everything can now be unlocked through gameplay, with the single exception being to colored blocks which still is a premium feature.
Weapons-
Since tiers are no longer a thing, weapons have been revamped so lower tier weapons deal less damage but fire signficantly faster than their higher tier variants allowing players to mix and match weapons to fit their playstyle.
Armors-
Electroplates have been removed and renamed Electroshields, I personally see no changes made but hey, now you can get the nicer looking GC only shields by playing.
Match making-
Supposedly MM has been changed to take in to account bot CPU usage and player skill.
Airmechs-
Sadly, once again, gets shafted once more. Every block save a scant few gets a 25% health boost. the few includes Rotors, Rudders, Aeroflak, PSK and Ion Distorter. Which the weapons make sense since they boast large health pools already this is made even worse when ground movement blocks such as legs and treads gain a boost on top of the 25% boost. Dev's reasoning for this is "They look tough so they should be tough"
Premium-
Personally while I won't be buying any protonium boxes from the store, however 5$ for the equivalent of 12 top tier victories in crates with crates giving the full 8x items with or without premium sounds alright. I'm sorta on the fence about the increase in price for premium time, however given that it now gives what I'd call a significant boost to gains after a match the increase in price only matches the increase in effect. And really the increase isn't that much from what I recall.
TLDR
Honestly, this update fixes every problem I've complained about previously. This update allows players to fight against similar skill/leve/cpu players without someone down tiering and rolling through with a protoseeker/flak/missile launcher and steamrolling the enemy team, it allows for a greater range of customization and building options, and promotes (one can hope I suppose) the use of more than just the gunbed bot. I mean really, this is the first time in over a year that I feel like the game is finally getting back to its roots and improving.
Edit: After skimming through the recent reviews. It is extremely laughable that people are complaining, saying things that anyone can get a protoseeker and just steamroll lowbies, or its p2w now, or they're now poor.
They think these are new problems or problems caused by the update but lets break it down.
Protoseekers/launchers/flaks, anyone can buy them, sure PSK is a bit more expensive than other low tier weapons but its obtainable and easy to get.
Its not p2w now, its the same level of p2w as it was preupdate. You were able to just buy these items from the shop for GC if you weren't the right level now everyone can buy them regardless of level, and just because someone drops 100$ on the game and grabs a large handful of crates doesn't guarantee they'll be swimming in robits, there is a good chance for them to get cosmetic blocks (the ones which were previously GC only) and which case they're screwed because those blocks are useless ingame and out since they have low cpu usage they sell for next to nothing.
And as for being poor after the update, if you were poor before the update you're poor now. You may want to take the time and go through your lego collection and see what you can sell that you no longer need.

I've been playing this game ever since the original alpha version, and I've left it and then revisited it a couple times now. There was a time when I got bored of it because none of my friends were playing it, but that feeling faded and I came back to it. There was a time when the devs completely destroyed the game: wait times skyrocketed and the battle class mechanic was terrible. I, along with most of my friends, set it down for awhile, but we've since come back. The game has been put back into a place where it should be, and it runs very smoothly, both performance and gameplay mechanics wise. It even runs great on my mid 2012 MacBook Pro, which is surprising. It's awesome that a great game like this can be played on not-so-great gaming machines like mine.

The new Expansion has significantly changed how things work from a progression standpoint.
The core idea (crafting robots from scratch using cubes, weapons and parts) still exists.
They have changed earning the in game form of currency to purchase level specific upgrades to "crates" that drop a random set of parts.
The parts can then be recycled into the in game currency to purchase ANY part regardless of level.
I like the concept of it, because it does level playing field a bit and it keeps you in the game (rather than needing to wait until level 100 to have access all of the parts). One of the implementation issues it brings is it now devalues ALL of the non-epic tiers.
I'm not sure if they've modified their match making to ensure that the higher tier weapons aren't matched against lower tier ones.
It'll be an interesting few weeks.

I really want to like this game but it has so many issues that are trying my paitence. I really enjoy the basic idea of the game: the building of your own battlebot. I like how creative you can be and the amount of different types of constructions that can be made. The combat can be very satisfying, requiring both strategy and tactical awareness besides just being a general shooter.
However, the past several updates have brought with them some major issues. The match making is inherently broken, often resulting in uninteresting games as one team rolls over the other. The new weapons are unfair to newer players as they are extremely powerful and nearly impossible to defend against. I dont hate the idea of having some kind of "super weapons", but only if its done correctly so that it doesn't result in spawn killing of newer players who havent put the necessary 120+ hours in to unlock them. Finally, with each update I find that the game becomes more and more unstable. I used to never have crash issues, now it occurs about once an hour.
While I would love to recomend this game, the amount of issues brought with recent updates has made it that I can no longer do so. The game has such great potential that is being lost due to some major design flaws.

I really wish that I could give this game a good review. Heck, a year ago I would've. Now though, I won't. This really used to be a great game. The only game mode was TDM, and there was no 10 second heal timer. When medics finally came out, they were the only way to get your otherwise stranded robot back on it's feet. It was a time of heroic deaths when you were being pounded an your only choice was to shoot back, not take cover and wait to heal. If you check the reviews, most of the positive ones are crap. They don't say anything. Meanwhile, the negative reviews are written by veterans of this game. People who have been here from the beginning. Below, I've made a list of the current pros and cons of the game at the moment of this review's creation.
Pros:
-Community store to help get better robots/equipment
-Several different gamemodes
-As many garage slots as you want
Cons:
-Creativity keeps getting more and more limited with each update.
-Armored blocks are gone. Health of a robot is now based on it's CPU.
-Most premium colors would be considered basic in other games.
-Veteran players have gotten no RP back from losing armored blocks or their tech tree progress (among other changes).
-Tiny bots can appear in lower tier fights with superior weapons and destroy everyone.
-Medics can make bots practically invincible when healing them.
-Matches are poorly set up. One side can have complete air control, while the other doesn't have a single aircraft or heli.
-Megabot fights where a team of smaller bots would take on a huge bot are gone.
-Homing weapons require no skill at all and kill the fun of the game.
-Leveling up is too easy. In 48 hours of gameplay, you could already be at level 100.
-Strategy has left this game. There is no longer coordination in matches.
As you can see, the cons massively outnumber the pros. Even though this is an early access game, the devs aren't listening at all to the veterans. They listen to the thumbsuckers who can't even try to lead a target or know how to build a good robot. I do not recommend downloading this game. It'll likely keep getting worse and worse.
I also ask the devs to hear the plea of the veteran players. We have been here for a year and a half, yet you still ignore us. If you continue on this path, this game will just end up like so many others. Started out with great potential, but stupid devs and babies messed it up.
