When I first played this game in early 2015 it was amazing! It had a nice tier system, many different blocks to choose from, and plenty of gear to make every vehicle special. As it updated though the tier system was completely redone, now being based on the actual strength of the bot. While that was hard change to get use to it was still for the best. Yet I had to eventually uninstall this game due to a lack of hard-drive space. Later down the line I get a nice 1TB and eventually I reinstall it. Now it has been a few months, but I was fairly good when I had left. I return to it to find complete trash. The game is ruined, the different color and levels of the armor is gone, with only a single low health white block that with premium can be painted. Not only that but the tree now has way less to offer. Though there is a large sum of gear it is mostly an eye sore to stare at and without a high-power of zoom things like plasma launchers are garbage as well. Not only that but there use to be pods you HAD to put somewhere in your bot so it will function. Upon hitting that pod with enough damage it would blow up your whole bot. Now you just have a giant hunk of metal marking to role around with that has the same armor as everyone else. Sure it sounds nice on paper, but it is kind of like communism. Communism is where all wealth is shared, though it sounds good the use of it is actually bad and only hurts countries. Russia use to be one, and they are still recovering from it. Robocraft is taking the same idea, spread the wealth so everyone has it. Yet if it doesn't work in real life than why would it work in such a delicate game like this?
I know I kind of went off on a tanget, but this is one of the games that took the wrong turn and is now a game that is complicated and nasty. All items and blocks white, no levels of armor, tech-tree is very linear, etc. With that said if you lived in 2015 and played this game then yes, it was a definate thumbs up. But this version is not worth the space on my hard-drive. I would NOT recommend this game to anyone. I would wait for games like Crossout to come out or find a better alternitive. (PS, Incase you don't belive me on it being better last year, just look at some of the youtube videos of this game during early 2015 and late 14. It was AMAZING!)

Another big game review from me? Yep.
GRAPHICS:
This game came out the same year as The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim, and graphically kicks it out of the room, even though it was 7 months older. Portal 2 is one of the most graphically impressive games I have played in my entire life. Almost every single texture is unique, and the same can be said with the particle effects. The atmostphere of this game is one to be rivaled with, and puts up a great fight against games even today. 99/100.
SOUND:
The background music, the echo, the silent hum of energy beams, portals, and the entire Aperture Science Facility. I don't even care for ASMR, but the audio in this game is so unbelievably pleasing. The sound engine that is used in this game cannot be matched, in my opinion. 100/100.
GAMEPLAY:
It is the same movement, physics, control, and feel of the original Portal. Nothing to be argued with by anyone. 100/100.
STORY:
While this is typically one of the most criticized parts of any game, I am a sucker for complex stories that never really end, and Portal is filled with that. Similarily to Bioshock, you play after everything big happened, and seek to end it. While that rung true for Portal, Portal 2 is a story of treachary, rise, and fall. It is seen in the "Old Aperture" levels, with Cave Johnson progressively becoming more and more weak. From a bustling businessman, to a mad dying man. Wheatly's rise and fall, and the rise, fall, and rise again of GLaDOS. While not the strongest story, it closes some doors, and opens many others, leading to a lot of speculation and room for fan-created maps. 92/100.
PUZZLES:
Ranging from stupidly easy to difficult, the game is ment to entice you and entertain, and thats what it does. 94/100.
MULTIPLAYER:
I haven't finished it yet, but it is really good, maybe even better puzzles than the singleplayer. 100/100.
PUZZLEBUILDING:
I can only give this 100/100, because it is so versitile and expansive.
OVERALL:
Get this game, play it, have fun. 97.85/100.
EDIT: Just replayed the entire singleplayer in 1 night. Still love this game. Bonus Point: Game actually takes place in Michigan, my home state. New Score: 98.85/100.

I stopped playing this game about 6 months ago. the reason had nothing to do with the game or anything. i just started playing some other games and forgot about this. However today i was bored, opened up my Library and saw Robocraft. Having not played it in a while and remember liking it a lot i decided to see what had changed since it was known to update often. (note that i played the game for 76 hours before today, but it only took an hour more to make me hate it.)
these first things is what changed and made it hard to play.
the "fair" review can be found after.
>Logging in<
What I found right away was shocking. right away it said i leveled up too 80 and unlocked a bunch of things. i found it weird because not only was no where near level 80 when i stopped, but you didn't unlock things by leveling up when i last played.
>interface<
Next i see the entire interface has changed making me have to relearn where everything is.
>tech tree<
once figuring that out i see that the entire tech tree has changed (this is the second time they have done this) and its now a single path. I was a little dissapointed all my work going up a certain path on the tech tree was basically meaningless.
>Robots and building<
next i checked out my robot and was horrified to see that the entire system used to build robots has changed! The game use to use a tier system with diferent level parts for each rank, but that is gone. but even worse is most of the tier parts are gone as well. In the past there was an event where you could get special T5 bright red color blocks. I spent weeks and weeks to buy up as many of those before the event ended. but they are now gone. I did have a large amount of them on my robot so my robot still looked the same, however i found out that if you remove the colored blocks, they go away and you can only replace them with white... COLOR BLOCKS ARE NOW PREMIUM!!!
>combat<
At this point i'm mad but trying to iggnore it. I decide to go do come combat, but that too has completely changed. I use to use a crawling sniper so i took out one of my already made bots and right away noticed that its not working the same. before i had two smaller railgun snipers and one larger sniper. the idea was the more snipers you had, once you took a single shot with the larger sniper, reloading would be faster then with a single sniper. also you could only have one type of shooting weapon at a time. however now you can have 5 different weapons but different size snipers count as different weapons meaning all my old designs and tatics don't work.
>the game<
after just one match the game instantly crashed sending me to desk top...
I don't feel like relearning the game just to have it change yet again in 6 months.
Honestly just for the hastle and wasted time i want to give the game a negative review. but I know i shouldn't just based on personal feelings. BECAUSE THE GAME WILL MAKE IT EASY FOR ME!
[REVIEW}
Honestly the concept is nice and The design aspect and the ability to make the thing you fight with is a really nice idea. but its presented quite poorly. Firstly the tech tree is a straight path and you have to level up to get better gear. while that may not sound bad, the issue comes into play with the match making. its based off of the points of your robot, meaning higher level players could use gear you don't have access too, and easily kill you. they can't use as many parts since better parts cost more robot points, but because there is a creative aspect people easily find a way around it and abuse it often. Not to mention the game is imballanced and favors certain weapons abover others. The game also has been known to COMPLETELY change how it works. this has happened many times, and when it does its like trying to learn how to play the game again. Finally what creative aspect the game does have is burried by the fact that many things including color are blocked by a pay wall. Color use to be something people had access to by diferent tier blocks, but that was removed. and if you do happen to have colored blocks but aren't premium, once you take them off your robot they are gone and become normal white blocks.
I do not recomend this game. It changes to often and isn't fun for new players.

I enjoyed this early on. For the first week of playing -I believe it's now in it's second year on steam- I had great fun zipping around with my friend, drifting about fast cars and making tanks. As a long time high level player, I thought i'd give it a crack and progressed up the tree. I'm at a point where I can build a robot that achieves a league rating, this is what i've discovered over that fairly quick journey.
This is not in any state to be called a game. The dynamics and gameplay have changed too many times, features thrown away and embedded before there can be some sort of established balance. No explanation on basic game mechanics, people at the top end of the game STILL DON'T KNOW THE BASICS OF TOWER CAPTURING. The way armour works is quite frankly a joke, 'triforcing' makes no logical sense where the way to make armour should be through spacing it, not some dodgy way of connecting things that barely even touch -note, I understand how in the game it works, but structurally it's nonsense, as is how weight and balance works-. The render range is pretty poor, the weapons are outright flavour of the month. The mathmaking; got tier 2 weapons? Cool, heres some shotguns on the enemy team that 1 hit you at range.
Sorry, it's just nonsense. The games been out for quite a while now and has no solid gameplay to speak of, as we speak they are completely overhauling the game. I might be back in a year, but I have doubts. Creatively it was fun and interesting till you discover that if you don't have a very specific build or FOTM weapon setup, you're useless.
Skill will still out-do those with 'all the gear and no idea', but you must spend many many hours perfecting robot designs to stand a real chance.
One redeeming factor? It runs great even on my old laptop with a GTX260m. On my main computer, I would like to see them implement some improved graphics options to reward those who can run it, that's after they actually decide how their game is going to work first of course.
Sadly, this is what happens with 'early release' games. It's ruining what could be a fantastic game. But having something so unfinished and untested and with microtransactions? Sad state of the game industry as a whole.

This game has dumbed itself down and filtered itself through so many different variables, that their next update is going to ♥♥♥♥ it all up for us.
No more RP (which they cut, earnings wise by over half unless you can kill off a full team and even then, still receive a whopping 80,000. When weapons cost upwards of a million, each.)
Instead, we'll get "Robits". That sounds promising.
So we'll see, will FreeJam un♥♥♥♥ the ♥♥♥♥ up?
Or will we be forever haunted by shotgun drones and Tesseract fliers that exploit stupidly overpowered bugs.
Who knows?

Portal 2 is a first-person puzzle game developed and published by Valve and released in April 2011. Portal 2 incorporates a campaign that allows you to solve challenging puzzles while treating you to a strong and simple storyline. This review will discuss the campaign, the voice acting, dialogue, and the co-op feature.
Portal 2 features a quality campaign that emphasises creativity through overcoming puzzles and excels in superb voice acting that includes funny humour. You begin the campaign as Chell, a female character holding a portal gun. Chell completes tests using her portal gun while being monitored by AI computer system Glados, voiced by Ellen McLain. Chell completes these tests while listening to Wheatley, a programming core that is voiced by Stephen Merchant, in which he wants to escape the facility. The puzzles are diverse and I do not grasp the notion they are repetitive. They do in fact become more difficult as the game progresses which is due to new things being added to each level that add a new layer of complexity. For instance, some levels feature turrets that can spray bullets at you, which you must destroy before advancing. Portal 2 has a really good ending that ends the story with an amazing final mission that mixes both emotion and intensity. Furthermore, the ending smoothly transitions into the credits that completely alter the atmosphere into a beautiful light hearted finale, complete with a song sung by Glados. Briefly, the single player experience does have some annoying glitches with freezing when pressing R for the feedback prompt and frequent crashing via alt tabbing. These two issues had minimal impact on my experience of the game.
The dialogue enhances the single player component by incorporating witty humour with dialogue that provides excellent characterisation to the characters. For instance, events showcase characters change of heart and provide some emotion to their robot personalities. This creates a juxtaposition of humans and robots because the game reveals human traits of emotion, self-interest for personal gain, and relationships with other individuals within Glados and Wheatley, both whom are robots. The voice acting in Portal 2 complement the strong dialogue because individually, Stephen Merchant delivers a memorable and excellent performance for Wheatley by striking different voice tones that match different situations within the game. Meanwhile, Ellen McLain provides a good voice line to showcase the personality and character of Glados. The dialogue and voice acting immediately created a sense of whose a protagonist and antagonist in the simple story of hero vs. villain.
The co-op element of Portal 2 provides more levels to lengthen the game. These levels add some exciting fresh dynamics to each level because you have to cooperate with your team mate and depend on the other to complete levels. For instance, I had to stand on a button while my friend flew to the other side of the window to retrieve the block in order to complete the level.
Portal 2 is a good and challenging puzzle game that emphasises creativity and excels in the simplicity of telling a story. The story nicely builds to an excellent climax that feels like a satisfying conclusion to the game. The game features beautiful voice acting and some exceptional performances from Merchant and McLain and strongly delivers in the quality of the dialogue. I am new to the puzzle genre so playing Portal 2 felt fresh and different. There are some issues outlined above in the game, but nothing that detracts from the overall experience. At $19.99, I recommend it.
Rating: 8.5/10
- The simple story that ends with an excellent climax.
- Excellent voice acting.
- Very good dialogue.
- The challenging and increasingly complex puzzles.
- Length.
- Annoying glitches with the R feedback prompt in single player and frequent crashes via alt tabbing.

I'll just get this out of the way: I have nowhere near enough time in this game to be an expert at it, but I can do something.
Robocraft is a game where you build robots using blocks, movement parts, armor parts, and weapon parts. You then drive around various maps with either wheels, tracks, skis, insect legs, walkers, hovers, helicopter blades, and wings. Then you fight the opposite team using different weapons: SMG, Plasma, Rail, Aeroflak, Lock On Missile Launchers, Ion Distorters, Proto-Seekers, and Tesla blades (or use Nanos to heal allies). There are also modules to help your battle. The Shield Module, The Jump Module, and the new Ghost module. There are game modes including Team Deathmatch, Battle Mode, and The Pit.
Sounds like fun with various bot types to be built, right? Well, yes, until you go against OP weapons and bots that make no sense. The LOML tracks on to you, how do you get rid of it? The answer is: Go behind a rock and pray or use an overpriced cloaking module. No flares. None. If it goes past you it'll just make a 180 degree turn in half a second right back at you. The Aeroflak is OP too. Shoot at something above the ground, and it explodes doing massive damage with little ability to avoid them. The Ion Distorter is absurd, its a shotgun which deals massive damage close range. What do you do if its point blank? Die. They have multiple projectiles per shot, which means Electroplates do nothing. The weapons arent all that are OP, some bots you go against make no sense whatsoever. Tetraweave bots are made of tetras or prisms, and they divert damage away from other armor blocks due to the fact they aren't touching. This makes no sense as Plasmas explode when hit, so they create a damage bubble on surrounding blocks. Tetraweave forces the blast radius on connected blocks, meaning another row can survive just fine for another hit. They created Aeroflak to combat the armor, but in doing so hindered other high altitude creations.
Freejam also removed game modes and gameplay elements that the community loved. The boss battle mode was a mode where an entire team of bots went against 3 high tier bots in a battle to the death. They also removed the Megabots, massive bots with heavy Mega Smgs or Mega Plasmas, using high tier movement blocks. They removed them with little warning, and in return gave our bots 200 or so more CPU to build with, and allowed Mega Modules a full refund for a week. They failed to realize that many players relied off of their Megabots to make their income, and Medics relied on Megabots to get damaged to make large scores.
They have done good things though. They recently added the ability to have multiple weapon types on one bot. They also added the Battle Mode, a sort of control point based game mode, capture towers to gain buffs and destroy the enemy Protonium reactor to win. They added paint to the game, at the cost of cube tiers. Also, when they removed cube tiers, they just changed to a basic block and no refund was given, meaning people with Megabots with tier 10 armor lost millions upon millions.
In summary, Freejam made a great game gradually worse by adding OP weapons and removing great elements from the game, not to mention embracing the OP bots.
tl;dr Freejam starts with great game and turns it into crap.

Came back from a long hiatus and the game design has changed so drastically that I no longer endorse this game. They had the perfect formula for progression and building strategy, but now it's nowhere near the tier it used to be on.
(TL;DR alert) I've decided to update my review a little further to elaborate on why I don't play anymore. I used to enjoy logging in to play a few casual matches, get some tokens, and have a feeling of progression - but it's kind of lost on me now. The removal of tech tokens changed the 'skill tree' like aspect of natural progression, but the actual gameplay itself is what killed my love for the game.
Originally, the pilot seat was the 'vip' so to say when you were designing a machine. All of the other blocks had to be skillfully placed to prevent the source block under the seat from being destroyed, and also from becoming detached from the rest of the blocks (if a single block connecting a mass of blocks to the pilot seat was destroyed, the mass of blocks was destroyed too). Exploiting this in matches was the most rewarding thing in the game - some robots could withstand volleys of fire with only cosmetic damage, but there were also those with obvious weak spots. Shooting said weak spots and watching 75% of their machine disappear was the highlight of playing a rail gun, or any other weapon for that matter. It was the highlight of the game. The second most rewarding part of this was playing the executioner afterwards; you drive along looking for the remnants of their bot (usually a wheel or two and a pilot seat) to deliver the final blow.
How did this change? The removal of pilot seats and the addition of an 'auto heal' mechanic for downed robots. This absolutely DESTROYED the enjoyment of the game for me. I regularly ended matches with my gunbed functioning at below 15% health, and this was due to having 3 working wheels and a gun left as a result of proper building around the mechanics of how damage was done. Not having any healing reinforced the importance of actually building properly and also the importance for players to have medic bots. The poorly built plasma bombers can no longer be punished - a shot to the weak spot will not destroy 75% of their robot, and in the off chance you ground them they will just automatically heal back up and continue flying.
Completely ignoring the pay to win mechanics and other atrocities that have come in to the game as well, the gameplay itself is sufficient to never play this game again. It used to reward building skill, strategy, and accuracy but now it mostly reinforces mediocrity. I got destroyed all the time when I first started playing, but I did research and learned how to make good machines which eventually allowed me to make variations that would give me usually about 6 kills per game (no respawns when I played)
I honestly don't even mind freemium models much, but I HATE when devs destroy a game which perfectly filled it's own niche. RIP Robocraft.

Portal 2 is a first-person puzzle game developed and published by Valve and released in April 2011. Portal 2 incorporates a campaign that allows you to solve challenging puzzles while treating you to a strong and simple storyline. This review will discuss the campaign, the voice acting, dialogue, and the co-op feature.
Portal 2 features a quality campaign that emphasises creativity through overcoming puzzles and excels in superb voice acting that includes funny humour. You begin the campaign as Chell, a female character holding a portal gun. Chell completes tests using her portal gun while being monitored by AI computer system Glados, voiced by Ellen McLain. Chell completes these tests while listening to Wheatley, a programming core that is voiced by Stephen Merchant, in which he wants to escape the facility. The puzzles are diverse and I do not grasp the notion they are repetitive. They do in fact become more difficult as the game progresses which is due to new things being added to each level that add a new layer of complexity. For instance, some levels feature turrets that can spray bullets at you, which you must destroy before advancing. Portal 2 has a really good ending that ends the story with an amazing final mission that mixes both emotion and intensity. Furthermore, the ending smoothly transitions into the credits that completely alter the atmosphere into a beautiful light hearted finale, complete with a song sung by Glados. Briefly, the single player experience does have some annoying glitches with freezing when pressing R for the feedback prompt and frequent crashing via alt tabbing. These two issues had minimal impact on my experience of the game.
The dialogue enhances the single player component by incorporating witty humour with dialogue that provides excellent characterisation to the characters. For instance, events showcase characters change of heart and provide some emotion to their robot personalities. This creates a juxtaposition of humans and robots because the game reveals human traits of emotion, self-interest for personal gain, and relationships with other individuals within Glados and Wheatley, both whom are robots. The voice acting in Portal 2 complement the strong dialogue because individually, Stephen Merchant delivers a memorable and excellent performance for Wheatley by striking different voice tones that match different situations within the game. Meanwhile, Ellen McLain provides a good voice line to showcase the personality and character of Glados. The dialogue and voice acting immediately created a sense of whose a protagonist and antagonist in the simple story of hero vs. villain.
The co-op element of Portal 2 provides more levels to lengthen the game. These levels add some exciting fresh dynamics to each level because you have to cooperate with your team mate and depend on the other to complete levels. For instance, I had to stand on a button while my friend flew to the other side of the window to retrieve the block in order to complete the level.
Portal 2 is a good and challenging puzzle game that emphasises creativity and excels in the simplicity of telling a story. The story nicely builds to an excellent climax that feels like a satisfying conclusion to the game. The game features beautiful voice acting and some exceptional performances from Merchant and McLain and strongly delivers in the quality of the dialogue. I am new to the puzzle genre so playing Portal 2 felt fresh and different. There are some issues outlined above in the game, but nothing that detracts from the overall experience. At $19.99, I recommend it.
Rating: 8.5/10
- The simple story that ends with an excellent climax.
- Excellent voice acting.
- Very good dialogue.
- The challenging and increasingly complex puzzles.
- Length.
- Annoying glitches with the R feedback prompt in single player and frequent crashes via alt tabbing.

I loved this game when I first started. It was simple yet involving. There were only a few types of weapons and blocks, and this very simplicity is where the genius came from. It all revolved around doing what you could with what you had. You had to build a robot with limited materials and size, and then compete against others. It was a game of skill. Now however, it seems the creators have forgotten what they were so notable for.
The game that robocraft has become revolves around buying other peoples' robots and then farming for more money. They have taken away the skill necessary to build the robot by allowing people to rent or buy premade robots, and they have taken away all of the skill necessary to play by introducing not one but many guns that have autotargeting. Not just that, but they are strong as well, making them a popular choice for players. When everyone else has only to see you for three seconds to be able to hit you with a barrage of missiles from long range, it doesn't leave you many options except to get your own lock-on missiles. On top of all this, Robocraft has fallen to one of the most common afflictions that free to play games suffer from: it is becoming pay-to-win. The prices of weapons is so high compared to the earnings from even a won battle that it gives a strong incentive to buy premium, because you get TWICE as much money as everyone else after a battle. This means you can actually afford the weapons you need to keep up, and rent the robots other people have built for you. Not to mention that there is also a second currency in-game that allows you to BUY robots that others have built, and this currency is bought using irl money.
I don't write reviews, but when I discovered this game it became my immediate new favorite. However, they have turned it into a sad imitation of both what it used to be and what it could have been. Maybe when it is completed, it will be fairer and more balanced, but at the time this is written (with over 170 hours clocked), I am very sad to say that Robocraft is a big disappointment.

11/24/2016 Update:
The forums are correct. This is "the most playable robocraft has been in years". It's also still very very broken. This most recent patch "Fast and Formidible" is a resounding "meh". It fixes >none< of the previous problems introduced by previous patches. "Fast" is still a invisible parking brake griding into your face. "Formidable" is actually fat, slow, and under gunned.
RNG slot machine rewards are still fustrating and tedious, much like the Battle Area mode. You >will not< be getting any of the parts a free form building games critically >needs<.
*Sound and VIsuals are great! They really add much needed environmental depth, and are the single positive to the game itself.
All other aspects of game balance, offense vs defense, match rewards, ect are dismal. That 2014/2015 steam rating of 95%+? Free Jam, You guys earned that.
The "Epic Loot" steam rating of 30%? You guys earned that too, and thats where the current 11/24/2016 build still stands.
Previous Review:
A very interesting, entertaining idea, with almost unbelievebly poor design choices.
A sadly accurate forum description was: "It's like watching a bunch cluless guys burn down my favorite pub."
These design decisions for the last year, expecially that last 4 months or so, have completely gutted the building aspect of what once was a building focused game. The devs decision to make every weapon nearly insta gib removed any sort of depth and flavor Robocraft once had. Additional poorly though out, crudely bolted on mechanics have added nothing but frustration to this now bland, generic FPS.
What was once my favorite game has become a strangely fascinating game development trainwreck in super slow motion. Not recommended for any age group.

This game was probably the most fun game I'd ever played back in 2014 and 2015. It was a nice competitive game and if you weren't that good it was still a nice simulator to mess around with. The game was heading towards a good direction right around the stage where rotor blades came in.
Along with time the developers must have ingored every new idea except ones that would corrupt the game (make it a pay-to-win) and as such the game started becoming worse and worse. One notable change that made the game would be the introduction of "salvage crates." These nearly completely replaced the income of what you earned, and if you did not get what you wanted you could sell it for 1/4 the price and have to go through another 4 battles to hopefully either get what you wanted or have enough to purchase what you want.
Another bad choice was the decision to add these overpowered weapons such as the aeroflak cannon, chin shredder, and the missile launcher which instead of firing missile-like projectiles that would track the target bot and miss if guided too harshly like a real missile would pursue the target vessel until it either hit terrain or would relentlessly circle closely around the bot until it explodes by hitting it.
Matchmaking has also suffered greatly, as there is no CPU cap which, means a 450 CPU robot can be matched with a robot 10 - 20 times its rank. They claim that the "energy" of lower level robots would be higher in these types of rounds, but no one can survive if the bulk of the enemy team is nearly invincible because your pea-shooters cant crack open the defense and you get killed instantly. Good job devs.
Another bad thing about matchmaking is that for players like me who don't have a lot of money to spend on yhis game, you're practically trapped. If you don't have in game cash to buy large robots beacause you can't earn nearly enough from rusted crates you receive, there is no way to level up or get better bots.
All of my creations that were meant to be played in similar environments to their own have completely been ruined because they cannot destroy high level robots, something they were NEVER designed to do and something I never thought would be a problem in matchmaking. Ive seen hundreds of bots on my team get annihilated because they were low CPU. I can't imagine would it must be like for new players, Hopefully the developers were nice enough to actually let them fight each other and not players who are 10x their rank.
I don't understand why the developers don't look at reviews, or at least build off the critisism, especially because the past 6 months has had mixed or negative reviews. Hopefully the developers realize that their matchmaking, shop, and means of getting revenue is annoying or doesn't work, and they will lead the game to a better place.
Keep in mind I've only gone over a tiny portion of the controversial updates or changed made to the game, like the removal of Megabots or the removal of certain gamemodes. For now, I advise that no one plays the game until it has mostly positive recent reviews, but it's your choice.

I really did use to love this game, and the game really went to crap when it got rid of the tiered system.
Back during the old Tier system, there was MANY different ways you could go about building your bot. Whether from using overtiered weapons and paper armor, to a small, fast and deadly vehicle using energy shields to soak up damage, to building a massive tank built to take hits to the hull without any critical damge whilst slowly and steadily rolling over any terrain. You would always know when your vehicle wasn't balenced, due to you hitting the teir cap as soon as you plucked down a few pieces of armor, or a few guns. The teired system gave you a good realistic idea of what are the possible designs you could face, and then plan against.
In the new system, they removed teirs arguing that it allowed for more "creativity". In my personal experience, all it did was essentially remove any possibility of success for creative designs for any non-shield related ship. The only guranteed effecient manner for a ship's effectiveness is to put as much as the highest teired weapon system as you can, with the minimum amount of shield and hull as you can.
As well, while the new "painting blocks" allows you to design your vehicle, it also completely hides any weakspots in your armor. The need to hide weakspots now is entirely uneeded. Ultimately, I feel that the game would have done better if they just simply added a new "Creative" mode granting unlimited amount of blocks place, color, etc. for you to use in suppliment rather than supplanting the entire game in it.
If they ever return to the old teiring system (which I doubt), I would GLADLY change my review.

If you are looking for a simple multiplayer shooter that you can download and begin playing in 5-10 minutes, this game may be a tad too complex for a mindset and requires much more time. Most aspects that I previously complained about before (defeat taxes, grinding, balance and phisics) seem overall better, removing that stupid driver being one of the best.
Though I have been expreiencing some crashes in the AI mode, I highly suggest you at least try the game.

edit: Added developer comment at the bottom.
My previous reviews have always been positive, albeit quite criticising.
After the recent removal of the megabots from the game, i installed it again. In ignorance? With hope?
Or perhaps it was because FreeJam has given me that tiny bit of hope, that they would make robocraft great again.
Unfortunately, with the recent edition of the shotgun, they just completely messed up and lost all of my trust.
Increase of TTK (Time to Kill)? That was a "maybe". Well, TTK is getting lower and lower with each passing day.
Skill should be an important factor! Well, with the addition of 3 guns that really don't require much skill, really doesn't strengthen that comment.
: Introduced to sooth the pain of the players that lacked the skill to deal with drones. (What is shooting me? I don't see it? I'm looking everywhere, except of course above me, because i'm a ground vehicle)
: Yes, this gun is as awesome as it sounds. Lock on and fire, no need to aim as the rockets will find their way to your target,
(or as i call it, the turdgun): On first introduction, it was litteraly a gun that fired crap. It hardly did any damage and was just plain annoying. And you could fire it without your enemy even seeing you, due to the ridiculous range. Just aim in the general direction of your enemy and you would simply hit aim. No skill required.
In the next update, the range was nerfed, but the damage was buffed. "Great" job FreeJam.
Let's talk about the "making robocraft a competitive game" comment that was made. It was most definitely a priority.
- The leveling is now a lot easier. What used to take weeks/months to do, can now be done in 1 week or 1 month. Depending on how much and how often you play.
- There is no more steadily unlocking of items. Meaning, combined with the leveling, new players who reach the end game in no time.
- There are no tutorials in the game, so what you learn you learn by doing, without having any clue what or where to start.
- The removal of the pilot seat: The importance of building a good (and competive bot) is no longer as important anymore. To "balance" this out, FreeJam decided to let your bot die, when it's at 25% health. It could still be functional and combat ready, but that no longer matters.
- Regen: Another "awesome" addition to the game. Because removing a part of this "competitive" game wasn't enough. And likely to make up for that *facepalm* die at 25%, you will heal up if you're not being shot at for 10 seconds.
- Tactical gameplay: Also note the irony in this part. In order to help the megabots (weren't they removed? Yep) move about more easily, about 50%+ of cover on all maps has been removed.
- Ranked: Just because you call a square a ball, doesn't make it a ball. And "ranked" in Robocraft is as much ranked as a pig is a carrot. It doesn't matter what "rank" you have or what "rank" your enemies have, the end result is still the same.
All that matters is win and loss and if you lose, score. Be in the top half of the scoreboard when you lose and you will not lose "rank". There are 5 "ranks". Bronze (1-5), Silver(1-5), Gold(1-5), Diamond(1-5) and Protonium(1-5), with Protonium being the highest.
This is one of the biggest fails FreeJam has made, as far as competitiveness goes. As a bronze player, you can be fighting with and against even Protonium players. The matchmaker doesn't really care (if at all).
Then there's the "ranking up". Just win and you'll rank up. Currently 6 wins in a row, will get you to the next "ranking league".
Combine this with the "awesome" matchmaker and perhaps you will guess that being a high-ranking players doesn't mean anything, there's also no point. Whether you are on the bottom or the top, you'll be playing with the same kind of players. Even new players, who don't even know what to do (yet?)
One little note: The one reason to rank up is to get the league badges. They do look really nice.
Now let's be honest... it can't be all negative, right? No, you are right. They did remove the tiering system and all armor is now the same. This means that artbots are actually viable. They also decreased the cost of the cubes you need to build your bot. AND... they added the paint tool. (4 colors standard, 16 (or was it 12?) with premium).
Secondly, they added the CRF (Community Robot Shop) in which players can upload their own designs and allow other players to buy them. However, the rating system has a big flaw. You can only rate a bot after the first real battle. As such, the ratings mean little to none, just like its ranking system.
Conclusion: Robocraft is turning more and more into a game that you'll play for a while when you are bored. All the promises are basically ideas that can be withdrawn/changed or be completely the opposite.
Would i recommend it? No. Not anymore. Robocraft Developers are basically like a 5 year old kid that has an attention span of a goldfish.
Note: I have over 1000 hours in the game. As such, i do know what i'm talking about. I could boast about my ranking, but whether it's Bronze 0 or Protonium 5, it just doesn't mean a thing.

This is the second time I beat the game. The first time I beat the game was back in 2011 on the PS3. Back then I loved it and it was honestly one of the best gaming experiences I had. Saw the game on summer sale, bought it, and man... This game that now is about 5 years old STILL beats a lot of recent AAA games. It's perfect in every way.
The story is interesting, you don't need to have played the first Portal game to understand what's going on. You actually care about the characters, even yourself (you never speak). And the physics. Oh my god is it on point. The satisfaction from traveling through the air bouncing of a blue gel. Going though portals.
Now there is a downside... ish... Not really a bad thing but I beat the game in 7 hours, which I assume is average. So there is "only" 7 hours of main story play time. Well, depends on if you're better or worse at the game obviously. But there is a little PC exclusive thing in this game that makes up for that. That is Community Levels. And well, they're levels built by the community. That should add a lot of play time. There is also a (not PC exclusive) CO-OP mode! It's neat since the robots you and your friend play as are in the main story aswell, although not actually that important for the story line.
I think you should pick this game up and play it as soon as you can. I love it, a bunch of other people love it, you will love it.

The attack on Pearl Harbor was a surprise, but Japan and the United States had been edging toward war for decades. The United States was particularly unhappy with Japan’s increasingly belligerent attitude toward China. The Japanese government believed that the only way to solve its economic and demographic problems was to expand into its neighbor’s territory and take over its import market; to this end, Japan had declared war on China in 1937. American officials responded to this aggression with a battery of economic sanctions and trade embargoes. They reasoned that without access to money and goods, and especially essential supplies like oil, Japan would have to rein in its expansionism. Instead, the sanctions made the Japanese more determined to stand their ground. During months of negotiations between Tokyo and Washington, D.C., neither side would budge. It seemed that war was inevitable.

This is the second time I beat the game. The first time I beat the game was back in 2011 on the PS3. Back then I loved it and it was honestly one of the best gaming experiences I had. Saw the game on summer sale, bought it, and man... This game that now is about 5 years old STILL beats a lot of recent AAA games. It's perfect in every way.
The story is interesting, you don't need to have played the first Portal game to understand what's going on. You actually care about the characters, even yourself (you never speak). And the physics. Oh my god is it on point. The satisfaction from traveling through the air bouncing of a blue gel. Going though portals.
Now there is a downside... ish... Not really a bad thing but I beat the game in 7 hours, which I assume is average. So there is "only" 7 hours of main story play time. Well, depends on if you're better or worse at the game obviously. But there is a little PC exclusive thing in this game that makes up for that. That is Community Levels. And well, they're levels built by the community. That should add a lot of play time. There is also a (not PC exclusive) CO-OP mode! It's neat since the robots you and your friend play as are in the main story aswell, although not actually that important for the story line.
I think you should pick this game up and play it as soon as you can. I love it, a bunch of other people love it, you will love it.

The attack on Pearl Harbor was a surprise, but Japan and the United States had been edging toward war for decades. The United States was particularly unhappy with Japan’s increasingly belligerent attitude toward China. The Japanese government believed that the only way to solve its economic and demographic problems was to expand into its neighbor’s territory and take over its import market; to this end, Japan had declared war on China in 1937. American officials responded to this aggression with a battery of economic sanctions and trade embargoes. They reasoned that without access to money and goods, and especially essential supplies like oil, Japan would have to rein in its expansionism. Instead, the sanctions made the Japanese more determined to stand their ground. During months of negotiations between Tokyo and Washington, D.C., neither side would budge. It seemed that war was inevitable.

Okay.
So, Portal, Portal is a great classic game. I grew up with this game and I was in love with it the first time I saw its crystal clear graphics and heard its lovely character voicing... this game is awesome. Great graphics, great audio, great storyline, great mechanics, great test chamber creater, great merch, great community, great music, everything about this game is awesome. I cannot stress how worthy of twenty bucks this game is, and with the new sale it's only four dollars. Try Portal or Portal 2 out. For four bucks you have nothing to lose! So do yourself a favor and play this game.
There are only about two bad things in this game. 1: The puzzles start to get slightly hard and you might rage... (like, a lot) and 2: sometimes the puzzles are a bit unclear with what you have to do exactly... but overall this is still a great game.
If you are looking for a first-person shooter that has tons of combat and circles around war, this is not the game for you. But if you are looking for a funny, quirky, unique, and interesting puzzle game then this is definitely for you. 9/10 stars!

I can't recommend this game.  The ONLY positive aspect is how they designed the bot-building, but even that has some major flaws.
Building:  Great at first.  Just snap some Primitive Shapes together like Legos.  Except..... why are the shapes so limited?  It's like they had a good idea, then stopped halfway through.  It doesn't make sense.
Weapons:  Okay, just no.  The weapons really just fall into three catagories: melee crescents (ram the enemy and hope), normal weapons, and pay-to-win weapons.  Melee is pretty much just what I said - a crescent you attach to the front of your bot, ram people, and hope they don't shoot the cresents off before you get to them.  Or kill you while you wait for it to do damage.  Pretty much useless after the initial thrill.  Normal weapons come in sniper, SMG, and grenade-launcher varieties.  Only it doesn't matter, because NONE ofthem have any ♥♥♥♥ing accuracy.  What good is a sniper rifle if you're sitting still, zoom in, take a shot, and the ♥♥♥♥ing shot veers up towards the top-lefthand corner of your screen for no reason?  SMGs are more like shotguns, considering their spread.  Put nine on a single bot and you MIGHT be able to take someone else out.  At close range.  Maybe.  Grenade launchers - calculate arcs and hope the target is going to sit still for you.  About the only thing these are useful for is on flying bots, since shooing DOWN pretty much negates arcs.
And then there's the pay-to-win weapons.  I don't give a♥♥♥♥♥♥what the game says about fair or even matches - once you get above level 30, prepare to never win again unless you want to throw money at the devs.  Pay weapons are overpowered and have homing capabilities.  After all, who wants to do things like aim, when you can pay five bucks and have homing missles or SMGs that never miss?
I understand the devs needed to make money somehow, but this is a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ way to do it.  I would have happily paid $20 for this game, just for the bot-building mechanics alone, if the devs had instead made a variety of types of weapons and ♥♥♥♥ING BALANCED THEM.  Instead you have the most blatant pay-to-win ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t ever.  "Free user?  Not even your sniper is going to be accurate.  Pay user?  Here, you don't even have to aim, just fire randomly in the general direction of a player and automatically win."
Speaking of winning and losing, the matchmaking is a ♥♥♥♥ing joke.  You wait for three, four minutes while it supposedly matches you to a lobby of people on your level, all while flashing some arbitrary "average wait time" number below thirty seconds - just so you feel ♥♥♥♥♥♥ about having to wait so long and start questioning your internet coneection, while other people are supposedly getting into games and lobbies faster than you.  Then it throws you into some ♥♥♥♥ed-up match where all your team seems to be using bots made of maybe twenty blocks total, while half of the other team has three-hundred-block builds, pay-to-win homing missles, and advanced weapons and shields you won't even have access  to for another twenty or thirty levels.
So all in all?  Don't even bother unless you like paying to win.

Alla fine del primo Portal avevamo lasciato la protagonista Chell priva di sensi, mentre veniva trascinata nuovamente all'interno dei laboratori della Aperture Science subito dopo aver sconfitto la malvagia I.A. GLaDOS. In Portal 2, Chell si risveglierà dopo essere stata per molto tempo sospesa in sonno criogenico e troverà i laboratori in stato di completo abbandono.
Aiutata dal maldestro robot Wheatley, Chell cercherà di raggiungere una delle capsule di salvataggio mentre le camere di test del laboratorio cadono letteralmente a pezzi attorno a lei. Proprio quando finalmente Chell e Weathely raggiungono la sala di controllo principale del centro e potrebbero quindi raggiungere la salvezza, la goffaggine del robot causa la riattivazione di GLaDOS, la quale si risveglia con una voglia irrefrenabile di vendicarsi di quella che considera essere la sua "Assassina".
Chell verrà quindi rispedita da GLaDOS nelle camere di test dell centro di ricerca della Aperture per essere sottoposta ad interminabili prove dalla malvagia I.A. fino a quando Chell non resterà uccisa nel tentativo di superare una di queste... Armata della Potal Gun e aiutata da Wheatley, Chell dovrà quindi cercare nuovamente di trovare il modo di sottrarsi al controllo di GLaDOS e fuggire dal centro di ricerca...Non voglio andare oltre a raccontarvi la trama di Portal 2, mi limito solo a dirvi che è ricca di colpi di scena e che ci condurrà anche a scoprire parte del passato della Aperture Science.
Per non ne avesse mai sentito parlare, Portal è un peculiare mix tra puzzle, platform e FPS che nel 2007 ha raccolto un grande numero di premi e il plauso generale della critica. Portal 2 riprende e perfeziona la stessa formula introducendo qualche interessante novità tra gli elementi utilizzabili nel gioco.
Le camere di test che Chell dovrà attraversare sono essenzialmente dei rompicapo che possono essere risolti utilizzando al meglio gli elementi interattivi presenti in ciascuna di esse e ovviamente la Portal Gun, una pistola in grado di sparare due portali, rispettivamente blu e arancione. Entrando in uno di essi Chell uscirà dall'altro conservando la Quantità di moto, permettendo quindi al giocatore di risolvere i puzzle delle camere giocando con le leggi della fisica.
Oltre ai portali Chelli si troverà ad operare con altri elementi interattivi come piattaforme mobili, laser, vari tipi di interruttori, pulsati e ovviamente il Companion Cube, un simpatico cubetto che potrà essere trasportato ed utilizzato per vari scopi, come ad esempio tenere premuti dei pulsati a pressione. Ovviamente non mancheranno le maledette torrette mitragliatrici che cercheranno di ostacolarci e che dovremo eliminare usando il nostro ingegno e gli strumenti a nostra disposizione.
Novità di Portal 2 sono 3 particolari tipi di Gel colorati: Quello blù permetterà di rimbalzare sulla superficie come su di un elastico. Quello rosso accelerà il movimento di Chell permettendole, ad esempio, di prendere la rincorsa per effetturare un lungo salto. Infine quello bianco permetterà di aprire portali su superfici dove a normalità di cose questo non è possibile. Faremo conoscenza con questi gel parte centrale della nostra avventura, quella in cui visiteremo la parte "antica" dei laboratori Aperture, parte che devo dire è stata realizzata con un ottimo gusto Vintage che ci stà a pennello.
Portal 2 abbandona l'atmosfera inquietante che era presente nel primo Portal per affidarsi ad un tono molto più scanzonato grazie a alla presenza di Wheatley (Il Dolce è una Bugia, ma qui il dolce neppure c'è) ma non manca comunque il mistero dietro ai messaggi segreti lasciati dai precedenti soggetti che come Chell che hanno provato a fuggire da GLaDOS e che possono essere rinvenuti esplorando le camere di test. Nel complesso però il gioco ne trova decisamente giovamento risultando essere più leggero e divertente.
Realizzato da Valve con lo stesso Source Engine  usato per Half-Life 2 (i due giochi sono per altro legati nella trama) Portal 2 offre al contempo un ottimo colpo d'occhio ed un frame rate molto altro anche su sistemi non nuovissimi: Sul mio PC ad esempio ha tenuto una media ben superiore ai 180 fps per tutte le 6-7 orette circa che dura la campagna single.
La serie Portal è stata un esperimento veramente riuscito sul come realizzare un ottimo gioco senza dover ricorrere ai classici cliché di genere oramia consolidati e abusati. Al momentio non sembrano esserci novità in merito ad un possibile Portal 3 (probabilmente uscià dopo il fantomatico Half-Life 3 ;-) ), ma mi auguro vivamente di avere un nuovo capitolo di questo splendido gioco in futuro.

EDIT: July '16
TLDR;
Developers initially showed great promise but have lost there way and the game is a shadow of its former self. Technically still is FREE-TO-PLAY but is considerable more grindy for new players and the random loot system including actual gambling real money for 'a chance to win decent gear' is just wrong. Still unique in it's concept but just poorly executed. Worth a look but please don't spend any $ on crates if you must spend $ buy premium.

I'm a veteran player, and Robocraft is just not fun for me anymore. The loss of Tiers, Tech Tree, MEGAS, specialisation is what make the game fun for me. Now it's like a completely different game. But it's still worth a look for a new player.
PROS: You get to build a fighting vehicle from blocks and components and then drive it into battle with other players. Yes, its very cool.
CONS: Random CRATE drop reward system is very unfair for new players. Basically only the best 3 players of the match will have even a chance at decent gear, everyone else gets ****.
Spending real money to buy crates is NO GUARANTEE of getting anything you want. It's a pure GAMBLE. Please try to avoid spending money on crates! It's a trap for people with a gambling problem! You also 'earn' free crates by logging in daily and playing single-player.
The developers have their own agenda, continue to add new, often game breaking content without addressing outstanding bugs, and do not listen to player feedback unless it agrees with them. They also have no problem removing or devaluing paid for content with little or no compensation. Any awards, reviews, videos or player guides you may see dated before April '16 DO NOT represent the game anymore.
Don't fall in love with any particular vehicle you built, or any gameplay mechanic, weapon, feature, function, gamemode, map etc. It might suddenly be nerfed to death or be removed completely with no compensation.
Match making isn't perfect, and you start with very basic items, so you WILL GET PWNED by experienced or crate-lucky players. It's called 'Seal Clubbing'. Prepare to die a lot at first. And remember only the match winners get good crates. So your progress will be slooooow.
Game is ALWAYS buggy - when bugs are fixed, new ones appear. Get used to it.
The physics engine is.. strange.. items like wheels and tracks don't quite behave how they would in the real world and there is an invisible altitude maximum for flyers that makes you loose control in odd ways if you get too high. Being a good player involves learning these quirks and how to work around them.
Devs seem to like making new weapons a lot so weapons always seem unbalanced, there is always some new weapon that everyone loves/hates depending if they have it or not, but remember, todays one-shot kill gun could be tomorrows nerfgun!
SO...
No doubt you have read all the negative reviews of people who have clocked up a few hundred hours: A lot of people are very angry how much this game has changed, because they have invested $$$ or hours of playtime or both, and have seen their progress devalued or destroyed.
But you are a new player: you don't know what your missing out on and have not yet experienced the sense of loss that is 'what Robocraft used to be'. So give it a go, theres still a chance for you to briefly enjoy it before the next big update hits and you become totally disappointed like the rest of the veteran players!

It's been a while since I last played this game and enjoyed it.
Where to start...
I had first heard about this game when my brother and a couple of his friends had been playing it. I started off in the laser-fest that was tier one, and slowly began making my way up the challenging but very fun slope of technology. School starts, and I make two new friends (which are still great friends today) because we all had one thing in common: Robocraft. I got a lot of my other PC gamer friends to join us and we had a blast. The developers were releasing updates fairly frequently, and added my most favorite weapon, the Nanotech Disruptors. The majority of my friends an I were in tier 4-5, and I couldn't wait to get them, since I love playing support. I literally couldn't wait, so I payed $10 to get them and some extra in game money as well. The game kept getting better, and everyone was having a great time. I was in tier 7 right as they added spider legs.
At this point, the game was at its peak.
Not necessarily the peak as in the most enjoyable time, but as in right when it started to go downhill. The updates got more obscure as the game went on, adding in tank treads and other cool new weapons and addons, rebalances etc. However, there was one update that completely crippled this game. What seemed a cool new concept and great way to have fun in the game turned into a huge cluster♥♥♥♥ of people spamming caps in the chat because we weren't defending top lane or that someone kept getting spawnkilled. This was the update that added the new gamemode with the huge mechanical mushroom looking things with gems or whatever the ore was called at the top. I heard about it and was actually decently excited, the game needed a new gamemode. I played about 40 of these matches, and figured out that it was no where near as fun as the risk vs reward of the classic gamemode. Of course, you could sitll play classic, but with this new shiny gamemode about 4 people in each tier were actually playing classic. We (being my friends and I) decided to take a bit of a hiatus from the game, to see how it was doing later in development.
Fast forward half a year or so, I meet a streamer from the Netherlands and a friend at school who have both played recently. The tech tree is essentially gone, all progress has disappeared (including my ten dollars mind you) and they add ♥♥♥♥ing round blocks, to a square based building system. The community gets more toxic, the demographic has completely changed, and was once a life changing game has transformed itself into a monstrous cardboard box of♥♥♥♥♥♥on my doorstep.
In its earlier stages, I would have reccomended this game. Now? Well, lets just say I'd rather play Bad Ratz for 4 hours straight than play this deformed atrocity for an hour. I'm sad that it had to end this way, and wish it would magically revert to its old state. We miss you, old Robocraft.

This game has a very good concept. The way it is put into practice however can be shaky at times. When entering a new tier, where everybody has better weapons than you, makes for very frustrating gameplay. Especially when in higher tiers. Another problem it faces is balancing. In one match, it is entirely possible that a team made up of mostly missile launcher tanks will go up against a team made up of mostly flyers. Of course, the flyers get destroyed. There is nothing you can do. Certain types of vehicles counter others, and often no counters will be in match to destroy a bot that is dominating. The satisfaction you get from having your bot kill an enemy is overshadowed by how many times you lose a game.
I have gone days without winning a single match.
To finish off; yes, it CAN be a very fun game, but balancing is an issue that can make gameplay frustrating.
I do recommend you try it, as Freejam seems to be working very hard to fix balancing issues.

I was in tier 7 right as they added spider legs.
At this point, the game was at its peak.
Not necessarily the peak as in the most enjoyable time, but as in right when it started to go downhill. The updates got more obscure as the game went on, adding in tank treads and other cool new weapons and addons, rebalances etc. However, there was one update that completely crippled this game. So FreeJam are now going around reporting some reviews because they are "abusive". Here's a screenshot:
FreeJam, if you can't take some simple constructive criticism then there is no hope for you or your game. I hope you drown in your money pool.
------------------------------------------------------------------------
New update, new paragraph. I admit, I didn't know what to expect. But I can't say I like it.
Well, the matchmaking issue is fixed, you're more free to build whatever, and for that I thank FreeJam. But what most people don't realise, is that you don't earn Robits from battle. Progression in the game is now completely reliant on the drops in crates, down to complete luck. No skill, just luck. It doesn't matter that you have 20 Protonium Crates, someone out there will unlock something better from a Rusted one. FreeJam, I think I know where the problem is. When you think of a shiny new mechanic, you base the WHOLE GAME off of it. Couldn't we agree that the new crate mechanic would be better added to the meta, and not rewriting it? Because right now, I've advanced more in Singleplayer than in actual battles.
**ORIGINAL POST**
Developers.
Do you not understand what this game is meant to be? I downloaded this game assuming I could build what I wanted and watch it explode in the midst of battle. Things like CPU caps and level progression just stop something that everyone wanted. And now you're getting rid of megabots, meaning the bots we can make are limited. You're getting further and further away from your original plan, and we suggest you turn around. Let us build what we want again!
This doesn't even take into account the god-awful matchmaking, in which a small plane will be matched against giant SMG tanks for no reason, and the terrible weapon balancing, where owning one weapon means you win the game. There needs to be more ways to build an effective bot than just "stick some missiles on it".
Game mechanics have come and gone. I admit, the new battle arena with respawning and protonium towers was a good idea, and I still enjoy it. But I also enjoyed Megaboss mode, a mode where a full team of smaller bots take on a Megabot. I've had instances where I have both won and lost as both sides, but of course FreeJam removed it.
Even further back, we had the tech tree. A sense of progression gave the game purpose, and it was hard yet rewarding work to earn the tech points needed to unlock a new weapon. I was super happy to have unlocked an end game item, but of course the tree wasn't finished. Then they updated the game, granting me access to every item, and completely eliminating this sense of progression from my game.
FreeJam, that is what the game should be. Please, for once in your careers, listen to us.

So I Haven't been able to play this latest update but from what i have seen the game is almost entirely pay 2 win. If you have been playing the game as long as i have then good for you, you now have lots of cash to spend on crates that will allow you to completely do whatever you want. If you're new to Robocraft then the news is a bit more unfortunate. Welcome to the latest in gaming inovation newbies as you are now in a sense gambling your way to a new bot, let's hope you actually manage to create something you like even though you're now forced in a certain direction then having free reign to buy any block like you used to.
A lot of people have used the term "Dated Concept" when referring to how robocraft's old tier system used to work, You level up and spend tech points to breach yourself into that sweet new tier that has an entirely new meta than the old one and etc. It's fairly simple and it worked quite well in my opinion, I always wanted to get to tier 10 and fight against people who had refined skill and bots to match.
Here's the thing i don't like about the term "Dated Concept" while this concept is old and everyone is used to it now that doesn't mean in any way that it was detrimental to Robocraft. If "Dated Concepts" didn't work in gaming then games like Terraria would have failed, it's pixel style in a 2D world is a dated concept and yet most of us would agree that this style is what we enjoyed about it. Robocraft had a style, it's take on the traditional progression system was one that allowed for a great flow of creativity and freedom in build.
You chose your parts and what kind of bot you wanted to be. Somewhere along the way the devs of this game got the impression that because this style was dated it needed to change. When most of us would have just liked some more gamemodes and the new parts.
Lots to read i know but I truly loved this game and i kinda wish i had it back. Don't get me wrong the game still has it's moments though.

Instructions

When it is too thick to stir, transfer to a lightly floured surface and knead for a minute or so until it forms a loose ball. Rinse your mixing bowl out, coat it with canola or grapeseed oil, and add your dough ball back in. Cover with plastic wrap and set in a warm place to rise for about 1 hour, or until doubled in size (see photo).
On a lightly floured surface, roll out the dough into a thin rectangle. Brush with 3 Tbsp melted Earth Balance and top with 1/4 cup sugar and 1/2 - 1 Tbsp cinnamon (to taste).
Starting at one end, tightly roll up the dough and situate seam side down. Then with a serrated knife or a string of floss, cut the dough into 1.5 - 2 inch sections and position in a well-buttered 8x8-inch square or comparable sized round pan (you should have about 10 rolls). Brush with remaining 2 Tbsp Earth Balance (melted) and cover with plastic wrap. Set on top of the oven to let rise again while you preheat oven to 350 degrees F (176 C).
Once the oven is hot, bake rolls for 25-30 minutes or until slightly golden brown. Let cool for a few minutes and then serve immediately.
Optional: Frost with dairy free cream cheese frosting or a simple mixture of 1 cup (112 g) organic powdered sugar and 1-2 Tbsp (15-30 ml) almond milk.

Well, I am going to edit my review. Previously I had given this a thumbs down. After playing an addition 200 huours, I am tentatively changing to thumbs up.
I like this game. I like that I can build my own robot practically any way I want and arm it any way I want.
Pros:
It's fun when you win. REALLY fun.
Build your own creations with which to do battle. You can build cars, tanks, planes, robots, girraffes, balls, boxes, spiders and almost anything else you can think of if you are creative enough. If you build well, you will sruvive and win. If you build poorly, you will have much less success.
Plenty of players so you can always get into a round although wait times can vary from very short to several minutes.
Minimal "grind" if you are premium but substantially less income when playing free.
Teams are a feature.
Cons:
This game has had major changes made to it since I started playing. These changes almost always effect the players who have been playing the longest and worked the hardest to get where they are. This game has been out for years but it still goes under the guise of Early Access. Not too sure what this says about the developers, but the game is fun.
There are bugs and there are cheaters but not enough to completely ruin the game.
At the end of battles you get crates instead of earnings. The crates contain random items which can then be recycled into the game currency. This is still hotly disputed and I personally dislike it.
The game seems continually being tweeked in order to aid incoming players. While this may seem great to those that are new, it creates a game where it is impossible to compete with players of matching exerience.
More maps are needed for Deathmatch mode.
Game physics vs real world physics are hit and miss. This is very beneficial to flyers creating excess advantage to those builds.
The community is very divided between the veterans and the newer players. The vets generally dislike most of the major updates and the new players, not knowing the game play previously, defend the game as if it were the answer to life, the universe and everything (42).
No hosting for players although there is talk of that posiibly coming in future updates.
Yeah, it has it's issues but it is still fun. Just approach with caution before spending much money on it.

You aren't in a premade tank, you build it yourself. It WILL be different from everyone else's. You might choose a hovercraft, or a car, or a plane instead, or something in between. Each option is strong in its own way and each is really fun, not just to build, but to fight, improve, and test.

Played this game since the moment it hit Steam and while it was lacking in features it was pretty fun to tinker and build custom bots and then pvp. The method of picking what you wanted to unlock as you progressed in the game was also very cool, meaning you would have to work to unlock the higher tiered weapons. The match making was also very good as you could only build bots up to a certain strength to compete at certain tiers and it took time to gain ground. If you were good and your team was good you could get pretty far pretty quickly currency wise, making money easily. Being a premium subscriber didn't mean a whole lot at the time as all it did was boost your currency gain after matches. Completely optional.
Now however I've come back to play this game after almost 1/2 a year without touching it, only to find out that it is now a pay to win game and if you're a casual player then you may as well forget about it as gaining access to higher grade weapons went from possible with a moderate time investment, to impossible unless you're a subscriber.
To illustrate this, you can buy some of the weaker tiered guns for pretty cheap, a few thousand of the green currency which amounts to a few games and you can have a decent outfitting of low end gear. New items however cost somewhere in the millions of the green currency, something that is pretty much unobtainable unless you spend real money to aquire them (blue currency). I had enough of the premium currency available to purchase 1 of the new weapons, some homing machinegun thing, and while cool, it was very ineffective as this game requires you to actually use more than just one type of weapon to be effective.
Regardless, I played for a good while until I finally gave up. Matches were only awarding maybe 100k of the green currency on a loss and maybe 200k on a win, maybe, and this was with a complimentary 1 day premium subscription. If I wasn't premium I'd see those values halved or more. No big deal though, just gotta grind more and I to can have the biggest bestest weapons like everyone else.
No big deal until you realize that unless you have the biggest bestest weapons like everyone else, you can't compete and may as well just hang back at the base because you'll get murdered the second you get outside the blue bubble.
Still, even with the obvious pay to win scheme here, the game is fun, and I spent a good portion of my time just building wierd vehicles and bots until I needed to grind more cash to get more parts.
Don't spend the money unless you are looking to blow a weeks paycheck to get all the good stuff. Play the game if you enjoy pvp, robot on robot action and tinkering.

The game mechanics of Portal 1 were already amazing, but in Portal 2 they are even better. Adding the gels adds a whole new element to the game. The way the portals work and the momentum works feels much nicer compared to the first game. The controls are tight and all can be changed.
This game by no means looks realistic. It is a stylized game and it looks beautiful. This is in the same realm as Mirrors Edge or Wind Waker where it is going to be a beautiful game for a long time.
I feel like all I have to say is, it's a Valve game. It uses the amazingly optimized Source engine. On my super budget Radeon HD 7750, I could run this game at 1080p 60fps at max settings. My friend could run this game and the same settings on an HP Pavilion with an APU. If you have a computer from the mid to late 2000s or any sort of APU, Intel HD graphics, or graphics card, you should be able to play this game no problem.
Compared to the first one, Portal 2 focuses more on the comedy and story progression as opposed to the puzzles and difficulty. Don't get me wrong, the puzzles are still great, but they aren't as fleshed out or difficult as the first one. The story is very well made and kept me interested with only a few plot holes. You get to explore old Aperture and the beautiful run down facility. The voice acting couldn't be better and the entire story sticks with the lore set in the first game.
The multiplayer is completely optional but I still highly recommend it. It has a loose story that I have never really followed, but the tests and puzzles are very fun, difficult, and well made for two people. It has so much replay ability due to the steam workshop support where people can post both singleplayer and multiplayer maps. This is a great way to have fun and get mad at your friends for not doing something right.
Do I recommend this game? Yes, yes, 100 times YES! Anyone who doesn't have Portal 2, needs Portal 2.

This game is a fine example of wasted potential.
Everything was fine in the early years, there was variety, there was fairness, there was a GOOD F**KIN GAME. Then they started adding updates that raised a whole lot of suspicion. Firstly, they removed tier 1 wings, balloons, and other types of flight modules. I can only assume they wanted to make sure players understood the game a wee bit better before they went super complicated, but its more likely that they wanted to suck money out of all the people who lost their flying vehicles by paying to get to the stuff they used to have. Over time, the game got worse and worse, player outrage followed, it was only a matter of time before IT happened. and then IT happened, the loot box update, this update ditched the Tech tree for parts in favor of a loot box system that was worse than the tech tree in almost every single way. Player riots followed, protests, petitions, etc. Newbie and Veteran players alike left en masse as the game was now a hollow shell of what it once was. I stayed behind, hoping that they would return to the old ways. I was wrong, the curency system was changed, you were given rewards base on performance (Ie. the better you do, the better your reward) This created a strong sense of Teamwork and assistance between others. Over the course of 1 update, that was gone. I've played video games ever since I was 3 years old, I can remember the first game I ever played (Crash Bandicoot 2 on the PS1) and ive seen some of the best of the best (Ie. Super mario Galaxy) and the lowest of the low (Stuff like The Slaughtering Grounds by Digital Homicide LLC). I went from casual to regular to Hardcore Gamer over the years. I play to win and to have a damn good time doing so. I dont play to get an RNG chest and get worthless crap that is only there to make me even more annoyed than I should be. I wish I could give this game a good review, I WANT to, I want it to go back to the good ol' days.
But that will never happen....

This game has come quite far. Read the short description, it'll tell you.
"Release Date: Jul 8, 2014" That is the steam release date, only. It also existed on a nonsteam, standalone platform prior. It's had it's ups and downs. Meta comes, meta goes. But some things stay the same:
Premium is a fantastic way to boost yourself, but doesn't provide any actual gameplay-altering benefits.
At this point, Premium lets a user set a custom avatar, get double the potential loot from a crate, double your experience gained from matches, and use more paint colors.
After it's release, the Factory is an absoulte crutch.
If one person makes one good bot and advertises the living hell out of it, you will see that exact bot lurking about RC for many updates to come. Even if it falls out of meta or never was actually anything near meta but the player got lucky both in the match and who heard the advertisments.
Moderaters keep chats generally clear (Shoutout to NeoSporinMD, medicating the toxic, festering wound that is enUS chat!), and they generally can answer any question that other players don't answer and one player keeps asking about.
Thruster Sticks never will go away. They simply wont. There will always be that one more thruster stick player that is actually good with it and doesn't use cam-control as a crutch.
LOML is and always will be the absoulte best Air vs Air weapon, with Protoseekers as a close second.
Helicopters shall always fear the rail cannon. Surrender to this fact.
Speaking of surrender, it is customary that the lowest scoring member of your team presses surrender off cooldown and complains intensely about how bad the team is.
If you see a bot using tank treads as a primary mode of movement, you've been blessed by the rare and endangered tank. Heal it and keep it safe.
Today, there was a news blurb indicating Megabots returning to RC. They weren't to my taste, I hate being the tank in games like this,  but I'm okay with it. I used to play this little bathtub with wheels and medibeams just to hide behind one wheel of the mega and keep it fully healed, very easy money back when money was based on how much good you did rather than how good you were compared to your teammates. I predict megabots will be hated just as much as before, but still heavily loved in their return.
Until further notice, anyone who is dumb enough to put a dozen flags, vapor trails, and runner legs on a bot with a ghost module needs to be slapped in the face with a fish, immediately.
