I loved this game when I first started playing. However, every single update will remove things that you like, worked hard for, or spent a lot of time on. This game is progressively becoming more and more marketed. Things that were free are now purchasable, and a lot of things that are purchasable give a distinct advantage. As a free game, you'll get some decent time and enjoyment out of it, especially if you are beginning to play and can't compare it to previous versions.
As is, I check back every month or two and re-install to check things out. Play for an hour or two while remembering how things were funner, or complaining about how certain things could have been done better.  For example, the latest complaint is an "autoheal" feature, where if you sit still you regenerate. The idea is that this keeps you from being left disabled on the battlefield and you play more. What this actually does is change dynamic of the game. You no longer see creative "ejector seats", or "breakaway bots" that continue to function while chunks get blasted off. What you see is giant mega bots ducking behind a rock and healing to full, making them nigh untouchable exept to other mega bots or those that have purchased things. Snipers can no longer cripple flyers for more than a few seconds. Healers aren't as useful now, and the healer damage isn't bumped up to compensate.
That is one example, but every update will add a few new things that frustrate and disappoint you. Prepare for that. Then play it cause it's free, and fun while it's new. Once your spirit finally dies by a thousand cuts, uninstall it triumphantly and see what's on sale.

This is a great game and I am happy to be able to assist in the development by providing feedback. People seem to not realise that this is still and early access and Not even BETA version of the game. It is only natural that there are going to be a few bugs (sometimes fully released games have more than I have encountered in robocraft) and that drastic updates could completely change the gameplay style or even make the progress and builds of the players redundant. This is only natural as this is a rapidly evolving game and is still far from release.
All the negative reviews seem to ignore the previous fact and treat it as a complete game than a game in progress. I understand change might be unwanted by some but it is unrealistic to expect at the current state of the game. The game in general is very enjoyable and creative and even though there can be some balancing issues multiplayer is great (again balance issues are expected in an early access game). Personally I love this game and cannot wait to see how it evovles in the future.

After investing a combination of a few hundred hours into P1 and P2, I can honestly say this is one of the most creative and innovative video games since Half-Life 2 and Unreal. The original concept of Portal was to introduce the havok physics engine and show off its realism. That concept evolved as Portal picked up a huge fan base and resulted in a much larger team who worked on Portal 2.
For those who are into first person shooters, you'll enjoy this game.
For those who enjoy completing puzzles, this is for you.
For the people who dislike using their brain or want something much mindless like Candy Crush or Angry Birds, then dont bother. This game is not hard, it just involves a basic comprehension of physics plus a little trial and error.
If you want a buggier but cheaper game similar to this, play Portal 1. This game is definitely worth the $20 and a no brainer for whenever it goes back on sale.

Portal 2 was an amazing game. One of the best I've played. It is a great brain game, when at the same time, it has a fantastic story, with great animation. It also happens to be very creative. Worth the 20$? Hell yes. Buy it right now.
This game was great. It was detailed, it had a great story line, and it had characters in it that really engage you into it like it's real. However, nothing's perfect. The strongest points of this game would be: The story line, the characters, and the puzzles. The part of the game I disliked the most was Chapter 6 (The Fall), and the beginning 7 (The Reunion). The reason is, I bought this game for more of the puzzle and thinking aspect, however chapters 6 and 7 mainly consisted of rummaging through the sewers of the Aperture lab trying to find portal-able walls. I personally found it just annoying, and was not stretching my brain at all. It was purely frustrating, and on those chapters, I mostly used tutorials. However, even though I disliked this part, it did not ruin the game. Actually, it was pretty frustrating at first when GLaDOS was taken over by Wheatley because I was filled with excitement that I was about to win the game, but boy was I wrong, since that was maybe a third into the game. However, I of course was happy for the game to go on. So, the best parts of the game definitely were the puzzles, or what GLaDOS and Wheatley referred to as "tests," and the worst (but still good) parts were chapter's 6 and 7. Again, this was one of the best video games I've ever played, and I hope we get more from Valve.

So what happened? Well, I can't say nor will I guess whats going on behind the screen on the dev side of things, I can only speak on whats placed in front of me, and whats been given as of late... well, its bad. Bad bad bad bad bad.
Robocraft, for whatever reason, has sold out. No more earning cash to slowly build up your masterpiece, no more clear and consice systems to work with, and worst of all, very limited creative freedom for god knows how long thanks to the RNG you now need to count on to make any form of progress. "But what about the forge?" I can hear asked. "The forge can allow you to pick and chose your parts rather then relying on a loot crate system worse then CSGO's." Well, sure, but like I said, you would still be hard at work for a good, long time. The payment you get via breaking down blocks will always be less (much, much less) then what they are worth. You, assumedly, could just farm loot boxes to build up on actual parts rather then being robbed, but due to that being a luck-based system it could still take a long time. Possibly (probably) many many many times longer then building up cash via deconstructing blocks in the forge.
Of course, you could just pay.
Or be grandfathered in via having had a fortune back in the earlier days like I was, yet still here I am, writing this.
Or, of course, just turn away.
I'm probably still going to poke my head in now and then. I do have some fond memories. I don't really have the means to try anything new that might come with time and THAT is what really is the final nail in the coffin for me (going back to the very limited creative freedom) but, I dunno. memories, I guess.

It's a brilliant game, although I'd recommend playing the first game first (obviously), and as a result this review will refer back to the first game here and there.
So, lets get into the review.
The general concept of the game is the same. Shoot portals to get from point A to point B, solving numerous test chambers. Except the gameplay is so much more than that.
This game takes place a while after the events of Portal, and the atmosphere reflects that. Aperture Science is beatifully torn apart and far from the state of the facility in the first game.
Apon starting the game, you are introduced to a brand new character. I wont spoil anything, but I'll just say that from the get-go, the writing in this game is astounding, a mix of so much comedy with somewhat sinister undertones which is backed up further by spot-on voice acting. But, new faces aside, you'll quickly be introduced to a familiar voice, one that fills players of the first game with glee and terror! And the emotions stirred by these characters are maintained throughout Portal 2.
So, you may be thinking; "Great, it's Portal, it still has good writing... what's new?"
Well I'm glad you asked. On top of graphical improvements galore, the gameplay has some nice additions. You still have the staple of the series, the Aperture Science Handheld Portal Device, but as the game progresses you'll be introduced to completely new puzzle elements, that meld so well with the flow of the game. Again I shant spoil them, but trust me, they're great.
Also new to the game is Co-Op! Here you and a friend can take control of a robot, solving puzzles that Chell alone could not. Each of you is armed with a Portal Gun, equalling a total of 4 portals. What's great about this is that the Co-Op has it's own story that, while set after the main Solo story, is completely seperate and has it's fair share of hilarious dialogue.
In addition, you can access the Community Tests, homebrewed puzzles from Portal 2 players across the world. You can play those Community Maps, or make your own and publish them!
The only major critisicm I have is that once you clear the main story, it's wasy to completely remember all of the puzzles, making replay value pretty low. Luckily. it seems Valve thought of this, so thre's plenty of achievements for you to hunt and a butt-tonne of easter eggs! So whilst the story may be easy the second time around, there's still stuff to do!
So to conclude, this game is a fantastic first person puzzle game, so much better than it's predecessor (which was still amazing!)
It struggles a bit in the replay aspect, but community maps and a plethora of secrets should keep you going for hours. Again, the characters, dialogue and voice acting are fabulous, the humour is high-brow and the overall experience just sucks you into the world of Portal. I would gladly rate this game 9/10, However, to reiterate I highly suggest you play the first game before this one, both for context and pleasure!

Have been playing this game for a year or more (have almost 800 hours) and through its many changes it has stayed my go to game for casual fps.
Originally it tried to be world of tanks where you make your own tank (personally i never thought it was that bad) which made it pretty hard to get blocks (you pay in-game or realz credits for every block) as you pretty much only had a positive income on mid tier games and had to suppliment your higher tiers with many mid tier games.
After alot of mucking around the devs decided to make repairs free which freed players up to make rediculous bots and rediculous credits.
After the introduction of megas it pretty much turned into a mega on mega game with a team of support players (which i also didnt mind ex. i made 6 mill credits one match) but got to be boring after a few weeks.
Then they turned it into a moba with a deathmatch mode (everyone played the moba mode pretty much) this was interesting but a problem ( not yet resolved ) is a match use to take around 5 mins. With this mode it takes upwards of 10-15 ( and people still can't figure out how to capture a tower ex. shoot where the protrusions are )
In its current state they have rankings, moba, and deathmatch modes with a new tier system that unlocks on lvl vs. the player unlocking specific items. There is no longer a robot driving so a bot now dies when a percentage of its blocks are gone vs. shooting the blocks around the robot. There are new weapons that i never would have amagined happening ( flak guns, homing missiles, and tesla coils i still consider crazy (you hit people and they do damge) ). Its a little imbalanced in that one player has a hard time making up for a team and basicilly the first min of a game can decide its outcome ( only talking about moba mode ). Still dont think they ever needed any kind of healing but maybe made it unfair. Now there is auto heal where if you dont shoot or get shot for 15 secs ( or so... ) your bot heals.
Its a much different game then it was but its still worth trying.

Hmm... Lots of negative reviews while I'm scrolling down... (I have 200 hours, just hear me out from the crowd of negatives, please?)
To be honest, I like the new meta. The new game. Sure, the tiers were an accomplishment and it was fun (kind of...) to go up them. Yes, players were enraged when the they discovered the ranking of their robot had changed. Yes, they were furious when the tech tree was revamped. Yes, they were as angry as the underworld when they discovered almost everything they loved and desired before had changed...
And yes, don't get me wrong, I am slightly upset at the devs too for some of the... rather random updates (aeroflak and missiles?).
But the game has changed. For the better? For the worse? I don't know. We'll find out, won't we? We've taken sides for now, but know this. If you do not change to play the game... If you vehemently deny that the meta has brought anything good... If you... if you never want to try this game... then you will never enjoy it.
I was a low level player when the meta changed. Maybe that's why I adapted to it. Listen, high tier people. I'm sorry that it seemed that all that grinding went for nothing. But... I think the updates have brought some nice things to the game that will make some of the newer players happy.
First thing's first. The tech tree. Yes, it isn't a tree anymore, but it is a whole less complicated. I never really understood the point of having only 5 models but 10 tiers... It was pretty confusing. I feel, by condensing each part from 2 tiers into 1, it has made things much simpler to use. What was the difference between thrusters, only one tier apart? One of them had a fin and an orange symbol on it. I guess there was some difference? I never noticed the power... but if you compare the thruster Puma and the thruster Cheetah, you see there's something... just something that calls out to you. Another example. There's now only 1 helium block vs... how many there were before. A lot simpler to use, in my opinon.
A major part of the tech tree was the tiers of the armor blocks.
"Just... why?" I always asked myself. Everytime I leveled up, I would have to go back and buy more and rebuild my tank with the new, higher tier armor cubes if I wanted to stand a chance. Now? There's just one, and its calibrated on your robots rank. It's a whole lot simpler, I tell you...
Also, just my personal opinion, the removal of the look of the old blocks and the replacement with the new makes the game look much more refined. That's just me, though.
The pilot seat... yes, that was a major change. But, it gives the creator... the builder... you, much more oppurtunities. You don't have to constantly worry about electroshielding that small area. You don't have to constantly worry about railgun snipers finding out the position of where that seat was. Although, admittedly, I do sometimes miss the thought of the "ejector seat," I feel that without the pilot seat (looked cool, by the way), players have much more freedom with what they can build.
Glass? Premium GC? Yea, it sucks.
The CRF. You can now buy robots there, and if you see any in single player that look interesting, look it up in the shop! It's nice compared to the same old same old robots you fight all the time that Freejam supplies.
Listen... I know that the game has changed. Maybe for the worse in your opinion. But let me tell you. Try it. Not for one second and then quit. Try it again. Try as a new player if you want to restart your experience. A lot of things have changed. Time isn't going to reverse.
Try the game and embrace the changes. Maybe you'll like it.

Robocraft is an early access game where you build your own robots in your garage.
You will build your insane robot, test it and eventually fight with it in battles.
I've played this game for a while, and at some point they changed the whole tier-system.. which is in my opinion both interesting as well as kind of sad.
Basically you would start with your white blocks which were the lowest ranking of all blocks, you earned tech points which you could use to unlock other kinds of blocks, they changed it so you unlock blocks by leveling - which is great.
They also changed the block types, so that the main blocks are all the same rank but can be colored. Which wasn't possible before, because for example a orange block had a different ranking compared to a red block.
This made building quite interesting compared to today - where you have to place blocks in a different way to reinforce them against stronger robots.
Even though at first I thought it was a stupid thing, I do - these days - still like to play Robocraft, and I adapted to the new system.
So that's the history I got to tell you..
In general Robocraft is an amazing game.
- Building robots and improving them is a really fun part of the game, and eventually when you enter a battle (the waiting time is really short most times) you will feel great when you are able to destroy every other robot in your way.
There are different builds popular from time to time, so one week you see a lot of flyers and you can make a AA-robot, the other week they are building something completely different!
- The battles are interesting as well, you can choose between team deathmatch, the Pit (which is FFA), and Battle Mode.
There is also a ranked mode, but the game mode is the same as Battle Mode - but it's called Battle Arena.
- There is a variety of weapons you can use, for example - SMG's, Rail cannons, Plasma cannons, Medic guns, Aeroflaks, Missle launchers. - and the last two have been added recently, so I am expecting more to come.
However, even though the game has it's cool features there are also some things they need to improve..
I will name some of the things I think need to improve, and I found someone on the internet who uses the username
who also started a topic about this some time ago.
I will copy some of hes ideas:

I totally agree with this guy, there is a great way to impove the game by adding a post game lobby/chat.
This way, people can interact with each other. For example I could compliment someone because they have a really cool robot, or congratulate the enemy team for winning.

Almost everything you see in the trailer and promotional images can only be bought with premium currency. For example, you know that really cool rainbow shark in the trailer? A grand total of 4 colors are avalible in game, 2 of which are grey and white. However, these are purley asthetic. But some things like the rhino head (also premium only) give you slight advantages in battle. I might also add the the complete rhino head is broken into multiple parts, so you will have to buy ALL of them with premium currency if you want it to look presentable. The game's combat itself is alright, the way you blow off bits of the opponent's robot-mech-thingy is satisfying, and could even allow for some strategizing, with targeting the opponent's weapons in an attempt to disarm them before finishing them off. This could be cool if it were not for the fact that the only weapons you have at the beggining are a sort of grenade launcher that goes all over the place and a blaster that makes the scattergun look like a precision rifle. Of course, I looked and saw that there are more accurate weapons in the game, but you either have to play for several hours or pay premium to get them. Finally, the game is poorly balenced. For example, the only robots really worth using are the flying robots, which are not unlocked immediatley (fortunatley they don't take long to get). And the people using the flyers have good reason to. The things zip around FAST. You know those awesome walkers in the trailer? Almost useless when there's a 3-inch drone zooming around your head firing a constant stream of lasers at you. The game seems to run smooth,  the building system is OKAY, assuming you have enough blocks at your disposal, and overall I have ran into very few glitches (although the one I did find required me to quit a match halfway through). However, my brief expirence with this game leads me to believe that this is just another cash-grab f2p mech game. Perhaps if they gave you more stuff to start with and did away with the premium currency it could be alright, but until then, I reccomend you give this one a pass.

Potentially brilliant game.  Done all the hard work then failed on the easy bits.
By the easy bit I mean the game modes - once you die, you're dead for good.  You have to quit and reload.... and that takes a long time!!  Most games have some game modes where death is permanent, but usually games allow you to respawn fairly quickly.  This doesn't.
So from the start:  First you have to wait for the game itself to load.  Then you have to log in and wait for all your stuff to load.  Then you have to wait for the robot build/select environment to load.  Then click start, and wait for it to find suitable matches.  Then wait for it to load all the players in.  Then wait for the actual map / game environment to load.  Finally we're here!!  Nope, not yet.  After all that waiting, for some reason you now have a 15 second count down.  What the purpose of this is other than to frustrate you I have no idea!  You're all ready to go, everything is loaded (finally!), all the players are ready, but no you have to wait for this 15 second countdown to finish.  You can't even adjust your zoom during this time, you can't do anything, just sit there looking round.  OK its only 15 seconds but on top of all the other loading, and the fact that after you have to go through this process so frequently, it gets annoying.
What exacerbates this problem, is that you can't change any settings or reconfigure the controls once you've started playing.  So any time you need to make any changes, or if you change something and decide you don't like it, you have to quit and go through the whole long loading process all over again.  Even worse, there is a bug that if you want to use a gamepad it doesn't remember the settings when you close the game, so you have to remember every time you start it up to reconfigure your keys.  And if you forget?  Yup, back to the painfully long loading process.
Incidentally it's worth mentioning I was trying to use the gamepad to help with the horrible steering of the bots.  If you want to use anything with wheels not legs, the steering is terrible.  So I tried the analogue stick on my gamepad thinking that might make it better, but it's not implemented correctly.  If you push the analogue stick only slightly your wheels will still go all the way over to full lock (albeit slightly slower than normal) which defeats the whole point of analogue controls.

I love and hate this game, it’s very mixed but I would still recommend it.
Pros:
*Sandbox construction of your robot. Literally if you can think of it, u can make it and put guns on it, u don’t even need to make it move if u don’t want to.
*Everything is unlockable without any real life money.
*You can play for 10 minutes and feel you accomplished something.
*Don’t like pvp? No problem, you can chill in single player and kill AI all day with no stress and still get points and level up.
Cons:
*Uneven matching: because of the way the game calculates the score of your robot, it is really unfair many times when matching with others. So you may load into a match and find urself one shotted by someone taking advantage of this imbalance.
*Too limited build options: Early game, u have limits on ur construction, which is fair, but the limits are too strict. They simply don’t give you enough wiggle room to make the cool thing u have in ur mind, so you have to go out and grind to level up just to add one more block to your robot.
*Repetitive: This is the game(Build bot, join match, tweak bot, repeat). That’s it, no joke...
Suggestions to the developer:
What this game needs desperately are, Armored core styled, single and multiplayer missions that have a story behind them and allow players to complete objectives together or alone for rewards and achievements.

Before I start ranting about the annoying amount of stupid features, let me point out - I DON'T need to play it for hours and hours to write a meaningful review. And, I'm not trying to hate the devs.
First off - FAKE LOAD TIMES. Who likes FAKE LOAD TIMES?! You leave a battle early and you get penalized. That's absurd. I've never seen ANY team-based or FFA games that do that... That's absolutely absurd and infuriating.
Secondly - 'Matching you "FAIRLY" with other robots.' Have you seen what new players undergo in their first matches? You almost NEVER win. This is ANOTHER fake load time when it says 'matching you fairly'. It doesn't even MATCH you. I'm always on a team where everyone builds stupid useless bots and the other team has almost ALL of the end-game stuff. Just stupid. It should be if you're a level 1, you're being matched with lvl1s and lvl2s. THAT's being fair. Later in the game once you get some good stuff, maybe it's not as simple with matching. But at LEAST balance the earlygame. Please... Make the earlygame enjoyable.
Another reason I'm downvoting this - some of the stupid agility glitches. Most of the time I can't even really turn my bots. Lastly, about this free2play thing. Sure it's free2play. One thing you should note - whenever you see Free2Play games, most of the time, it's PAY2WIN. So, overall: Free2Play, Free2Lose, Pay2Win. That basically sums up every F2P game in a nutshell. The company name 'Freejam?' how about 'the next generation of moneyclip.' Seriously...
Overall: I rate this 3/10, needs a LOT of work to be done, among a bunch of other stuff. The devs dont seem to care at all about the community. Read the early access game part of the store page... Wow, lies. They don't jam with you, they don't keep it free. They make it pay2win and they just kill off the userbase. It's also not polished whatsoever AT ALL. Waste of time, a disappointing reminder that free2play games and most early access games are disappointing games by companies who only care about money and don't care about the community... :( Don't waste your time on this game.

Don't get me wrong; this is a great game, but has many flaws which ruin the casual gamer's gameplay. To start, it's a huge pay to win game, with microtransactions to quickly unlock the best weapons. This leads to a huge imbalance in the game, with people who have paid with missile launchers and anti-air turrets, while the rest only have the base weapons to flail around with. The different vehicles lead to different games everytime, however; the majority of the players use scarab designs with the insect legs to get to annoying places and camp. Using an air vehicle is suicide, the missile launchers spot you five seconds after your spawn, and if you avoid those, a guy in a heavily armored block with an anti-aircraft turret wipes you out before you can regenerate. This severe imbalance leads to un-fun gameplay - and for the average player, hours of grinding to get vehicles anywhere near as good as the pay-to-win players - with the added bonus of being hassled to buy GC (galaxy cash) or premium. This game HAD a lot of promise, but it seems like they abandoned the fair-teambased gameplay and instead turned to pay-to-win money grabbing gameplay seen on mobile devices. In conclusion; unless you plan on spending £50 on galaxy cash and premium, don't bother starting...

Portal 2 is a first-person perspective puzzle game. The Player takes the role of Chell in the single-player campaign, as one of two robots—Atlas and P-Body—in the cooperative campaign, or as a simplistic humanoid icon in community-developed puzzles. These four characters can explore and interact with the environment. Characters can withstand limited damage but will die after sustained injury. There is no penalty for falling onto a solid surface, but falling into bottomless pits or toxic pools kills the player character immediately. When Chell dies in the single-player game, the game restarts from a recent checkpoint;in the cooperative game, the robot respawns shortly afterwards without restarting the puzzle.The goal of both campaigns is to explore the Aperture Science Laboratory—a complicated, malleable mechanized maze. While most of the game takes place in modular test chambers with clearly defined entrances and exits, other parts occur in behind-the-scenes areas where the objective is less clear.
The initial tutorial levels guide the player through the general movement controls and illustrate how to interact with the environment. The player must solve puzzles using the 'portal gun' or 'Aperture Science Handheld Portal Device', which can create two portals connecting two distant surfaces depicted as matte white, continuous, and flat. Characters can use these portals to move between rooms or to "fling" objects or themselves across a distance. Outlines of placed portals are visible through walls and other obstacles for easy location.
Game elements include Thermal Discouragement Beams (lasers), Excursion Funnels (tractor beams), and Hard Light Bridges, all of which can be transmitted through portals.Aerial Faith Plates launch the player or objects through the air and sometimes into portals. The player must disable turrets or avoid their line of sight. The Weighted Storage Cube has been redesigned, and there are new types: Redirection Cubes, which have prismatic lenses that redirect laser beams, spherical Edgeless Safety Cubes, an antique version of the Weighted Storage Cube used in the underground levels, and a cube-turret hybrid created by Wheatley after taking control of Aperture.The heart-decorated Weighted Companion Cube reappears briefly.Early demonstrations included Pneumatic Diversity Vents, shown to transport objects and transfer suction power through portals, but these do not appear in the final game.All of these game elements open locked doors, or help or hamper the character from reaching the exit.
Paint-like gels (which are dispensed from pipes and can be transported through portals) impart certain properties to surfaces or objects coated with them.Players can use orange Propulsion Gel to cross surfaces more quickly, blue Repulsion Gel to bounce from a surface,and white Conversion Gel to allow surfaces to accept portals.Only one type of gel can be effective on a certain surface at a time only. Some surfaces, such as grilles, cannot be coated with a gel. Water can block or wash away gels, returning the surface or object to its normal state.
The game includes a two-player cooperative mode.Two players can use the same console with a split screen, or can use a separate computer or console; Microsoft Windows, Mac OS X, and PlayStation 3 users can play with each other regardless of platform; a patch provided in late 2012 added split-screen support for Windows and Mac OS X users under "Big Picture" mode.Both player-characters are robots that control separate portal guns and can use the other character's portals.Each player's portals are of a different color scheme, whereof one is blue and purple and the other is orange and red.A calibration chamber separates the characters to teach the players to use the communication tools and portals. Most later chambers are less structured and require players to use both sets of portals for laser or funnel redirection, launches, and other maneuvers.The game provides voice communication between players, and online players can temporarily enter a split-screen view to help coordinate actions.Players can "ping" to draw the other player's attention to walls or objects, start countdown timers for synchronized actions, and perform joint gestures such as waving or hugging.The game tracks which chambers each player has completed and allows players to replay chambers they have completed with new partners.

Portal 2 is a FPS puzzle game. It is a direct sequel of Portal 1, and has many similarities to it. However, portal 2 is not the kind of game to sit there and copy what its predecessor did. Absolutely not, it’s here to improve on its past and give you an even better experience then last time
The game uses your standard FPS WASD and mouse controls, but also supports a special razer controller, and Xbox gamepads 10/10
The game sounds great. the OST is nothing special, but it gets the job done in the game. All explosions and sound effects are fine. The voice acting in this game is also great, and the dialogue can be quite funny. 10/10
The game looks great, it runs well on any modern pc, and the specs match the performance and graphical output. 10/10
The game's difficulty depends on your puzzle solving skills. Personally, I got through fine without a walkthrough, but I know others who have gotten stuck at points. There is no difficulty or hints, should you get stuck and not be able to proceed, then you will need to turn to the internet. I can understand how one would get stumped in this game, with some of the testing chambers being massive. and i wish valve would have put in a hint button for new or younger players. But in my experience, i got through just fine. 8/10
The story picks up right after portal. X amount of years have passed and Chell must once again be tested. There are several new characters to the series, which it needed. It also manages the bridge the gap between the Half-life and Portal series. I had no issues with the story, and was impressed to see how clever valve was at linking things, and giving background. 9/10
A new feature in Portal 2 is the ability to play 2player co-op testing chambers together. This has no real story to it, but takes place directly after the single player campaign. It's very enjoyable to play portal with a friend, and because of the emote commands, you won’t need a mic, or even a chat box really.  10/10
Both the single and multiplayer game modes can be completed in about 10hours total. That’s too short to make this game worth buying unless it’s on sale, Luckily, valve has opened the community to map making, which means, now the game is basically endless. There will always be another community level to play, but not all of them are good. 8/10
Portal 2 is a must have for every steam library. Delivering 2 decent story modes, and endless community levels, you’re in for a good time. You will get to build on the half-life universe, and have a few good laughs while you’re at it.

This is going to be a long review, but it should help you understand the other reviews.
Long time ago the devs had a tech tree system requiring you to grind hours worth of tech points to unlock new parts, you had to unlock both cubes and parts. Everything was ranked in tiers and if you had tier 3 parts and cubes you played with tier 3 and 4 players. At tier 10 you would be fighting with others who were the same. But you could abuse this system, if I wanted to use tier 4 weapons in tier 1 you would have to make sure the majority of your cubes were tier 1. Tier 10 fights were basically shoot each other for 1min or until you break off a piece of your opponent and gain an advantage. Devs thought this was boring, too grindy. They removed tiers and added a adding system, the more advanced your technology on your bot is, the higher tier you are. Armor blocks are a standard health each and no longer range depending on tier, you can color them too allowing for more customization without sacrificing functionality. Overall they made the game more flexable.
To adress the comments of Pay to Win, the game is only slightly pay to win. You can buy tons of blocks and weapons with real money, in fact each block costs 1 GP or about $0.001 USD. Weapons and movement at tier 1 costs about 25~45 GP. With those prices it's deffinately Pay to win, if not for the fact that new players get free blocks to make bots. and that some of the best bots in the game are made with 4 hover blades, 2 thusters, and 6 SMG blasters. People complaining about op bots made of a few blocks that are Pay to Win are players that aren't playing the game right. Robots need to be balanced, probably measured, and caculated. You only have so many pFlops to use, you need to make sure anything you make is balanced correctly or it will be top heavy/not fly, and you need to make sure you are armoring the correct spots so that you don't get killed in 4 shots. The fewer blocks you have the less health you have, Everything needs balance.
The people who hate the new updates are the ones that put hours into the game and had everything reworked. The new updates make the game less difficult for new players, but the physics required are still the same. If you are someone who likes building robots and fighting them, this is the game for you. If you are someone who understands simple physics and mathmatics and likes to play shooting games, play this game. This game is fun, it's buggy as hell but it's deffinately fun when it works.

I give up with Robocraft.
TLDR; Robocraft devs don't know what they want their game to be. They've tried DM/TDM, E-Sports, Creative Building, MOBA, Player Choice Progression, Forced progression, bland progression. Each and every update drastically changing how the game plays and nullifying ANY work players have put in to creating their bots.
They establish one set of rules only to change them a few months down the line under the guise of "Balancing" or enabling "player creativity" and doing the complete opposite.
Not to mention the game has flaws from years ago still not fixed and now being hidden by new changes. For example MM being broken turning it into "Who has the most medics, wins"and hiding the poor matchmaking by removing robot classification "because not all bots were classified correctly" (translation, 1 in maybe 100 were wrong, and "its haaaard.")
-------------------------------
Too many wild changes, one step forward two steps back is this developers motto.
Robocraft initially had a sensible mixture of Creativity and Function. There was also a sensible mix of Grind, Progression and sense of achievement. It was a little lacklustre in places.
For example, the RP system allowed you to choose what you unlocked and the level system determined how "effective" those unlocks were. As you progressed in Level and CPU, your bots got bigger, your weapons better.
This has now been swapped out for a system where equipment is unlocked in order, over time with no player input. Once you unlock an item, that is it, theres no improvement. Everything is by default "Tier 10".
This in turn made building robots boring, no more balancing weaponry vs armor vs mobility. If you chose to go cosmetic-bot there was a challenge to making a bot functional but in "theme".
Now sure you can build a bot "exactly" as you want, as long as you like Yellow, Pink, White, Grey & Brown as your color palette. The other colours are locked to premium (Note they touted this "flattening" of tiers as an 'improvement' to creative robot building).
Then theres the slew of problems with actual Gameplay mechanics.
Initially there were balancing issues as expected, they kind of balanced themselves out up until Unleashed/Legendary update and the devs got stuck in a nerf cycle on everything except SMGs.
This last update saw them add the near useless flak, severely nerf the Medics Nano and turned it into SMGcraft again.
They also did away with many of the useful gameplay information elements.
Spotting now just says "Enemy Spotted" with no indication of flier, hover, walker, they claimed this is because bots were "complicated to classify" yet for the most they were classified correctly. This means you find it far harder to prioritise the right targets.
This also affects your own team negatively as you can no longer easily see if a friendly medic is nearby or if a push block is Rail Heavy and needs more SMG or plasma.
The game has also suffered Match making issues from day one. Resulting in differing metas.
The latest of which is "The Team who has the most medics, wins".
The hiding of Bot Type and spotting call outs I think was done to merely hide how bad the matchmaking is, especially as in the past when we could see the team makeups we would see matches where it was 6 rails and two plasmas vs say 6 SMGs and two medics.
Put simple, the devs have taken this game in far too many directions, too rapidly and with no forethought.
Initially it was a DM/TDM game, then they opened it up to the Creative Block Builders, then expanded to Boss Battles (removed, was one Megabot vs lots of little bots quite fun), then switching to try their hand at MOBA-like Tower matches, then trying to create some kind of bespoke "Robot Market" where players can sell their bots, but their currency system is too expensive to support.
Its like they saw all these good ideas from other games and tried to cram it into their own, trying to snap up a bit of another niche in gaming and half assing it so badly that it introduces more problems than it gains in players.
This is likely the reason why they "flattened" their game down to basic progression.

Portal 2 is a FPS puzzle game. It is a direct sequel of Portal 1, and has many similarities to it. However, portal 2 is not the kind of game to sit there and copy what its predecessor did. Absolutely not, it’s here to improve on its past and give you an even better experience then last time
The game uses your standard FPS WASD and mouse controls, but also supports a special razer controller, and Xbox gamepads 10/10
The game sounds great. the OST is nothing special, but it gets the job done in the game. All explosions and sound effects are fine. The voice acting in this game is also great, and the dialogue can be quite funny. 10/10
The game looks great, it runs well on any modern pc, and the specs match the performance and graphical output. 10/10
The game's difficulty depends on your puzzle solving skills. Personally, I got through fine without a walkthrough, but I know others who have gotten stuck at points. There is no difficulty or hints, should you get stuck and not be able to proceed, then you will need to turn to the internet. I can understand how one would get stumped in this game, with some of the testing chambers being massive. and i wish valve would have put in a hint button for new or younger players. But in my experience, i got through just fine. 8/10
The story picks up right after portal. X amount of years have passed and Chell must once again be tested. There are several new characters to the series, which it needed. It also manages the bridge the gap between the Half-life and Portal series. I had no issues with the story, and was impressed to see how clever valve was at linking things, and giving background. 9/10
A new feature in Portal 2 is the ability to play 2player co-op testing chambers together. This has no real story to it, but takes place directly after the single player campaign. It's very enjoyable to play portal with a friend, and because of the emote commands, you won’t need a mic, or even a chat box really.  10/10
Both the single and multiplayer game modes can be completed in about 10hours total. That’s too short to make this game worth buying unless it’s on sale, Luckily, valve has opened the community to map making, which means, now the game is basically endless. There will always be another community level to play, but not all of them are good. 8/10
Portal 2 is a must have for every steam library. Delivering 2 decent story modes, and endless community levels, you’re in for a good time. You will get to build on the half-life universe, and have a few good laughs while you’re at it.

Portal 2 takes an already fantastic concept and builds on it with a whole epic back-story that you garner through the narration of Cave Johnson, the founder of Aperture Science.  The beauty of the storyline is really in the details that aren't told.  You can choose to charge through the game if you wish, or you can choose to explore and get some of that backstory - a reward that is worth the extra time.  But don't take the game too serious, because it is truly a work of satire and comedy (and a great one at that).  The puzzles are much more challenging than the original, but not so much that you will find yourself stuck for too long.  In all, the game is absolutely impressive; it rankes very high on my list of favorites.  I expect it will be a favorite of yours as well.

Alright. Here I go. EH hem.
Back when I started playing this game it was RIDICULOUSLY fun. I lost enough sleep some nights playing this game that I simply elected not to sleep at all before work. Now I can't stand a singular match, have uninstalled, and watch the chaos unfold from the sidelines. I used to hope I would see "We screwed up and we're fixing it" but it's too late for that now. The devs are complete morons and their only focus is on making the game as unplayable as possible to create a greater inflow of cash, because that's what people pay for, right? Bad games?
So, from the perspective of what this game USED to be, it's horrible now. Literally unplayable, and I'm not throwing that word around. I haven't lasted more than one match every few months to test the waters. There is simply TOO MUCH going on. Every robot is bigger than yours and abuses mechanics harder than yours. Its in your face and if you beat it, POOF! It's gone! It's not dead, it just teleported somewhere not near you to fix itself (So much fun by the way. You just sit still and don't get shot while your robot magically repairs itself. Not game breaking at all) and it'll be back to wreck you with any one of the 4 other weapons it has mounted all over its surface. The game has sunk into a term of simple unbalancability, there are just some weapons that you cannot balance anymore because some genius elected that roles need not be in the game any longer. Everyone is a gunner, everyone is a plane, shotgunner, bomber, everything. Building a bot isn't about how good it looks or how well it's made, it's about how many blocks and guns you can fit before you can no longer fit your teleporter. (freejam elected that you should be able to fit 5 modules so now everyone is a machinegunning bomber medic shotgunner with a teleporter). The short range of the shotgun is complimented by the long range of railguns and so on. The downsides are completely canceled out by the unteen other weapons and modules you can fit on and creativity has simply no place in the game anymore.
HOWEVER, Let's take this from a standpoint of what the game is now, forget what once was...
It's not creative. Nothing about the game is creative. Creativity is shunned by losses.
It's not balanced. Every downside can be countered with another addition.
It's not fair. Between the rampant hacking and blatant abuse of mechanics, nothing is fair.
It's not fun or profitable. Both of those aspects have been thorougly hammered out.
It's a big gambling game.
Let me explain that last bit. Some god like figure in freejam assumed that what the players wanted was not to be rewarded for their work, but to be given a slot machine and hope for the best, only you don't get to keep the slot machine. You see instead of taking the logical approach to the situation freejam elected that the best way to make money was to throw a random number generator into the game. Imagine runniung 5 miles, getting to the finish line and getting a box. Inside the box isn't a gold medal. It's SOMETHING, but what? Well, is it a medal of sorts? Maybe. Maybe it's new shoes, an energy drink? Perhaps a backpack? WHO KNOWS! Fun, right? So you take a week to prepare for that five mile sprint, train, eat right, finally get to do it and come in first place. Your reward? Open the box. Audible gasp! It's a cup of water. The guy that came in 4th got a track shirt and a silver medal. "But I did better than him!" you may say to yourself. Well, eff you, RNG decided that his box was better than yours despite you, coming in first, statistically having a better chance to get better loot.
Oh the beauty of chance. You have to play a game as best you can for a CHANCE TO GET ANYTHING OF EFFING VALUE, A DAMN CHANCE. Of course our saviors at freejam came up with a solution! You can BUY these boxes for cash and have however many chances you pay for without playing the game. They don't want your reviews or game time, they want your money and they'll destroy the game further to obtain it, just enough to make it look fun but unplayable if you don't throw money at it.
The latest update removed the last bit of creativity I could find, the only reason left to play. You see, if you wanted to build something that looked nice it almost had to be a medic. Being a medic allowed you to be a screwball but sill be useful. One update introduced an automatic healing feature. In the past if you got shot your team needed a medic to heal you, otherwise you would stay damaged. Now if you get shot, just like all bad modern FPS games all you have to do is avoid getting shot for 10 seconds and poof! You're healed! After that medics were no longer needed, they were simply a luxary for the team, something that could heal you faster and while under fire. That's not it though. Medics used to be able to autoaim their healing lasers of godliness onto allies to heal them without focusing which allowed them to stay alive by paying more attention to moving around to cover while healing allies. Now they have to aim their medic beams. Because eff you, that's why. So the game has been entirely leveled out to "Sure you can use your creativity, but you won't get jack done".
See that picture of the robocraft logo? That's what the game COULD be, but isn't. Each and every one of those robots is absolutely useless. The fact is the greatest designs are also the most uninspired ones. Literal flying blocks or literal walking blocks. That's the meta. Make it big, make it tanky, and make it able to teleport away to heal itself. So the game is a bunch of moving contraptions having no real differences between them duking it out and whoever has more teammates with them wins.
So my belief is that really HAVE taken after world of tanks. They have successfully made a game so bad that the only way to play is to throw money at it and they've hidden byhind this "early access" BULL(crap) to justify it all. Well, the straight jacket is off now. "Free to play" my fat A.  Freejam can feel free to jam my foot up this "game"s rear end. Open the box though, it might get two feet or my middle finger. You never know.

My how far this game has fallen.
I've been into this game since pretty damn near the beginning. Back then it was a sense of adventure to rank up through the tiers and levels, both of which were very hard to increase - so the challenge was there. That sense of "Yeah, I built that" when you finally make that perfect bot was also brilliant.
Those days are long since past.
The tiering system is gone entirely, and it is SO EASY to level up, that when I started the game after it was first changed. I jumped from 55 to 100 instantly, and I heard you could jump from even further back than that. The game's menus are SO CLUNKY now and they're hard to navigate... I still don't know what many of my button mappings actually do on the menu, but they do something. The colouring system was a neat idea - though it's just a consolation prize for losing the tiering system - but you have to be premium to actually have creativity with the colours, which is just... marvelous. Oh, no more tech points? There goes the fun in unlocking things too.
The Community Robot Factory, while well-intended, is just a plagiarism facility at worst, and at best utterly annihilates that thrill of finally completing a robot which you built yourself. Also, HOW MUCH ARE THESE WEAPONS?! TEN MILLION RP FOR A SINGLE TOP-POWER WEAPON? GET STUFFED I AIN'T PAYIN' THAT I ONLY GET LIKE 50-100K PER BATTLE!!!
Medic bots have been rendered obsolete, as has any form of stategy in the game and the building, by the auto heal feature. If you do actually take damage, you can hide behind a corner, and get all your health back. What a load of♥♥♥♥♥♥ And the pilot seat was removed, so no need to worry about protecting the weak spot now.
I really miss the old boss battle/megabot challenge. Couple of strong bots against a full team of weak ones. That was actually really fun and it was balanced too. Guess they decided it gave the veteran players too much enjoyment, and they didn't want noobs rage-quitting after one of these fights, so it's gone now.
Worst of all, the game crashes a LOT more than it used to, which really pisses me off, as if you're in the middle of a battle, SEE YA NO REWARD FOR YOU WE JUST WANNA WASTE YOUR TIME BYE! I swear the amount of times I heard "A PLAYER HAS DISCONNECTED" in one match was frightening, just before I crashed myself.
I remember the days when I used to enjoy this game, but now it's both too complex and too simple at once. Complex, in the sense that all those CUBE VARIATIONS; inner slope, edge slope, what? WHAT ARE THESE FOR?
At least they refunded all those new garage payments I made so now I have thousands upon thousands of free GC. So there's that at least.
UPDATE TIME:
So, they changed the mechanics again, by changing prices so they are a bit cheaper. Fine, that's alright, it's a good start. What isn't so good is that they lowered the maximum reward whilst raising the minimum one, so now you earn roughly the same amount of RP whether you're complete crap or absolutely amazing. To quote, "Our intent was to help boost the RP income of below-average skilled players so they felt they could make progress regardless, and to lower the bonus obtained for doing exceptionally well to something far more reasonable."
So now what? Now there is ZERO incentive to actually put effort in to get good at the game, because you still get a decent amount of RP just for participation. This just downright insults those who have taken the time to learn and master the game by restricting the value of their skill, and patronizes the weak and makes it so that they don't have to actually master the game at all. Add this factor to the appalling matchmaking and you get a complete and utter mess of a competitive game.
... If you do exceptionally well at something, you expect to be rewarded for it. If you're bad, you're deprived of that reward so you have incentive to get better so you will EARN that reward. But no, everyone gets similar amounts now. It's as if the devs wanted to be modern-day Robin Hoods, or those feminists trying to sort out the mythical "wage-gap" that no-one can prove exists. There's a better way to fix the progression issue; stop making everything so goddamn expensive. Even with these price drops, most of the top-tier weapons are seven million or so anyway - so what's the point of all this?
Well, at least they tried. They killed off all of their veterans with this change, but they tried. I know some of you will call this "nitpicking" but when you see how much of a stupid concept this all is...
UPDATE AGAIN:
Ok. They reverted the reward changes. I take back all that I said before. Good to see that the devs are actually listening to the community for once. Let's see where the future takes the game now. They still have a bit to fix.

Also, HOW MUCH ARE THESE WEAPONS?! TEN MILLION RP FOR A SINGLE TOP-POWER WEAPON? GET STUFFED I AIN'T PAYIN' THAT I ONLY GET LIKE 50-100K PER BATTLE!!!
Medic bots have been rendered obsolete, as has any form of stategy in the game and the building, by the auto heal feature. If you do actually take damage, you can hide behind a corner, and get all your health back. What a load of♥♥♥♥♥♥ And the pilot seat was removed, so no need to worry about protecting the weak spot now.
I really miss the old boss battle/megabot challenge. Couple of strong bots against a full team of weak ones. That was actually really fun and it was balanced too. Guess they decided it gave the veteran players too much enjoyment, and they didn't want noobs rage-quitting after one of these fights, so it's gone now.
Worst of all, the game crashes a LOT more than it used to, which really pisses me off, as if you're in the middle of a battle, SEE YA NO REWARD FOR YOU WE JUST WANNA WASTE YOUR TIME BYE! I swear the amount of times I heard "A PLAYER HAS DISCONNECTED" in one match was frightening, just before I crashed myself.
I remember the days when I used to enjoy this game, but now it's both too complex and too simple at once. Complex, in the sense that all those CUBE VARIATIONS; inner slope, edge slope, what? WHAT ARE THESE FOR?
At least they refunded all those new garage payments I made so now I have thousands upon thousands of free GC. So there's that at least.
UPDATE TIME:
So, they changed the mechanics again, by changing prices so they are a bit cheaper. Fine, that's alright, it's a good start. What isn't so good is that they lowered the maximum reward whilst raising the minimum one, so now you earn roughly the same amount of RP whether you're complete crap or absolutely amazing. To quote, "Our intent was to help boost the RP income of below-average skilled players so they felt they could make progress regardless, and to lower the bonus obtained for doing exceptionally well to something far more reasonable."
So now what? Now there is ZERO incentive to actually put effort in to get good at the game, because you still get a decent amount of RP just for participation. This just downright insults those who have taken the time to learn and master the game by restricting the value of their skill, and patronizes the weak and makes it so that they don't have to actually master the game at all. Add this factor to the appalling matchmaking and you get a complete and utter mess of a competitive game.
... If you do exceptionally well at something, you expect to be rewarded for it. If you're bad, you're deprived of that reward so you have incentive to get better so you will EARN that reward. But no, everyone gets similar amounts now. It's as if the devs wanted to be modern-day Robin Hoods, or those feminists trying to sort out the mythical "wage-gap" that no-one can prove exists. There's a better way to fix the progression issue; stop making everything so goddamn expensive. Even with these price drops, most of the top-tier weapons are seven million or so anyway - so what's the point of all this?
Well, at least they tried. They killed off all of their veterans with this change, but they tried. I know some of you will call this "nitpicking" but when you see how much of a stupid concept this all is...
UPDATE AGAIN:
Ok. They reverted the reward changes. I take back all that I said before. Good to see that the devs are actually listening to the community for once. Let's see where the future takes the game now. They still have a bit to fix.

Every step of the way, you be interested in the unraveling story of Aperture Science. The comedic situations are smart and well timed, and the character's personalities are deep. The puzzles have multiple ways to be solved, so there is a fair amount of re-play-ability. You don't need any friends to play the coop, you can easily find a random player online to play with. The soundtrack fits perfectly with the events that take place, and really help set the mood and tone. If you buy this game, you will not regret it. You will think every penny is worthit. This is not the game I started playing in 2013. In my opinion, it's a much degraded version. Everything but the basic idea of building robots to battle is different from how the game originally was. For someone who began playing back then, the current implementation of research and robot building is downgraded. The research tree is no longer a tree, but is now linear. There is no longer any armour, and weapons and mobility are overcomplicated. There is also no longer a "core" (pilot's seat) to defend while building your robot and no longer any reason to style the robot in interesting ways.
From the perspective of someone who began playing more recently, however, this game is pretty good. It's a solid game with decently fun gameplay and fair monetisation. I can see why someone would be able to play this game for many, many hours and still have fun with it, as content is mostly player-generated. As long as they don't make any more massive reductions to the game, any new players should be pretty happy with it.

The storytelling is excellent. Plot twists are practically sitting behind every corner, and you never know where the story is going to go next. It has amazing pacing, very memorable and lovable characters, and an overall great atmosphere.
The score adds a certain ambiance to the levels that completely enhanced the experience of the game. In fast-paced chase sections, the soft, futuristic music transforms into a high tempo chase theme matching the gameplay. The composers definitely stepped up the game in this department.
Where the game falls short, however, is the gameplay. Unlike the first game where it's just you, the portal gun, cubes and buttons, this game tried too hard with the gimmicks, whether it be the light walls, gels, or the gravity fields. Sure, some of the rooms had me stuck for a couple of minutes, but none of the new mechanics introduce puzzles truly challenging.
Between the memorable storyline / characeters, Co-op mode, and the workshop allowing the creation of your own  levels and testing others' levels, I would still highly recommend this game to just about anyone. 7.5/10

So yeah, if you liked Portal and like puzzle games, go get it, it´s great

Robocraft is actually extremely fun . . .
.
The idea of the game is great, and there are a lot of fun mechanics.  The developers release updates at faster pace than I've seen in almost any game ever, which is sort of a good thing.
Except that so many of their updates seem so poorly thought out or untested.  Don't get me wrong, Robocraft is improving as a game over time, but every update is two steps forward, one step back.  Each update will release cool new features, and completely breaks something else.  The next will fix the previous issue, but break another part of the game.
Currently, the biggest issue is probably the matchmaking.  Your robot can be placed in a match with robots with hugely better parts.  It completely ruins the game to spend hours carefully designing your bot, and months honing your piloting skills, only to have it get wrecked by a box on wheels because the box on wheels has guns that deal twice as much damage.
.
Matchmaking is not the only issue either, other issues include:
-  Lack of voice chat, making communication and strategy with the team nearly impossible.
-  Some very, very flawed map design.
-  The medic tools heal faster than most guns can deal damage (unless at short range), which does not make for fun gameplay.
-  The platoon system (which allows you to play with friends) is glitchy and has been for over a year, which is a long time compared to the very frequent updates this game gets.  It is starting to feel like the developers don't care that trying to play with friends can be a huge pain.
-  The main game mode, battle arena, has some weird mechanics that make for a very strange and not very interesting meta-game.
-  Robots take too long to kill, especially in the early game.
-  Respawn times are too short (<10 seconds) early on in a match, although they do reach more reasonable times after a while.
-  Players frequently abandon the game.  To be fair, sometime it's not their fault and their game crashed.  This often makes matches uneven (like a 6 v 8).  The game tries to balance this by reducing the smaller team's respawn times, but reduced respawn times don't help the smaller team, they just make it take longer for them to lose.
If anyone doesn't understand or agree with something I said in this review I can try to explain in more detail.  Some of the issues are hard to explain in simple point form because it's more like a net of complex problems that exacerbate each other.
Despite the long list of issues, Robocraft is very fun
.  None of the other issues completely ruin a match like the terrible matchmaking can.  This review will remain negative until players are being put into fair fights.
If the matchmaking is fixed (and another game-breaking issue isn't introduced) in the next update and I forget to update this review, message me or leave a comment and I will.

Robocraft is a creative "build drive fight" game where you build your vehicle, called a "Bot" and take  it to battle. You can build any type of bot you want and robocraft currently features:
Cruisers - bots that use wheels
Tanks - Bots that use tracks called "caterpillar tracks"
Mechs - Bots that use Mech legs(Robot legs)
Hovers - Bots that uses hoverblades
Choppers/helicopters - Bots that use rotors
Planes - Bots that use wings and rudders
Sleds - Bots that uses Thrusters and ski's
Drones - Basicly a Sled on drugs that can fly
Walkers/Crawlers/Spiders - Bots that uses walker legs, theese can cling to any surface
Of course, you can mix both them as you wish.
recently you were also allowed to use a different mix of wepons and modules in addition, to perfect your hybrid Bots of destruction!
After every battle you get a Crate depending on your leaderboard position(sort by score) where you get a somewhat random set of items. You get better items using a bot with higher cpu(bigger bot) and ending up on the top of the scoreboard.
All items in robocraft are balanced to be viable, so don't worry if you can't get the rarest items immediatly. Many of the rare "legendary" items are actually quite weak and have easy to counter mechanics, like how the shotgun only works on short range or missiles can be blocked by terrain.
You can also paint and customize your bots, since the game is F2P, pay to progress style of game many cosmetic features are premium.
Theese features do not have any actual effect on gameplay though and are almost exclusively catered towards cosmetic items and faster progression.
Be wary not to progress to fast however as you don't want to fight end game bots as a fresh beginner player. Afte all "Skill" can't be bought and that is going to be the deciding factor in Robocraft.
If you ever have any questions just make a thread on the forums and you'll hopefully get some useful advice.
Note - Robocraft is an "Early Acces" game, though it is planned to exit early acces after the "vision updates" somewhere at the end of the year/early 2017 if things go as planned.
As a result the game is subject to change over time and your feedback is welcome to polish the game. Theese updates are also a source of frustration for some players as you will probably see in the negative reviews.

Superior to Portal 1 in every possible way. For the first 1-2 hours, I figured this game would be more of what I had already experienced with Portal 1, I was wrong.
*SPOILER WARNING* For that amount of time it's a continuation of Portal 1, but then the story drastically changes. You're no longer facing the same antagonist, but this time it's someone new. What's great about this is that you're pretty much sent to various different areas of this facility and it expands on the story of the first Portal. You learn what went into building this super secret science facility, but you can also see what went into building the portal gun. Getting to experience the early stages of this portal technology was truly great and I loved it. The gameplay in the first Portal was great, but I felt that the story was alright, nothing great. This sequel gives you a story that's richer and fleshes out what has already been established.
If you enjoyed the first Portal, then you'll absolutely love this one. I give it a 4.5/5 and I definitely recommend it.

A great game, with wonderful graphics. Especially for when it was released.  It's another one of Valve's many masterpieces. One which thus far has brought me much enjoyment, and a little bit of mind bending. The puzzles are very good, and can require some out of the box thinking for a few of them.
+ Great Graphics for 2011, and for now honestly.
+ Gameplay is sublime, easy to learn, difficult to master. The way games should be.
+ Comical, there are some pretty funny moments with dialogue, that start within your first 5 minutes. I got a few laughs          out of it for sure.
+ Pretty solid length for a Puzzle-Platform game. I've not quite finished yet, and it's got what seems to be good "replayability" basically beating friend's times, and the like.
+ It has Co-Op, with a MM system as well. So if you don't have a friend to play with it will find you one. Very cool.
+ User Generated Level Creater, or UGLC for short. Which is connect to the Workshop. I haven't tried many out, but they seem pretty well done and are fun to play.
- Weird stuttering on many levels. (Might be intentional but I can't tell, and it's very annoying.)
- Camera changes angles when you go through a portal. (Minor gripe, and is probably a gameplay 'feature' but gives me a headache and can make some levels frustraiting.)

1.Preheat the oven to 180C/350F/Gas 4. Grease and line two 20cm/8in sandwich tins.
2.For the cake, place all of the cake ingredients, except the boiling water, into a large mixing bowl. Using a wooden spoon, or electric whisk, beat the mixture until smooth and well combined.
3.Add the boiling water to the mixture, a little at a time, until smooth. (The cake mixture will now be very liquid.)
4.Divide the cake batter between the sandwich tins and bake in the oven for 25-35 minutes, or until the top is firm to the touch and a skewer inserted into the centre of the cake comes out clean.
5.Remove the cakes from the oven and allow to cool completely, still in their tins, before icing.
6.For the chocolate icing, heat the chocolate and cream in a saucepan over a low heat until the chocolate melts. Remove the pan from the heat and whisk the mixture until smooth, glossy and thickened. Set aside to cool for 1-2 hours, or until thick enough to spread over the cake.
7.To assemble the cake, run a round-bladed knife around the inside of the cake tins to loosen the cakes. Carefully remove the cakes from the tins.
8.Spread a little chocolate icing over the top of one of the chocolate cakes, then carefully top with the other cake.
9.Transfer the cake to a serving plate and ice the cake all over with the chocolate icing, using a palette knife.

This game is AMAZING!!!!!!!!!
And yet very annoying!!!!!!!!!!
Overall Robocraft delivers unique creativity with fun gameplay that requires very little effort to get into.
The main gameplay is quick fast paced arcade style of gameplay of combat with very awesome robots.
However while the game play is arcade the sometimes realism of crafting can get in the way of combat.
For example the position of gun placement needs to be considered as a bot with a really awesome looking design, will be hindered in combat due to your weapons shooting your own robot.... This feature gets very annoying particularly for me when the BIGGEST selling point for this game is the unlimited creations you can make, but I feel the more awesome the creations are the less perfect they are in combat and vis versa.
Crafting robots also has its problems, as CPU, Mass and Cost are all things to consider when building a bot as some parts have higher values than others and it’s this that often makes a fun challenge to get the balance just right.
However as you get higher up in levels (100) you think this would get easier right? WRONG!
The cost of parts is so high you need to spend at least a week playing nonstop just, to afford just one of these high end parts.
Guess that’s why they tempt you with low price parts for micro transactions.... for SHAME!!!!!
Actually I did investigate this and actually got really good value for only putting $10 on!
On top of the cost of parts in higher levels the CPU required for each part isn’t better. The total CPU is a very random 1515... WTF? Why not just make it a nice even 2000? Even that may not be enough to make a half decent Godzilla!!!
I know this all sounds really bad and that I hate the game, actually..... I DON'T!
It is still awesome but I feel that with a few small changes to the game this could be VERY EPIC!!!!!!
1: Keep it Arcade!  Don’t let reality get in the way of fun gameplay! I don’t care if my guns shoot through the body of my robot, I just want to be able to hit my target! That goes double for rail guns that take ages to reload! You don’t want to waste a shot!
2: Reward creativity!!!  If I have quit my job just to waste 4 months building a very realistic replica of the Statue of Liberty, I should be rewarded for it!!! Just a simple voting system on the loading screen before each game would be nice & the most points get the reward. Or even just the simple thing of my gun being positioned in places that don’t ruin the look….
3: Keep it Cheap, Quick & Simple: The BIGGEST thing I love about this game is that it is a great time killer. I need to go out soon but I want to play a quick game this is my go to game! It is simple to play simple to craft and the only thing that seems to get in my way is lack of rewards and high prices for parts and this can be overcome in my next point….
4: Missions/Campaign: Have missions, campaign or monthly challenges that are very hard but offer very high reward! It would be nice to have an offline campaign to test my robot in that will give me rewards when servers are down or running very slow. Monthly challenges are great to make sure fans stick around.
5: Better AI: For a game that is about robots, the AI in single player mode….. Really suck!!!!!!!
I start to wonder if there is any AI in there at all with them not shooting at me or running around in circles for no reason… I mean is it that hard to make them actually do something? ANYTHING!?
How else do I test my robot in combat before putting it up against a human player?
Overall I feel this game has sooooo much potential to be a great game that will last the times, however it runs the risk of becoming greedy with micro transactions and frustrating to anyone who cannot devote themselves to this game 24/7.

The Portal series of games have a very simple concept. You must make your way thru a testing facility ripe with obstacles and armed only with a gun that shoots 2 different colored portals into surfaces (walls, floors, ceilings, panels, etc.). You enter one of the portals and come out the other while being prompted along by a sarcastically condescending and evil (?) female voiced AI. Simple right? Mwahaha ... think and think again :)
The game was artfully made. The ambience of the testing facility is nothing less than captivating. Each test chamber is a game in and of itself. With each completed test chamber you'll get a "pat yourself on the back" sense of achievement.
Try it - You'll like it.
