2017 Update:
Tried Robocraft out again for a few hours. To see where progress has been made or lost.
As predicted, most changes are made due to the dwindling playerbase. This explains why in the past they removed barriers to matchmaking like Tier Divisions, Level affected matching, reducing the amount of players per team etc.
I joined now to find that they've further made changes that exacerbate imbalanced matches by removing level requirement to unlock CPU, giving everyone the same CPU allotment at maximum and allowing bots of any CPU mixture to play together. It simply totals up the CPU on a team and makes it match up on the other team. The problem with this is, it inevitably ends up where you'll have one team with CPU evenly spread among them ranging from 1.4k to the maximum and the other team will be full of scouts with a single person at maximum cpu.
The game still suffers mobmentality wipeouts and favors it to be played as so. As much as there are cries of tactics are valid, nothing still beats team rushing.
Sadly though, these changes have done nothing to help new players, against old hats like myself and even older hats who understand Triforcing and damage mitigation, which is near gone, most resorting to either sheer bricks upon bricks or mobility evasion (read; drones). Only played a dozen matches today, lost one and thats because I decided to use a stupid bot you'd expect a noob to (one megaleg, rocket launcher, shield gen, thats it.) and even then, it was a close loss.
The ultimate kick to the teeth though, is the changes to the Battle Arena mode, specifically, the "Imbalance Detected" system, where it will cause Protonium to spawn on the map. If the enemy destroy it, they instantly equal the progress the winning team has made.
All this serves to do is infuriate the winning team and delay the match even further, as the losing team may have now equalised, but is still on a losing footing control point wise. If the losing team choose to ignore the Protonium and focus on the control points, again.. theyre still on a losing footing.
As it stands Robocraft has an average weekly player base of 3,000 spiking 6,000. In 2014 it was 14,000 spiking 25,000.
Lets see how you fare in 2018 Freejam. If youre even still around.
2016 Update: FJ are now trying to censor negative reviews as "abusive" even if they are not.
I give up with Robocraft.
TLDR; Robocraft devs don't know what they want their game to be. They've tried DM/TDM, E-Sports, Creative Building, MOBA, Player Choice Progression, Forced progression, bland progression. Each and every update drastically changing how the game plays and nullifying ANY work players have put in to creating their bots.
They establish one set of rules only to change them a few months down the line under the guise of "Balancing" or enabling "player creativity" and doing the complete opposite.
Not to mention the game has flaws from years ago still not fixed and now being hidden by new changes. For example MM being broken turning it into "Who has the most medics, wins"and hiding the poor matchmaking by removing robot classification "because not all bots were classified correctly" (translation, 1 in maybe 100 were wrong, and "its haaaard.")
Edit to include the latest update (Max Loadout) - Again FJ don't understand normal development practices. They threw in MASSIVE changes all at once and are no sat scratching their heads wondering why it broke. Flak is bugged (DMG), Nano is bugged (LMB+RMB = superspeed heal), MSMGs are bugged (free aim firing, without LOS), matchmaking is atrocious (still), Blink and DSM are stupidly expensive (Both RP/GC and CPU). They should have done a slow implement of these changes one by one to iron each minor kink, instead of this.
-------------------------------
Too many wild changes, one step forward two steps back is this developers motto.
Robocraft initially had a sensible mixture of Creativity and Function. There was also a sensible mix of Grind, Progression and sense of achievement. It was a little lacklustre in places.
For example, the RP system allowed you to choose what you unlocked and the level system determined how "effective" those unlocks were. As you progressed in Level and CPU, your bots got bigger, your weapons better.
This has now been swapped out for a system where equipment is unlocked in order, over time with no player input. Once you unlock an item, that is it, theres no improvement. Everything is by default "Tier 10".
This in turn made building robots boring, no more balancing weaponry vs armor vs mobility. If you chose to go cosmetic-bot there was a challenge to making a bot functional but in "theme".
Now sure you can build a bot "exactly" as you want, as long as you like Yellow, Pink, White, Grey & Brown as your color palette. The other colours are locked to premium (Note they touted this "flattening" of tiers as an 'improvement' to creative robot building).
Then theres the slew of problems with actual Gameplay mechanics.
Initially there were balancing issues as expected, they kind of balanced themselves out up until Unleashed/Legendary update and the devs got stuck in a nerf cycle on everything except SMGs.
This last update saw them add the near useless flak, severely nerf the Medics Nano and turned it into SMGcraft again.
They also did away with many of the useful gameplay information elements.
Spotting now just says "Enemy Spotted" with no indication of flier, hover, walker, they claimed this is because bots were "complicated to classify" yet for the most they were classified correctly. This means you find it far harder to prioritise the right targets.
This also affects your own team negatively as you can no longer easily see if a friendly medic is nearby or if a push block is Rail Heavy and needs more SMG or plasma.
The game has also suffered Match making issues from day one. Resulting in differing metas.
The latest of which is "The Team who has the most medics, wins".
The hiding of Bot Type and spotting call outs I think was done to merely hide how bad the matchmaking is, especially as in the past when we could see the team makeups we would see matches where it was 6 rails and two plasmas vs say 6 SMGs and two medics.
Put simple, the devs have taken this game in far too many directions, too rapidly and with no forethought.
Initially it was a DM/TDM game, then they opened it up to the Creative Block Builders, then expanded to Boss Battles (removed, was one Megabot vs lots of little bots quite fun), then switching to try their hand at MOBA-like Tower matches, then trying to create some kind of bespoke "Robot Market" where players can sell their bots, but their currency system is too expensive to support.
Its like they saw all these good ideas from other games and tried to cram it into their own, trying to snap up a bit of another niche in gaming and half assing it so badly that it introduces more problems than it gains in players.
This is likely the reason why they "flattened" their game down to basic progression.

Note (1/9/2017): It's official. This game will simply never leave EA. It is very much a complete game. But why bother leaving EA when it just means you won't be able to use early access as an excuse to dismiss criticism?
*TL;DR WARNING*
Before you read the rest of the review, I want you to notice a trend. Look at the positive reviews. Notice how most of the positive reviews (except for the ones at the top) are from people with very few hours, rarely more than 100, and almost never over 200. Also look at how the positive reviews (for the most part) sound like they were all written by little children. Compare with negative reviews. Most negative reviews have hundreds of hours, tons of experience, and have watched this game go from something amazing to nothing more than a depressing reminder that you should avoid early access games. On top of that, you can tell that the people who write most of the negative reviews for the most part sound more mature, or at the very least can spell words correctly. Many of the recent positive reviews are worthless comments saying "good gam" or "10/10" or something equally meaningless.
Okay, now I can explain this. The devs for a while now have been deliberately trying to pretty much kick out all of the veterans. They ignore our feedback, ignore our problems, and on top of that, they move out updates that kill massive amounts of the playerbase. Their strategy of getting new players is horrific, and they do it by exchanging experienced veterans for new players, and given that new players usually quit pretty soon after starting the game, you will see on Steam Charts how much this game has fallen in popularity. around 4000 online while writing this, when it was released on Steam a little after I joined, this game had on average around 14000. The game gets a small player spike every time an update is released, but then they eventually lose more players than they gain. FreeJam is attempting to rebuild there playerbase, this time instead of it consisting of friendly and mature players, their new playerbase is made 99% of illiterate 10 year olds that probably all have a below average IQ.
Now, let me take you down memory lane to explain to you the updates that really screwed up this once amazing game. Unfortunately, I forgot which order the updates go in, so instead I'm just going to say which major changes screwed over this game, it's community, and it's future.
Tiers were what made Robocraft.... Robocraft. I still vividly remember how much I enjoyed moving up tiers. I eventually got to tier 10, and that was a huge accomplishment for me. Now, they removed tiers, and so no one else will be able to feel awesome after finally achieving tier 10. Now, the whole system is based on levels, which was screwed up also.
Is it even possible for a game to seriously screw up something as basic as a simple leveling system? It is when you work for FreeJam, to aid them on creating a trainwreck of a steam game.. Now, the game depends on leveling, and not tiers. But wait! There's a catch. Now, leveling is so easy, An experienced player could probably create a new account and reach level, 100 within 48 hours. The first time this happened, I went from level 42 instantly to level 100 (the max level at the time), and I heard that they later made it even easier to level up later on.
A fairly recent addition to the game was the CRF, or Community Robot Factory. Now, it's easier than ever to plagiarise the bots of other players. Not into plagiarism? Oh well, the CRF still means that much of the element that the game was known for, building, is gone. This game was supposed to be a game where you build, drive, and fight. Now it's a game where you drive and fight bots that you took from someone else. A place to share creations is good for most games, but Robocraft is not one of them.
This was actually a better update that the other ones, I'll admit, but it does take this game a step closer to being pay2win, and does take something else away from the game aswell. Now, cubes are no longer tiered, and with that, they no longer have their own colors. To get better cubes, you need higher robot ranking or levels (I forget since I haven't played this game in weeks) but now all cubes are colorless, all parts are colorless. Everything is white. Non-premium users get only 4 colors, (white, orange, and 2 others that I forgot), while a premium user gets them all.
What happened to TP (tech points)? Well, the developers thought to themselves, "This is unacceptable. Our players are actually enjoying this feature. It must be removed at once!" and now we have no more tech points. They were originally used to gain access to new parts, although now the tech tree is no longer a tree, it's an ugly elliptical spiral where you get everything on it for free, by leveling up. They may as well just remove the 'tech tree' entirely, cause that implies that there's actually different paths of things to unlock, but nope, not anymore.
This entire section used to be about how grinding for RP took hours upon hours, which took a total of 112 hours for the "perfect" regular bot, or otherwise about 450 battles, and about twice as long for a megabot, which has since been removed. Now, however, it's based on an awful CS:GO style RNG clusterf*ck, which is even worse than before. Since the game is now RNG based, I'm unable to make any reasonable predictions about how long it would take to get what you'd consider a "perfect" bot. Weapon prices are completely hell now, even worse than before, and now the currency is a "robits" system which is beyond terrible. To put it into perspective, every block ingame now costs a certain amount of Robits. Previously unobtainable and rare holoflags (or whatever they're called now) are also now obtainable, which is also where Freejam screwed up. The old premium currency of GC was exchanged for money that you could use to buy premium or crates with. Unfortunately, we got completely ripped off and my 2300 GC was changed to about 3 dollars or something, barely enough for 3 day premium. Anyways, any ingame block has a price of robits, but you can also find any part in crates. However, when recycling something, you literally get a tenth of what its worth, making the whole recycling system an effective waste of money. Another thing worse mentioning is that when opening a crate, you can see what you would have gotten with premium, since premium users get twice as much stuff. And then if you would have gotten something incredibly rare if you were premium, you are just left to feel bad about it unless you want to actually buy premium.
This was a longer review than I thought it was going to be, but everything said here is true, except that my statistics may somewhat inaccurate since I haven't played in a while. I'd keep writing on, but apparently there's a limit to how big reviews can be, so I'll stop here. This game is probably the biggest disappointment i've ever played.

This is undoubtably one of the game's strong points. For this game, "Perpetual" means
. The workshop is bursting with innovative tests/levels to try out, whether they have received a thousand reviews or none (try them- 0 stars ≠ a bad level, just an untested one). There is a full (although not complete) parts palatte in the in-game designer, and you can download Hammer (a more complex, but more powerful) level editor for free.
The game spins a wonderful single player narrative, which consists of at least 40 hours of my gameplay, and is filled with hidden areas and special achievements. I have not scratched the surface of the multiplayer story mode, but if the single player campaign is any measure, the multiplayer offers not just twice the portals and players, but also twice the story richness. The soundtrack can be downloaded for free, and features wonderful tracks found both in-game and outside of it. From a performance perspective, this game runs excellently, even from an external drive, and maintains good framerate, animations, and graphics (I run Portal 2 on a windows 10 operating system upgraded from Windows 8, so results may vary -if your computer is older than the release date of 2011).
If you are viewing this via steam, you must at least appreciate Valve for providing you a well-designed platform to buy games. This is one of theirs. The concept is wonderful, the community is awesome, and from what I can tell, Valve is pretty on top of things.

What to say about this game...hmmmmm....well lets start at the begining....
Robocraft, a game where you build a vehicle of your own design out of verious shapes and arm it with one type of a few weapons (for most players this usually ended up as a flat platform with so many guns pasted all over it that you cant even see the blocks under said guns). The Game started out well with a rather large (and messy) tech tree, where you selected to spend your earned points on the module of your choosing. You would pit your beloved creation againt that of many other players in an arena type setting, where you would earn tech points, experience and RP for killing the creations of others. Sometimes one would encounter a boss battle, where a number of lower leveled players would be put up against a few high level players with superiour armaments.
This game was relatively fun.....but this is no longer.

Ingredients:
1. 6 tablespoons unsalted butter
2. 1/2 cup white sugar
3. 1/2 cup brown sugar
4. 1/4 cup water
5. 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon
6. 1 pinch salt
7. 5 apples - peeled, cored and sliced
8. 1 pastry for double-crust pie
Directions:
1. Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
2. Combine butter, white sugar, brown sugar, water, cinnamon, and salt in a saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a boil, remove from heat and set aside.
3. Roll out half the pastry to fit a 9-inch pie plate. Place bottom crust in pie plate; pour in apple slices.
4. Roll out top crust into a 10-inch circle. Cut into 8 (1-inch) wide strips with a sharp paring knife or pastry wheel. Weave the pastry strips, one at a time, into a lattice pattern. Fold the ends of the lattice strips under the edge of the bottom crust and crimp to seal.
5. Pour butter-sugar mixture over top of pie, coating the lattice, and allowing any remaining sauce to drizzle through the crust.
6. Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and bake until the crust is golden brown, the caramel on the top crust is set, and the apple filling is bubbling, 35 to 40 more minutes. Allow to cool completely before slicing.
Eat.

Cluster♥♥♥♥.... That's the only word i can use to describe what this game has devolved into. When i started out, there were 3 types of guns: SMG, Plasma Artillery and Sniping Rail Guns. Simple, easy, sufficient. They soon added tank tracks, tesla coils, walker legs, wings, and then improved on elector shielding, even the MOBA-like new game mode. These were all good additions, it made gameplay more diverse without breaking everything. It added content without sacrificing the essence of the game.
But then... it all went to Hell... Mech legs, Flak guns, homing missiles, helicopter blades, "aero rods", and completely re-vamped (and gutted) health system that destroyed the very reason Robocraft building was so unique. it was getting out of hand. The problem was, FreeJam realized that the more content they added (and the higher they priced it) the more money they raked in. So off to the races they went, and they're never coming back....
The final straw for me was when they added "abilities" for the vehicles. stealth modules, dash modules and shield modules. FreeJam had gone full-blown mad.... all the while, the content they teased to their fans (the HUB for example) got swept under the rug because they figured it wouldn't bring in as much sweet sweet cash as New, Flashy Guns! And Awe-Inducing Ability Modules!
FreeJam used to be one of my favorite developers, constantly giving out free 1-day premium codes if the servers went down, and pricing most things relatively cheap. I had no problem at all paying my money to them because they were so great. Now i regret every cent I gave these people.. and every minute I spent playing this game only for them to ruin it, and waste all the potential it had... The last time i checked in on a Robocraft stream, the streamer had a chaingun on his walker and I wanted to cry...
Now i'm just waiting for someone to learn from FreeJam's screw ups and make a game like this... hopefully they don't ♥♥♥♥ it up as badly as FreeJam has... R.I.P. Robocraft... You could have been so great.

This is undoubtably one of the game's strong points. For this game, "Perpetual" means
. The workshop is bursting with innovative tests/levels to try out, whether they have received a thousand reviews or none (try them- 0 stars ≠ a bad level, just an untested one). There is a full (although not complete) parts palatte in the in-game designer, and you can download Hammer (a more complex, but more powerful) level editor for free.
The game spins a wonderful single player narrative, which consists of at least 40 hours of my gameplay, and is filled with hidden areas and special achievements. I have not scratched the surface of the multiplayer story mode, but if the single player campaign is any measure, the multiplayer offers not just twice the portals and players, but also twice the story richness. The soundtrack can be downloaded for free, and features wonderful tracks found both in-game and outside of it. From a performance perspective, this game runs excellently, even from an external drive, and maintains good framerate, animations, and graphics (I run Portal 2 on a windows 10 operating system upgraded from Windows 8, so results may vary -if your computer is older than the release date of 2011).
If you are viewing this via steam, you must at least appreciate Valve for providing you a well-designed platform to buy games. This is one of theirs. The concept is wonderful, the community is awesome, and from what I can tell, Valve is pretty on top of things.
This is one of the most innovative games designed and it deserves recognition. Any human being who plays these games and appreciates good quality would be out of their mind to NOT buy this game, whether you are anxious to buy and play it now or are a cautious cheapskate like myself (I bought it on sale for < US$5.00). tl;dr Great game, try it out if you are interested and don't let those negative reviews fool you. Maybe the game is for you, maybe it isn't, it's mostly about taste. My playtime isn't reflected correctly because I play with the Launcher version.
I play this game for quite some time now, sometimes with breaks of a month inbetween (I am that kind of player..)
The game changed drastically in every aspect since I started off. It seemed to change for the worse for about a year iirc.
However now that the last few updates are out and the dev-team rethought about what they want to achieve with this game, it changed for the better big-time and I can fully recommend this game despite some issues.
With the last updates (Full Spectrum Combat being one of them, the Flak-update being another one) the devs
changed the direction of Robocraft from a vertical progression system to a horizontal one, solved the identity crisis
their game had, updated the engine (unity 5 now) and overhauled whole parts of the game in general.
+ The game is still not finished yet, but it never felt as satisfying as it does now.
+ There is a learning curve when you start off the game with no knowledge whatsoever. It's not steep in any way though,
some stuff will look like common sense after a while. Everyday Physics only apply to a certain degree.
- (You can cover up whole wings and rudders and it won't affect the way the robot flies other than the weight)
+ Building a robot is quite challenging if you try to combine design and efficiency, but in case it proves too challenging
at first, there is always the possibility to buy a bot from the shop and look at those designs closely
(they are mostly community made, you can also upload a bot yourself there.)
Some designs work much better than others even thought they may look similar from the outside.
- A negative point I really have to add is the fact that this game is still not running as great as it could run.
You can run it on a potato gpu or cpu, but even with a great pc you may experience some issues like awkward
framepacing, some stutter after about 10-15 games (much much better since Full Spectrum Combat)
sometimes also errors that may not make much sense, but oh well, this game isn't alone.
+However, the dev-team works hard in order to improve those things and have made really great improvements in the
last 5 weeks alone and will continue to do that.
- Another negative point.. The Robocraft community is a tough one to handle at times. (This review section... really?)
It's generally nice ingame, other than the special flowers.
But in case you should wander to the forums, you will see a huge rift between parts of the community.
There are those that complain about every change, no matter if it benefits the game or not.
Then there are those who write constructive Feedback. Those who "know everything" without even playing updates...
And then you have those who threaten to abandon the game the second something isn't going their way. (Very visible
during the reveal of Chapter 3, or how I call it: nobody-trusts-nobody-in-fanboy-times;
I'm pretty sure quite a few player actually jumped the gun and left at that time as well,
mainly the diehard-ones who don't even.)
Luckily enough, they are a small small part of the whole community.
Some of those negative reviews after mid-december complaining about the game going downhill
are one thing that shows this situation very well.
There may be some genuine negative reviews around, but what I've read they are only trying to pull the game down
now that they left it after being butthurt without ever leaving a Review before. (And as mentioned before, some
issues they mention are solved. Time does not stand still)
_______

You as a potential new player have nothing to look back to so quite a few negative things said about the game are
basically non-issues.

However keep in mind in case of issues that this game is Early Access.
Anyway, I fully recommend to at least try this game for a while if you are interested.
Maybe you love it as deeply as much of the community does. Or you hate it deeply and enthusiastically.
(Or both)

Robocraft has a strange place in my library. Its right between the games I love to play, and the games I wont touch anymore. The game used to be so much more simple, from the way you level up to the number of game modes to choose from. In my opinion, the game has gone from a fun, simple, creative game into a meh, crazy confusing, streamlined boring title.
Gone is the strategic building layout of your robot - you dont have to protect a seat anymore, you dont have different armour levels to mix and match for different builds, cosmetic discontinued blocks that we spent loads of money on and hoarded are also gone and worst of all, half of the items in the game were removed, causing most, if not all of your robots to become obsolete,
The game used to have an exp type system with the option of spending real money to use the xp from one tier on another. Those of us who did this to get to end game sooner got no refund or recompence when that was removed and everyone was given everything for free.  Now the unlock system is automatic the more you play. You no longer have to do anything well in the game, play enough and you will get to end game.
The game used to only have two game modes. Boss battle and team deathmatch. I have devoted 670 hours (according to steam) into this beautiful gem. I loved it. It was beautiful, but unfortunately Freejam has made some very fatal mistakes recently. Barely none of my friends play it anymore.
First: They removed tiers. The Battle Arena was a pretty cool concept, but tiers were the only things that gave you a sense of what equipment you should be using. Do I know what type of guns I should be using if my robot's rank is 7,000? Well no I don't. Often times I go into a match and people are using higher tiered guns and armor because I don't know what the standard is. Removing tiers was just the beginning.
Second: The Tech Web. Back then, we had the tech tree and tech points. We could unlock whatever we wanted, now, every time you want something new you need to painstakingly grind to level up, while before it took significantly less games just to grind for the tech points. And even then, you at least get to pick whatever you wanted in the tree. In the web, you don't get to pick what you want. Did you want helium after spending 2 hours grinding? No? Well too bad.
The third and final mistake: Removing armor cubes. I can get the idea of implementing paint in, but why can't you keep the armor cubes? People have spent so much RP for those things, and (as far as I've seen) you don't get a refund for the RP that you've spent on every single armor cube, and what do we get out of this? A paint system that's limited to only 4 colors unless you have premium. Was this really worth removing armor cubes? What were they thinking?!
My conclusion: This game, makes me extremely depressed. There were so many things they got right with the game in the past, the game was at it's greatest and now they've ruined it. There's plenty of new players so the game is thriving I guess, but it's sad that I can no longer have fun anymore. Matches are filled with thruster sticks and matchmaking in general is more confusing and complex than it should be. Never have I had a team deathmatch where people actually coordinated as a team. It hurts really bad to not recommend this game. I've spent maybe over 30 bucks for this game because I loved it.
For the new players in Robocraft who like this game, I envy you. I really want to love this game, I really do. But unfortunately I just started off playing too early. The nostalgia got to me. I'm just not wired the way everyone else is. Unless you've experienced what I have in the past, you will never truly understand.
RIP, another veteran player.
Post-Script: I forgot, but they removed robot seats too, there goes another key aspect about the game. When you build your bot, your goal is to protect the seat as much as possible. Now what are you supposed to protect? Your own armor? Freejam please...

This had been a great game. I have 138.6 hours on it, and most of them were awesome. I started during the era with tiers, and I got up to teir 6. I came back to this game to a brand new game mode, that is now called "Battle Arena". With the teir system, this was great! It allowed you to play for longer. Then, the removal of tiers. Also went the pilot seat, which was the fundamental building block. The armour cubes left, and paint came in! Now, the idea of levels givng you something didn't seem bad, since it just gave you CPU, but you have no choice what you get. Now in detail:
-Tier system: This was based on your robot ranking. The more you had, the amount was based on each item having its on specific number, the higher your tier. You could face harder people when you wanted, and if you found it to hard, you could downgrade. This was also the matchmaking component. You faced people your tier.
-Tech TREE: This is were you got new parts. You got Tech points from playing in matches, and then chose what you wanted to unlock. Each tier had its own Tech Points, TP1-TP10. Evenbtually, you would get eveything, but you would get what you prfered first. As a rail tank, I could get new treds and new rails first, than plasmas and other stuff.
-Pilot seat: This was a factor that made the game fun and challenging. The pilot seat was the fundamental and most important block on your robot. If all connections to the pilot seat were broken, regardless of how much of your robot remained, it would be destroyed. This had the challenge. You had to defend your robot enough to defend the pilot seat, but still make a working robots. Again, as a rail tank, I learned where to fnd the Pilot seat on most robots and could take robots out because of that. It allowed SKILL in the game.
-One block system: Only one block. As a community, no clue if higher up weapons do the same damage to cubes. "But wait! You can PAINT THEM, Is that SOOOOOOOOO COOL" is probably what Freejam thought, but NO. IT AIN'T FUN. Now, you can have an ally be red on blue team! SO you are even more confused since the recent update doesn't show or tell you what type of robot they are!
-Matchmaker: Now. I have a couple things to say about this matchmaker. My friend and I started ne accounts since we got use to the game, and he was progressing more than I was. We were level fours. With the teir system, we would go against teir ones, because that would be normal. But no! This game puts two LEVEL 4S against LEVEL 90s! On the other accounts, I had just gotten the second plasma (Not tier 2 btw, its named like the devastator or something) and was up against people with MEGA PLASMAS.
You know, if you asked me if I liked this game about a year ago, I would say no. No I didn't like this game. I bloody loved it! It wa sincredible. But recetnly, with the rotten lower community that are negative and could scare away new players, and these new updates, its dead. My friend and I named a little term after this. Robocraftitis- When a game, through bad updates and devs who don't listen to the community, turns crap. Usually, that game used to be good, but is then the opposite. Try Gear Up if you want a fun game.

As many others have said the main reasons lie in the new updates.
Removing the Pilot seat essentially made it so you have to destroy the entire craft, eliminating the idea of hitting weak points so you can take out enemies more efficiently.
This was a huge one, now instead of choosing the style of gameplay you prefer or excel at, it's all jumbled up in a confusing level up system. Forcing you to unlock items that are, for you intents, useless. This seems like a easy way to get money from the players or to make players grind in the game to have better looking stats.
The makers have yet another trick up their sleeve to make players grind their mind out or pay up to play. It takes around 5-7 games give or take to level up for an extra 11 pFLOPS. Thats about a small thruster or 11 blocks. Very little for about 25 minutes of gameplay.
I've played at around 12:00 - 5:00 and repeatly had the issue of massive imbalancing. It's not uncommon to be a level 7 playing with someone at level 15-20. While not as prevelant at lower levels, this still makes it very difficult to level up at around the level 10-25 range.
While not as bad as the tech tree/web issues, this is still annoying because I have a MacBook Pro and a very good desktop PC. The best graphical setting still lakes Anti-Aliasing and smoothing so I'm stuck with 300+ fps and no Anti-Aliasing or smoothing. On the MacBook it's a different story, while I can run other games like Garry's Mod and HL2 at a smooth 60 fps. I can run this game at a stuttery 60-58-1-57-60-43-2-60 and so on.
This was a major mistake. It was simple, useful and frankly very easy to learn and still was fun to play. You had to play and to a certain extent grind but it rewarded you appropriatly. Grinding for an hour now allows you to go up maybe 2 levels.
In other games like LoL, Dota 2, CS:GO or COD, whenever you objective is being taken, you'll have a verbal or visual alert. Whether it be "Bomb Planted at _!" or the objective with an alert or timer over it. In RoboCraft, it's a small hard to see and hard to spot bar at the top of the screen. That needs to go, it need's to be more visible to alert the team that someone is capping it. This is a major design flaw that needs to be fixed.
This was removed for no real reason, it was useful and a good design feature. Didn't seem to pose any type of imblancing issue. Now it just makes you use more blocks, which makes you use more pFLOPS, which makes you grind more.
These helicopter pack the same punch as tanks except many times more mobile and easier to protect, because you can simply put the rotors inside of the craft.
I feel like this narrows down what you can do so you can excel at it. But this feature is minimally useful as the tech spiral was introduced and made it so you can't choose your "class" or path you want to choose.
While not worth all the negatives, it's still a nice little addition.
This one was also squandered because of the tech spiral, but all of the block are useful and had balanced functions.
* Add Campaign, it seems like something that you guys were planning on doing but left unfinished.
* Add more weapons, maybe have a rail cannon that shoots quicker but does less damage so if you're in a sticky situation you won't be completely unprotected or a plasma grenade launcher that shoots with less drop but takes longer to recharge or does less damage. Maybe an laser SMG that shoots 3 bullets in a spray and each of the 3 bullets do 1/3 of the damage but damage more parts of the enemy craft.
* Add teamwork bonus, maybe giving you extra XP or money.
* Acheivements, let's say you win 3 games straight without dying. You could be rewarded pFLOPS, Decals or colors.

First, let me state that I haven't played any of the games similar to Robocraft. Second, just because I recommend playing this game, it doesn't show how enjoyable the game might acutally be for you; for that matter, you'll have to read this whole thing.
Skipping the basic description of the game which you can read elsewhere, let me explain what you can expect. The game in its current state is well enjoyable for up to 12, maybe 15 hours of gameplay. After that, it really matters whether it hooks you up and you are willing/enjoying grinding for ingame money. The graphics can't please a gourmet of sorts, the gameplay is repetitive (as any comptetitive multiplayer game would be nowadays), the game probably can't be played as frequently as, let's say, CS:GO or anything else that provides itself with its own replay value by just being enjoyable. But then, for some of the players, the satisfaction of playing the game could be enough as a replay value, although on a more casual level than in other games.
As the game is F2P, there's bound to be some microtransaction nonsense, in this case in a form of another ingame currency, for which you can buy a premium account removing some not-so-impactful restrictions (such as expanding one's squad slot number by one, thus up to 4 players can share a squad) or doubling the amount of ingame money obtained from matches. The pay-to-win factor in this game isn't very significant, as even though one can buy equipment for real money, one also has to level up in order to unlock said equipment.
Now commenting on the updates spanning across the past year-or-so: the game has been quite simplified in terms of vehicle variability (removing different armor tiers and the pilot seat), and also quite foolishly restructurized (implementing coloring your vehicle, which is good, but making available only 4 colors by default and the rest for premium users is not as good; the tech tree used to unlock gear was rendered useless - rather than a tree, it's just a linear spiral where you can only unlock one thing per level without the freedom of choice; also renaming the gear using some random names, possibly with a sexual-or-something context).
I don't know, it's fun, it was more fun before the stupid updates, I feel like the devs are meaning to make a good game out of this, but it would probably be better if they made this game paid for.

And the puzzles can be frustratingly hard, but hey, that's how puzzle games are supposed to be.
But other than that, Portal 2 is great. Gameplay? Equal parts thrilling and cerebral. Comedy? You'll chuckle more than Santa Claus playing Cards Against Humanity. An irresistably catchy pop tune? You got it. A solo opera performance by the actress who plays Glados? Oh, you didn't want one of those? Well, you're getting one, and you'll love it. Just like the rest of this game. You'll love it.

You don't need to be good at it to complete the levels. If you really do get stuck there are so many people out there who own this game who can help you, Walkthroughs on the internet ect ect.
The controls are fine. I had a♥♥♥♥♥♥of a time getting used to going through portals and judging when I should Jump for certain things but this generally happens to me because I'm definitely a stratagey gamer. The only downside I can see to the controls is The zoom function really doesn't help on quite a few levels where you'd think you'd need it, This downside is INCREDIBLY small so don't even bother letting this deter you from buying the game.
Graphics are spot on, They may not be from a blur trailer but they definitely give a nicer vibe than the origional portal did. They really make the characters like wheatley and Glados Pop out from the background and the standard black/white contrast from the first portal is still there. Sometimes the high contrast effect isn't that high and can prove difficult for certain people. But there isn't anything really wrong with that.
In general gameplay it's hard to hate Glados or Wheatley, Both attempt to kill you in this game and glados has been trying since the first portal. But wheatleys Idiocity really gives me the feel that he's harmless, and We'll be fine no matter what he does. Glados may be a little on the lack of sanity side. But In the end glados respects you. I mean how many games pull this off this well?
To conclude this rather rough review, I'd like to say I most definitely Reccomend this game and to anyone looking for a quick game that does have Mp Co/op and isn't too tricky. This is definitely for you. I rate this game 9.8/10, the only 0.2 being those extremely minor things that I would've liked to seen improved on, but hell it's hard to make a perfect game so good job to the team at Valve for making Portal 2 what it is today.

Only THEN can you get all the pieces and solve the puzzle. I believe Zero-Punctuation said it best when this is essentially everything that was Portal and improved upon it....while at the same time discarding some puzzle aspects by throwing in obligatory story points.  In his review, he essentially said that Portal was for the puzzles, where Portal 2 was for the story.  For the most part, I agree, but not in the negative sense.  The story is good, but there are a lot of times where puzzle experiences are interrupted by storypoints.
Portal 2 removes some puzzle functions from Portal such as the light-ball puzzles (which are now substituted by lasers) and rocket turret puzzles (which are now substituted with gels, funnels, and light bridges).  In a nutshell, Portal 2 has a lot more functionality than the first game, but it is (once again) on the easy side.  The humor with your sidekicks and antagonists (spoilers with-held) is also there, but the humor may not survive more than 1 or 2 playthroughs, which cuts down on the replayability.  It does, however, have a multi-player campaign and a community map-maker campaign, which includes maps you make and maps others make, which you can download and play at your own leisure (with humorous commentary before every map).
PROS:
New map features (Gels, lasers, funnels, and light bridges)
Humorous voice-acting
Great aesthetic presentation
Great cinematic cutscenes
Multi-player campaign (lengthens replayability)
Community maps  (lengthens replayability)
CONS:
Light-ball and rocket puzzles removed
Humor can get dull
Limited replayability (Gets boring once you've seen just about everything the game has to offer, then you'll rely on some insanely difficult community puzzles that'll make you rage-quit)

This game used to be so much fun! I have put so much time into it, only to have everything fun and great snatched away from me. The mechanics of the game have changed so much over the course of the development, that it's hardly Robocraft anymore. They got rid of the Tech Tree completely. They are like you can unlock anything you want to... As long as it's the next thing in the list... If they ever go back to when Robocraft was a game of creativity and competition, that will be a day of celebration. But for now, this game has been renamed Robocrap.

(Changing this to Recommended so as to prevent bots from downvoting this, It's still actually Not recommended)
Where to begin? I suppose at the beginning....
When this game first came into my que, I was overjoyed at the possibilities it offered; Progression, Creativity, Engineering and Fairness...
Now I was concerned with several of the updates, and overjoyed in anticipation of others; The removal of Repair costs, the addition of megabots with boss battles, several new maps and the spotting/messaging system to promote teamwork to name a few...
But these latest few updates have stripped the game of all four of these qualities...
First is progression, with the removal of weapon, movement, and armor tiers Robocraft is no longer about progression from a weak starter bot fighting against other weak starter bots towards higher tiers and more complexity...
True, grinding was there as is in any free game, but the sheer prices required for just one weapon are rediculous; The front facing smgs were suppose to be FREE to allow someone to start all over at the beginning should they wish...
This brings me to the second point:
There is no longer any creativity... With the advent of the robo-shop, anyone can buy a 'powerful well built bot' just by paying some real world cash rather than having to build it themselves or learn/analyze a new design... With the removal of the pilot seat and different tiers of armor blocks, there is no longer a need to protect a 'central core' portion of the bot, which removes most of the challenges involved with designing a good vehicle.
As a result the higher tiers (Including ranked) are filled with Tesseracts and exploit builds bought straight out of the Roboshop, and good luck finding anything remotely unique from these standard UGLY flying boxes. Likewise the lower tiers are FILLED with high speed hovercraft plasma gun wielding bots, that while still within the confines of the 1-10k system OFFER AN UNFAIR DISADVANTAGE to the new players who have yet to gain these weapon types UNLESS THEY SPEND MONEY.
The third and final stroke is of course what I mentioned earlier; The unfairness...
The game now caters to those who are willing to spend more money by increasing the in-game currency prices for guns to EXORBANT RATES... The latest update which offers a COUNTER to the tesseract problem costs 11,000,000 RP just for an example... (1 million RP takes roughly five wins if you get a high score/kill more than 3 enemies if at rank 25k.... Also you have to be high level for it's absurd cost in CPU)
A developer who promises to counter a exploit design they made with a part that will take weeks for the average player to save up for is not only rediculous, but devious...
If anyone at freejam listens to this or any other steam review, they must understand that the path away from fairness, progression, creativity, and engineering challenges that made ROBOCRAFT what it is are what keep most players around... If you don't... I predict within a year your game will be down to a few hundred players at best... When it used to be 22k strong.

Portal 2 and the series as a whole are fantastic games made with a simple idea:
You have a gun that makes a teleportation hole to put you somewhere else. You keep your velocity, angle, ect. when you go through it.
The single player is more of an expansion on the original, adding mechanics here and there to freshen it up.
The real fun is the multiplayer and the steam workshop. The campaign is pretty fun and has it's challenging moments, but the most fun I've had with this game is playing some workshot stuff with a friend. The levels users create can be anything from fully custom adventures with entirely new assets or something someone made in the in-game level creator.
(The best one we played was a pack called "The Order of Things", I forgot by whom.)
About the mechanics themselves...
When you hear the phrase "Thinking with Portals" you might just think it's just something they say becouse it's a puzzle game and it's in the title.
No, once you start playing portal, it becomes a part of how you think in the puzzles, and adding another player with their own portals makes it even more of an addition. You don't realize it, but you just start thinking and making new uses of the portals while they also teach you the mechanics (in the singleplayer) if you didn't get it.
The game's one of the best multiplayer puzzlers out there, so go grab the 2-pack and redirect lasers at your friends.

I believe Zero-Punctuation said it best when this is essentially everything that was Portal and improved upon it....while at the same time discarding some puzzle aspects by throwing in obligatory story points.  In his review, he essentially said that Portal was for the puzzles, where Portal 2 was for the story.  For the most part, I agree, but not in the negative sense.  The story is good, but there are a lot of times where puzzle experiences are interrupted by storypoints.
Portal 2 removes some puzzle functions from Portal such as the light-ball puzzles (which are now substituted by lasers) and rocket turret puzzles (which are now substituted with gels, funnels, and light bridges).  In a nutshell, Portal 2 has a lot more functionality than the first game, but it is (once again) on the easy side.  The humor with your sidekicks and antagonists (spoilers with-held) is also there, but the humor may not survive more than 1 or 2 playthroughs, which cuts down on the replayability.  It does, however, have a multi-player campaign and a community map-maker campaign, which includes maps you make and maps others make, which you can download and play at your own leisure (with humorous commentary before every map).
PROS:
New map features (Gels, lasers, funnels, and light bridges)
Humorous voice-acting
Great aesthetic presentation
Great cinematic cutscenes
Multi-player campaign (lengthens replayability)
Community maps  (lengthens replayability)
CONS:
Light-ball and rocket puzzles removed
Humor can get dull
Limited replayability (Gets boring once you've seen just about everything the game has to offer, then you'll rely on some insanely difficult community puzzles that'll make you rage-quit)

This was one of my favorite games of all time.
A very intricate building system based on physics, the progression balanced with the learning curve and the freedom to choose between casually having a good time or delving into the depths of the building system.
When Building a robot there were reasons behind everything placed:
Having a wide firing arc would help do maximum damage while pointing in different directions.
A very mobile robot is important to avoid taking unnecessary damage.
Protecting Important parts like the weapons, mobility equipment and pilot help with longevity.
Balancing the centers of mass, lift and thrust to prevent unwanted yaw, pitch and roll.
Doing all these things in a way so as you take damage your robot can still function.
Between auto-repair, removal of the pilot, removal of tiers and removal of tiered armor and helium (with different mass, lift and armor levels) I cannot think of a reason I would want to play this game, let alone recommend it.

More pay2win, less free2play options as the game's life have progressed....
When I first started playing this game, it was the kind of game I had been wishing for to exist for the longest time. It kind of reminded me of Robot Wars but with more laser guns.
However, as updates came, the game got worse and worse. First they balanced fliers so they were more fair and that was fine since " Satelite  " enemies were boring to deal with with their 1-3 railguns and 20 helium blocks so high up in the sky. Then they finally removed the pilot seat, what used to be an important engineering task when creating a robot to design it around making the pilot safe from fire. Now with it removed, the premium material is even better since free to players can't even have a chance to pot shot the pilot through a crack of previous attacks on said premium robot that blew up enough to show the pilot seat.
Then they started to enforce energy shields more and more and making actual blocks obsolete as a means of defense. I used to run a very blocky tank with 2-3 layers of armor near the center (wheels protected by 1 layer of blocks). However, as weapons grew stronger and blocks weaker, this wasn't much more than a piñata for the opposing team to smash up. And these energy shields can only be placed in such restrict manners that robot designs took a severe hit outside of the tier 1-2 games.
Then they changed the game mode from capture enemy base to capture points on the map by shooting on them. Which only promoted more " Gunboats " than free weapon design, you needed a lot of guns to take points fast instead of investing in some speedy, low gun robot. It's more fun designing machines around fighting than capturing points.
And now in the recent months, all these premium robots have made their way like proper walkers and other cool stuff. Back in the day there were no premium limited items.
The tech tree also got worse, it used to be a tech web where you could skip one tier of an item and jump to next if you researched an item that was next to it and connected through the hexagon web. It gave you a wider freedom to research the things you wished for. Rather than straight tech lines from gun I to gun II to gun III and so on.
What used to be a fun game turned into a cash milker. And a lot of the positive reviews here comes from a former era when the game was better and less stiff for the free to players out there.
Maybe one day the devs will go back to the roots of the game, I will keep watch. But for now, its a waste of my time.
And I'm very sad the game had to be controlled by whatever greedy people made all these decisions that made the game more of a cashgrab and less fun overall.

You used to be able to pick what things you wanted more than others, if you didn't want helium, you didn't need helium, they could care less. Now you get helium regardless of what you want.

-The pilot seat-
This used to be what you had to protect, you had to deal with the weight of it, engineer creative ways you could protect it from being damaged, now thats removed, what is there to protect? Guns? Wheels? Blocks?
-Teirs-
This was the "Leveling up". It was implemented a way i loved, you upgrade your blocks and guns, so that would count towards your new teir, as soon as you had enough of htose blocks and guns your teir would go up, now it's a level thing, A little to confusing to under stand as well. -"Tech tree"-
The tech web, yes at one point is was a tech web, now you get one item after the other, so you are forced on the items you get one after another. You used to be able to pick and choose what YOU wanted, they had tech points you earned and with those you evolved your tech web, and you would get to choose what item you wanted, although eventually you would need to get the rest but you could get the stuff you wanted way before them. Now you are stuck with the spiral tech pole.
If they revert this stuff it will become my favorite game, but now, it's just not even fun to play. It's pointless, and dumbed down. It used to take skill, now you can spam blocks and actually still do decent. Out of my 50 games at the momment this dropped down from #1 to bottom 3 favorite games.

Robocraft: This is a Free to Play PVP shooter game using Third person vehicles on maps, has cursor targeting and a level unlocked tech tree.  It gives you 3 free vehicles in 3 bays, 2 with wheels, 1 hovercraft, armed with basic SMGs or basic cannon.  Drive with w,a,d,s.
Has a Testing map in battle mode where you can shoot and drive without being shot at.  Your creations can get stuck on the maps, if you are a careless driver, requiring you to respawn. Like building vehicles with Lego and then fighting them.  You start out with a few bricks of each shape, if you dismantle all your free vehicles, that gives you a few more parts.  Building mode looks easy enough, hard part is coming up with a good design.
Pro:
It works. Gives you 3 simple vehicles and 3 bays on start.
Cons:
You can buy better robos with real money from the start, so it is pay to win. Many of the negative reviews are from veteran players upset with all the changes the developer has done resently. It is still in Early Access.  No Matchmaking in battles.  Low player base now, leading to long queue waits. No Tutorials.  No PVE except Testing map. PVP in this game will be frustrating with the wide variety of tactics, no teamwork and no matchmaking.
I don't suggest you buy anything from this game.  I just loaded this game to test and review it, not wanting to play it.

Robocraft is a building and fighting game, where you build your own ships, robots, drones, mechs, ect. then you fight with them, attacking others and gaining expereinces and points to upgrade your builds, it is highly addictive, and fun.  Its free to play but you have the option to buy in game credits to get perks and upgrades you normally would not get.  So far I have not seen too much bad about this game, however it does get agravating in Single Player when it takes a million shots or so just to destroy something created by players randomly generated to test fight with and gain expereinces off of, while other ships/robots are popping shots on you tag teaming you.  I feel overall this game is great, fun, and addicting, I recommend it to anyone who like Building/crafting games and space battles or robot battles like Mech Warrior style.
Update:  I still give this game a positive more than a negative review, and have spent money on it, but here are my Pro's and Cons of the game in the time I have played it. (200+ HOURS)
Pros:  You can build, test, and play with bots you create.  Has a great assortment of guns, and blocks you can use to build with, you can do many fun things with your bots, and play.  You will probably still be addictd to this game if you play good, and know how to aim.  This game takes skill, and thats whats good about this game.  There is also the abuility to make your bot anyway you want just about.  There are 150 Levels. There is an ption to play League battles, and up your ranks.  Its free to play if you have the patients for it. The creators, FreeJam  are good about keep this game going and fixing what they can, and releasing new items to the game, like guns and such, so this is a plus.
Cons: This is the bad, about the game.  Once you are in League you can't change back to show your level in the chat, instead you are stuck with a League tag you might not no longer be interested in having.  You can't really afford most of the stuff you need to build with, it takes a lot of fighting to gain anything without cash money, which I find makes the game displeasing and expensive, and harder to work with.  Since this game is still considered an early access game and its free, I can't complain too much.  The next thing is bugs, they happen, and balancing.  With the resent crashing it has made the game seem less fun, but freejam is working on that issue.  Although I have  alot nbegative to say about this game, I still recommend it, and still think it is worth the money.
I hear negative stuff and reviews on these post, and I can say that I might not of been here before the major changes accured such as removeing the cockpit, which seemed cool, but I feel that is over-exagerative and they just want the old feel back, and not consider the changes that are coming up, so my opinions are not as critical than what old players are on the cons and negatives of this game.
Update:  I do not like the new crate system, even though I have paid money into this game, and not liking the direction it is going, I still recommend it.  The game changes a lot, and when you think its the same, its not, and still constantly changes, new things come and get old, and the game stays interesting because of this.  The crates would be better if they gave more useful items that I might need, and if the recycling cost was half that of the forge costs, but thats just me, maybe most others think this as well from what I have been reading in the forums, and in the in-game chats.  It wil be interesting to see the direction the game will go from here, but I play less since I reached level 150, and my goals are less now that I have 12 bots and 1 million or so robits.
Changes since my last review: RP the old currency in game dropped for Robits.  Even though things have been changed, such as the name of Recycling versus selling, and Forging versus buying, its still a currency to me.  You still have Robits which is a currency, even if its supposed to represent broken robot parts in a pile of green dust, it is still a currency.  Also you get random items or parts now after matches in crates, versus gaining RP the old currency after matches. New Map and Gamemode, TDM which is a plus, and I am enjoying playing it when I do play.  You get daily crates and I get on now mostly just for the daily crates every day. Megabots was removed, and level increased from 100 to 150, and 1750 cpu max now.
New Major Cons since the update:
-Cost of recycle and forge is uneven, and harder to get Robits especially if you are new player.
-Progression of gameplay is slow, and takes longer to get anything than it did before.
-You have to play very good at the game and be Pro before you can get the good crates.

My stance on Robocraft is pretty neutral, so I'll list some pros and cons.
Pros:
-Easy to play
-Free to play
-(somewhat) Rewards teamwork
-You can make lots of money for making a good bot
-Alright to play for a bit for a laugh
-Runs on potatoes (My 8-year old iMac can run it at 60)
Cons:
-You can pay (lots of) real money to nearly complete the game in terms of ranks
-You can pay (sometimes lots of) real money or in-game money to buy a bot that someone else has made
-There used to be a defined tier system, but they removed it
-Community isn't great
-Very grindy to get to higher levels
-Weapons and vehicle designs aren't very balanced
-I'm really not sure where the devs are going with it.
Overall, it's free to play. I recommend it for killing some time every now and again, but I don't recommend playing it for very long. If you want a solid game you can really sink some time into, unless you're a 10 year old, look somewhere else. (And yes, I know I have >300 hours on it.)

A lot of controversy of the game firstly, my opinion:
- I think it's a great game, good mechanics, having to build and improve a robot to win games and the choice of building different robots.
Now recently Robocraft has been majorly changed but im going to list the +ves and the -ves of the changes.
+ves
-Now you can have 1 colour for all your robot, OCD for having different teir cubes different colours really bugged me.
-Diversity, you still have the choice of making a SMG tank or a Plasma bomber which is great!
- No longer the need for waiting for tech points to unlock the next cube instead you just level up and have access to them!
- New gamemodes instead of the same old deathmatch before all the recent changes which is great, adds a little dimension to the game
And Now the -ves
-Having only 1 tier cubes?! Personally I think this is both good and bad, good because no need to worry about trying to get enough to replace all your cubes and bad because YOU HAVE 1 CHOICE!!! It ruins the work you need to upgrade your bot :(
- Now the Pilot seat- I again see this as both good and bad because good- you no longer need to worry about trying to make your seat fit, I have had so many bots where the pilot seat just wouldnt go somewhere nice but bad because it ruins the element of engineering defenses so you dont get shot down as easily.
- The tech tree- Its still fine but not really much of a 'Tree' more like a dumb swirl which confuses the hell out of you because you cant bloody follow it! SO IT SUCKS!
-Ahh yes the garage bays- I think the ability not having to pay for extra ones is great! being a F2P and having 3 bays was hell in simple terms
To sum up I think it's still a great game but has become too simple, FreeJam has removed all the elements that made it what it was, its now just become a RUN AND GUN game really which is why most recent reviews are negative. I say play the game and find out for yourself! its great but simple and having 100 Hours does give me good enough evidence to say this

I seriously used to love this game. It was my life for a few years. Every morning, I'd sit down and play Robocraft for 2-4 hours. I played before hoverblades (Ignore my play time, I used the launcher for a while before it started crashing on me, then I downloaded it on Steam) existed, and enjoyed the game so much.
For a while.
Than things started going downhill. Tiers (the old ranking system, went from T1 to T10) were removed. This didn't bother me, because I found it difficult to go up tiers, and I honestly enjoyed this change. But then Freejam completely removed armor abilities. You used to purchase armored blocks and they would make your robot more durable, but they were expensive. I have spent days, weeks, MONTHS in-game, collecting RP's (the old currency, stood for Robo Points) to buy those blocks. The day after I had finally completed collecting all those blocks, and put them on my robot...Freejam removed armored blocks, all of a sudden, and without warning, from the game, saying 'they're OP'. I tried to be as optimistic as possible. I thought to myself, 'Now that blocks are only 1 RP each, maybe I can focus on leveling up and buying more guns instead!'.
Nope.
Freejam removed RP from the game a few weeks later.
Now there were 'crates'. You get crates from playing, you open them and you get guns that way. Does that sound like a CS:GO ripoff to me or what? And, you can BUY crates. But Freejam say you can buy crates 'As well'. But the GOOD crates are ultra rare, and you pretty much have to buy them.
Freejam say that the 'free' part in their name means that the game will forever be free2play and never be pay2win. Yep. Totally didn't stick out to that one, Freejam.
Also, I feel like they scammed tons of players. When I was trying to upgrade my robot's armor (mentioned above), I spent about £2.00 on blocks. That's £2.00 on blocks that Freejam won't give back, even though they TOOK those blocks.
They took away my items of purchase, without warning, and without a full refund (I was given 1 day of premium instead, which didn't match the cost of my purchase).
That sounds pretty illegal to me.
So, with a (slightly) heavy heart, I'm changing this review from positive to negative. Don't get this game. Don't. Freejam (or they should be called FreeScam) have turned a beautiful creation to a pile of mush, and now they're currently sprinkling dog poop on top.

Portal 2 is the continuation of the classic Portal game and it fixes many of issues that the first game had, namely falling through Portals and not repositioning the character.
This sequel follows Chell again, the main protagonist of the game and improves upon the game graphically and introduces numerous new technologies, namely the hologram platforms, which can be used as both a shield and a platform to walk on. These platforms are also capable of moving through portals if placed correctly. The game also introduces levitation holograms which can also be used through portals to reach new areas without relying on momentum-conservation through portals.
Story-wise, the developers decided to add a very loveable character named Wheatley, a worker bot that runs on rails with a thick English West country accent. He follows you along through your quest to once again escape from Aperture Laboratories until he unfortunately reincarnates an old nemesis.
It was very refreshing to finally quit doing trials over and over again in white rooms. In this game, you learn about the history of Aperture Laboratories, the birth of GLaDOS, the creator of Aperture, other test subjects, etc. In the first game, you only got to see glimpses behind the walls of the testing chamber. In this game, about 80 percent of it is spent in the chambers themselves.
Over all, the game is a vast improvement on the first game. In terms of time-frame, it took twice as long to beat and I haven't even TOUCHED the co-op portion of the game yet. If I ever get to it, I'll put my 2 cents on that as well. If you are a hardcore puzzler, I'd say buy it ASAP. If you're not very good at puzzlers and get irritated when you can't figure out the solution, I'd say wait for a sale to pick it up.

I didn't like Portal 2 as much as I was supposed to. I know I know it was made by Valve and as an "educated" video game fan I'm supposed to fall head over heels with everything they make (apart from HL2EP1) but Portal 2 left me feeling a bit flat. I think part of it was the game so completely removed handholding and storytelling (to a certain extent) that I was left with a feeling of emptiness. I'd be stuck in a huge room with no idea how to find the exit, a character that never talked (which is now boring) and a seemingly existential void in the game itself. Who cared if Chell never made it? I knew nothing about her and so if she died it seemed to make no difference. Another factor is simple sequilitis, yeh sure there's new gels and potions and stuff but fundamentally it's the same "shoot portal there, slingshot over there" gameplay which while not boring is a bit.....flat by now. I will say that I found the writing pretty funny and interesting but overall as a package I found myself trudging through it rather than actually....you know.....enjoying it.

Another factor is simple sequilitis, yeh sure there's new gels and potions and stuff but fundamentally it's the same "shoot portal there, slingshot over there" gameplay which while not boring is a bit.....flat by now. I will say that I found the writing pretty funny and interesting but overall as a package I found myself trudging through it rather than actually....you know.....enjoying it.

Please bear with me since english isn't my native language, then again i'll do my best to explain my point of view.
Robocraft is an online third-person vehicle shooter game set on fictional areas of different planets where players construct machines that are used to fight with others in battles.
The idea of building and engineering your own robot to send in a battlefield is really exciting and that's why I decided to give this game a try. As you can see, i've been playing for quite a while, and could be considered as an "old player" since i still have some robots that have a colored name, and reached the level maximum through hours and countless destroyed cubes, getting higher in tier, unlocking parts with tech-points in the tech-tree ... It seems that all this process now has been simplified. Ok ... Why not ?
Pros :
+ Game in perpetual evolution (Robot parts, Game, Community, ...And yes it's a pros.)
+ Satisfaction of defeating your oponent with your own brain-made robot
+ Share your creation (As an open-source defender, i find this nice)
+ Play with friends (Coop game is always nice)
+ Develop strategies according to your "robot type" (Type of gun, transportation, ...)
Cons :
- Jerks
(They are everywhere : some of them decide to screw up the game with a "woody build", or haven't properly tested a build. It's annoying and 80% of the time not funny)
- Balancing
(I sincerely thank the dev's for keeping up the interest they have in this game. BUT, even if they are listening to their community, they may not change some "balancing measures" they did. Gravity + Truster + Weight + Airfoil patches achieved to kill all my bots, resulting in my resignation to simply quit the game.
What was great during that time is that you could let free your imagination. Now, it's much more normalized.)
- Keybinds
(I don't know if it's been fixed, but there was a time when you couldn't assign your control keys ...)
- Few bugs
(I know, it's still not perfect and it's F2P. Fact is that restarting the game over and over is sometimes a bit annoying. Old player that used to play with friends and tried to team work know what i'm talking about.)
- Removing all the challenge (Seats removed ? Really ?)
Conclusion (TL/DR) :
Good game, lot of fun if you never played it before the "big balancing changes", skill challenging.

When I first played "Portal," and prepared to play "Portal 2," I wondered how they were going to take such a simple game and find a way to top it in the sequel. But I found that "Portal 2" didn't just do better than the first game, it exceeded it. It maintained what made the first game work in the first place, and added some new features and more story to make it even more of a fun ride. And it really manages to maintain the quality standards that were set by the first "Portal."
Once again, this game uses the Source Engine, just as the original did. And given how this engine has aged very well, it works very well in this context. The graphics are still very gorgeous. You are again in the Aperture Science Labs, albeit, ones that have seen better days. Once again, this environment feels very fresh, while at the same time, familiar to returning players who've played the first game. The Old Aperture areas are a very nice addition to the game, with their style aesthetics from each section's respective time.
The gameplay is unchanged from the original game, and the game's challenges are equally as challenging and engaging as the original game. But I'm glad the game has some additions to the gameplay, such as being able to see which portal is where, so you can more easily keep track of which portal you've used in one location, and you can use the other one in the proper manner. The tests aren't hard if you're smart, but at the same time, they've added some new challenges, such as using the gels. The gels can be fun to use (my favorites are the acceleration and repulsion gels) and they add new dimensions to the gameplay in tandem with the portals.
The voice acting once again shines in this game. Ellen McLain outdoes herself as GLaDOS in this game, while Stephen Merchant as Wheatley really steals the show at times. Wheatley is such a lovable idiot, you really look forward to every moment he appears. GLaDOS still manages to be funny as well, especially when
. But then there's Cave Johnson, voiced by J.K. Simmons, who really steals the show during the Old Aperture section. Johnson is such a colorful joy to listen to. The game's voice acting does a great job of not taking this game too seriously, it makes you want to come back just to listen to it. And even the turrets are still funny.
The game maintains the immersive nature that the first game had. It lets the game unfold before you as it did in the original. This of course, made the plot less predictable. It worked in the first game, and it works in this game. And I liked how they were able to make this game twice as long as the original was.
I have fewer complaints about this game than the first one. This game reduced the dependency on using Portals to make some of the jumps. Of course, it's still present, but it's not as big a deal as in the first one. Also, at times, it can be a bit easy to get lost in some of the Old Aperture sections.
This game was a good ride and definitely worth revisiting in the future. It's still a game you want to come back to and try again. Again, you'll think up new ways to solve all the tests, and the learning curve is simple enough for first-time players, and there's enough challenge for experienced ones. This game has improved greatly on the original in that respect to challenge. The voice acting makes the game more fun to enjoy, and overall, the game avoids changing it's formula too much so that it still feels like the game it started off as. When a sequel is able to outperform the original, you know it's doing something right. I will be playing this again.
Edit: And yes, "Funniest A.I. Characters" is a legit reason why I would award this. GLaDOS and Wheatley....priceless.

The best part of the game right now is that it is growing so much and evolving at a rapid pace. You can see how the community has shaped the game and how much FJ interacts with the players and evolves the game. The Meta changes every few months as FJ makes tweaks and big changes but the players always evolve.
This is not a simple game. This is not an easy game. No matter what some people want to scream about hte game being "dumbed down" it has only changed. The subtle depth to the game is huge and as you play more and more you will earn more and more about how to build and play your bots. This game is challenging, it is not for the lowest common demoninator. It is certainly no Dark Souls, but this isn't CoD etc.
That said, this game is currently VERY MUCH in development and is frequently updated with changes that can be rather huge. But FreeJam (the Developer) has proven to be very receptive to community feedback and has made nearly every change based off player feedback. They can't please everyone so there are a number of very loud negative voices, but that goes with anything. FJ is truly trying to make this the best game possible!

But I'm glad the game has some additions to the gameplay, such as being able to see which portal is where, so you can more easily keep track of which portal you've used in one location, and you can use the other one in the proper manner. The tests aren't hard if you're smart, but at the same time, they've added some new challenges, such as using the gels. The gels can be fun to use (my favorites are the acceleration and repulsion gels) and they add new dimensions to the gameplay in tandem with the portals.
The voice acting once again shines in this game. Ellen McLain outdoes herself as GLaDOS in this game, while Stephen Merchant as Wheatley really steals the show at times. Wheatley is such a lovable idiot, you really look forward to every moment he appears. GLaDOS still manages to be funny as well, especially when
. But then there's Cave Johnson, voiced by J.K. Simmons, who really steals the show during the Old Aperture section. Johnson is such a colorful joy to listen to. The game's voice acting does a great job of not taking this game too seriously, it makes you want to come back just to listen to it. And even the turrets are still funny.
The game maintains the immersive nature that the first game had. It lets the game unfold before you as it did in the original. This of course, made the plot less predictable. It worked in the first game, and it works in this game. And I liked how they were able to make this game twice as long as the original was.
I have fewer complaints about this game than the first one. This game reduced the dependency on using Portals to make some of the jumps. Of course, it's still present, but it's not as big a deal as in the first one. Also, at times, it can be a bit easy to get lost in some of the Old Aperture sections.
This game was a good ride and definitely worth revisiting in the future. It's still a game you want to come back to and try again. Again, you'll think up new ways to solve all the tests, and the learning curve is simple enough for first-time players, and there's enough challenge for experienced ones. This game has improved greatly on the original in that respect to challenge. The voice acting makes the game more fun to enjoy, and overall, the game avoids changing it's formula too much so that it still feels like the game it started off as. When a sequel is able to outperform the original, you know it's doing something right. I will be playing this again.
Edit: And yes, "Funniest A.I. Characters" is a legit reason why I would award this. GLaDOS and Wheatley....priceless.

*...a player showed conclusively that there is a 90% chance that your actions will have no influence of the outcome of a match.  It's decided more by how many people stay on your team until the end of the round.  You will lose rank for the negative outcome as well.
